title: The Hong Kong digital-asset map
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can name who regulates each digital-asset activity in Hong Kong, which regimes are live, and which are still coming.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong splits digital-asset regulation among several bodies, each covering particular activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) supervises banks (Authorized Institutions, AIs) and licenses stablecoin issuers. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.1]; [S:270f1f7324ab, Register introduction] The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licenses virtual-asset (VA) trading platforms and sets codes of conduct for regulated securities activities. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.2] The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) sets policy and, with the SFC, consults on new laws; the Legislative Council (LegCo) passes bills. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 2]; [S:6186c01c6649, cover page]; [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.1] A bank that carries on SFC-regulated activities must register with the SFC as a Registered Institution (RI), but the HKMA is its day-to-day, frontline supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] Live today: the VA trading-platform regime, the Stablecoins Ordinance, the joint SFC–HKMA circulars, HKMA custody and tokenisation guidance, and the Basel cryptoasset capital standard (see Status board). Coming: statutory licensing for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management, and crypto-asset tax reporting under the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) Part 5B VA trading platform (VATP) licensing + VATP Guidelines | LegCo / SFC | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | VATPs; banks and other intermediaries may deal in VAs only through SFC-licensed VATPs | [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.2]; [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2]; [S:8a016a912528, para 17] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | LegCo / HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Stablecoin issuers; only regulated entities specified in the Ordinance may offer stablecoins to the public | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]; [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities (Dec 2023) + supplement (Sep 2025) | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023; 30 Sep 2025 | In force | Licensed corporations (LCs); RIs (banks), with the HKMA as frontline supervisor | [S:8a016a912528, p.1, para 31]; [S:b79266f3da51, paras 1, 10] |
| RI circular on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| AI interface with VAs and VA service providers (VASPs) | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | All AIs | [S:642680fa4467, p.5] |
| Updated custody guidance (replaces Feb 2024) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs + subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] |
| Distributed ledger technology (DLT) risk-management considerations | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs (non-binding considerations) | [S:1884530ff235, p.1] |
| Basel cryptoasset standard (amendment rules + CRP-1) | HKMA / LegCo | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:974899bbef4d, p.1]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.1] |
| VA dealing + VA custodian licensing | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks would register with the SFC; HKMA proposed as frontline regulator | [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48]; [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 6] |
| VA advisory + VA management licensing | FSTB + SFC | 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Only banks could register (not be licensed) for these services; current RIs would need registration | [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] |
| CARF / amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) bill | FSTB / Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / LegCo | 22 May 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Reporting crypto-asset service providers | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Ensemble TX (tokenised deposits) | HKMA | 13 Nov 2025 | Pilot | Participating banks | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA does not currently plan to stop banks taking VA exposure, provided controls and senior-management oversight are adequate. [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3]
- A bank intending any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA and get feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals, p.5]
- An AI carrying on regulated activities must register with the SFC as an RI; the SFC keeps ultimate responsibility, while the HKMA supervises the RI day to day and the SFC may rely on that supervision. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3]
- Banks meet the joint circular as RIs, with the HKMA as frontline supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3] Intermediaries are reminded to tell the SFC ahead of time (and the HKMA, where applicable) before beginning or changing VA-related activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- The SFC and HKMA require intermediaries to provide VA dealing services only by partnering with SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- The Stablecoins Ordinance commenced on 1 August 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- The HKMA register lists two licensed stablecoin issuers, Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02), both effective 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury (SFST) told LegCo that the HKMA received 36 applications in the initial application period, and that any further licences would keep the overall number very limited. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply para 1 and (2)]
- The SFC's live list showed 13 licensed VATPs at its 29 May 2026 update; being on the applicant list is not the same as being licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; applicant section]
- The HKMA's 2026 custody annex expects AIs to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage and to generate, store and back up seeds and private keys in Hong Kong. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), para 11(l) and fn 8]
- The Basel cryptoasset capital, disclosure and exposure-limit rules came into operation on 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, p.1]
- Under CRP-1, the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual module on classifying cryptoassets, a bank that acquires a new type of cryptoasset must notify the HKMA and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's classification assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- For the coming VA dealing and custody regimes, the Government proposed that the SFC lead licensing and standard-setting, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- Under the proposed dealing regime, banks would need to register with the SFC, in consultation with the HKMA, to deal in VAs. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]
- No deeming (grandfathering) arrangement is planned when the VA dealing and custody regimes commence; SFC-licensed VATPs, LCs, RIs and banks already providing these services are to get an expedited approval process. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
- The CARF bill appeared in the Gazette on 22 May 2026 and had its First Reading in LegCo on 3 June 2026; subject to its passage, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]
- The IRD plans a dedicated CARF portal, and the bill proposes that every in-scope reporting crypto-asset service provider register an account on it. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Reporting portal section]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- [ ] As an RI, notify the SFC and HKMA when intending to start or change VA dealing, advice or asset management, including a change of client type. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- [ ] Classify cryptoasset exposures under Part 12 of the Banking (Capital) Rules, reading CRP-1 alongside, from 1 January 2026. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Set prudent VA exposure limits and conservative loan-to-value ratios for VA collateral. [S:642680fa4467, p.3]
- [ ] Keep client digital assets held in custody segregated from the bank's own assets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 6]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the HKMA on acquiring any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Discuss custody plans with the HKMA before offering custody. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For VA dealing, route business only through SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- [ ] Check a VATP's status on the SFC's licensed list, not the applicant list. [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section]
- [ ] Check a stablecoin issuer against the HKMA register, which the HKMA says holds the latest list of licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]

## Talking points

**To the chief compliance officer (CCO)**
- The bank's VA conduct duties reach it as an RI supervised day to day by the HKMA, not through direct SFC supervision. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- The bank must comply with the HKMA's anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) Guideline; as an RI it must also have regard to the SFC's AML/CFT Guideline, including its Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1]

**To business heads**
- Any new VA product needs an HKMA discussion before launch, and RIs must pre-notify the SFC and HKMA. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- Only two stablecoin issuers are licensed; the Government says any further licences would keep the total very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]

**To the CEO**
- The Government proposed an SFC-led licensing model for VA dealing and custody, with the HKMA as the banks' frontline regulator. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- No deeming (grandfathering) arrangement is planned when these regimes start. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

**To Risk / chief risk officer (CRO)**
- The Basel cryptoasset standard applies from 1 January 2026; exposures held before that date, and any new type of cryptoasset, stay in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.4.1-1.4.2, 2.1.2]
- The HKMA's custody annex expects AIs to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]

## Common mix-ups

- "The SFC supervises our VA business directly." No: the SFC holds ultimate responsibility, but the HKMA is the RI's day-to-day supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- "The 50%/100% insurance rule applies to our custody." That rule is the SFC's VATP expectation of an SFC-approved compensation arrangement covering 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot and other storage; the HKMA's 2026 annex instead makes the bank liable for losses attributable to it and expects adequate financial resources. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- "A deemed or applicant VATP is licensed." Not so; only the licensed list shows licensed platforms. [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section]
- "The 2022 joint circular still applies." The December 2023 joint circular superseded the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. [S:8a016a912528, note after para 3, p.1]
- "The dealing and custody bills are law." They are at consultation-conclusions stage; the Government's stated target was to introduce a bill in 2026. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]

## Read these first

1. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs** — HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3-5 (prudential, AML, investor protection, prior discussion). The HKMA's base position on banks and VAs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
2. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)** — HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 2.1.3, 2.2.4, 4.16.1 and 5.6. Explains why the HKMA, not the SFC, supervises your RI business day to day. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
3. **Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong** — FSTB, 26 Jun 2025. Read paras 4-6 and 16. Sets out the LEAP framework and proposes the SFC-lead/HKMA-frontline split for new regimes. https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf

## Open items

- The VA dealing/custodian/advisory/management bill: the SFST said on 24 June 2026 that it would be introduced this year; no bill text or gazettal is in the documents reviewed for this guide as of 25 Sep 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- CARF bill: introduced for First Reading on 3 June 2026; No document reviewed for this guide has a record of passage. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]
- No Insurance Authority rulebook on digital assets is in the documents reviewed for this guide; insurer-side rules are a gap.
- The VATP list is live; the 13-platform count is a 29 May 2026 snapshot. [S:b14be2203d39, Footer]

## Related modules

[A2](#m-A2), [A3](#m-A3), [B1](#m-B1), [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3)

title: How Hong Kong rules are made and how to read them
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can place any document on the law-making path, tell how binding it is, and cite it to the paragraph.

## In 60 seconds

The stablecoin regime shows the path a Hong Kong digital-asset rule can take: a consultation paper, published conclusions, a bill gazetted and passed by the Legislative Council (LegCo), a commencement notice in the Gazette, then a transition period. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]; [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6]; [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]; [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3] Below the statute sit other instruments whose force differs: rules made as subsidiary legislation, Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) modules, guidelines and circulars. Each SPM module states its own classification on the cover, so check it. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, para 1]; [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification] For a bank, a key reading rule sits in the anti-money-laundering (AML) Guideline of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA): both *must* and *should* mark a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6] HKMA circulars and SPM modules are published in its Banking Regulatory Document Repository (BRDR); circulars of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) open from its e-Distribution site; conclusions of the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and government press releases record the legislative milestones. [S:974899bbef4d, landing page]; [S:8a016a912528, p.1]; [S:6186c01c6649, p.4, Next step]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026. Worked examples of each stage. AI = authorized institution (a bank); RI = registered institution (a bank registered with the SFC); LC = licensed corporation; VA = virtual asset; VATP = VA trading platform.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stablecoin issuer regime: consultation paper, then conclusions (July 2024) | FSTB + HKMA | 27 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Prospective issuers | [S:54aa01e7396e, cover, p.1; Introduction, para 1] |
| Stablecoins Bill gazetted; First Reading set for 18 Dec 2024 | Government / LegCo | 6 Dec 2024 | Superseded | Issuers | [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) commencement notice made by the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury (SFST) | SFST | Gazetted 6 Jun 2025; commenced 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Issuers, offerors | [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3-4] |
| Banking (Capital) (Amendment) Rules 2025, with the Disclosure and Exposure Limits amendment rules | HKMA / LegCo | HKMA gazettal letter 11 Jul 2025; in operation from 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:974899bbef4d, landing page, Directly related Document; letter, paras 1-2] |
| CRP-1 clarification letter on para 2.6.4 | HKMA | 3 Jun 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4] |
| VA dealing and VA custodian regimes | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | VA dealing and custodian service providers, incl. LCs and RIs | [S:6186c01c6649, p.3, footnote 2; para 35]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48] |
| VA advisory and VA management regimes | FSTB + SFC | May 2026 | Conclusions published | Advisory and management providers, incl. SFC-licensed or registered intermediaries | [S:01c5c5c4045f, cover, p.1; para 62] |
| Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) and amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) bill | FSTB / LegCo | Gazetted 22 May 2026; First Reading 3 Jun 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Reporting crypto-asset service providers | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |

## Key facts

- The stablecoin conclusions of July 2024 said a bill was being prepared for introduction into LegCo later that year. [S:54aa01e7396e, Way Forward, para 12.1, p.29]
- The Stablecoins Bill was gazetted on 6 December 2024, with its First Reading in LegCo set for 18 December 2024. [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6]
- LegCo passed the bill on 21 May 2025; the government release refers to a six-month non-contravention period. [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]
- A commencement notice made by the SFST and gazetted on 6 June 2025 set 1 August 2025 as the start date; the notices were to be tabled in LegCo on 11 June 2025 for negative vetting. [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3, 7]
- The Banking (Capital), (Disclosure) and (Exposure Limits) (Amendment) Rules 2025 went through a 28-day LegCo negative-vetting period, which expired without extension. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, para 1]
- The Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) amendments passed LegCo on 7 December 2022; the HKMA said the amendments relevant to banks would start on 1 June 2023, to allow time for preparation. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2]
- Transitions can be hard stops: VATPs operating before 1 June 2023 could continue for 12 months to 31 May 2024 without breaching the licensing rules, and the SFC had no power to extend the 29 February 2024 deadline for the deeming arrangement. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 20]
- For the coming VA dealing and custodian regimes, the conclusions say existing providers will not be offered a deeming arrangement under current plans. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48]
- The HKMA AML Guideline is published under AMLO s.7 and Banking Ordinance s.7(3), and compliance is enforced through both ordinances. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.1, 1.3]
- In that Guideline, both *must* and *should* denote a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- SPM modules state their own force: SB-1 is a statutory guideline under Banking Ordinance s.7(3), while CRP-1 is a non-statutory guideline issued as a guidance note. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification]
- Where CRP-1 and the Banking (Capital) Rules (BCR) differ, the BCR prevail. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- Some HKMA papers say they are non-binding: the April 2024 distributed ledger technology (DLT) considerations are non-binding and non-exhaustive, and the HKMA's detailed expectations are discussed with each AI bilaterally. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction, 4th bullet, p.1]
- A circular can change how a module applies at once: the 3 June 2026 letter clarified that the CRP-1 para 2.6.4 condition may also be met where the tokenised asset's business activities are supervised by a financial market regulator, effective immediately, with the module's wording to be updated later. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]
- The SFC Guidelines for VATP operators are published under section 399 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO) and AMLO s.53ZTK. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1, Note]
- Later circulars can supersede earlier ones outright: the December 2023 joint circular replaced the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. [S:8a016a912528, para 3, closing sentence, p.1]
- The HKMA's 27 May 2026 custody letter supersedes its 20 February 2024 custody circular. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- Budget speeches announce plans, not rules: the 2026-27 Budget said a bill would be introduced in 2026 for dealing and custodian licensing regimes, and an amendment bill for CARF in the first half of 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Read *should* in the HKMA AML Guideline as mandatory, not optional. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- [ ] Where CRP-1 and the BCR differ, follow the BCR; Part 12 of the BCR sets the classification principles. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- [ ] Reflect the 3 June 2026 clarification of CRP-1 para 2.6.4, which took effect immediately. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep a regulatory inventory that records each document's classification and supersession, e.g. the 2024 custody circular replaced by the 2026 letter. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Track commencement dates separately from passage dates (e.g. AMLO amendments: passed December 2022, relevant changes from 1 June 2023). [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] The dealing conclusions encourage firms in, or planning, VA dealing to contact the SFC or HKMA (as applicable) early, e.g. to start pre-application; firms that do not will have to stop operating on commencement. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 33-34]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Tell a formally licensed VATP apart from an applicant or a deemed-to-be-licensed applicant; the SFC keeps them on separate lists (last updated 29 May 2026). [S:b14be2203d39, List of VATP applicants; Last update]

## Talking points

**To the CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)**
- Our AML Guideline says *should* marks a mandatory requirement, the same as *must*. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- Check each SPM module's classification: SB-1 is statutory; CRP-1 is a guidance note that yields to the BCR. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]

**To business heads**
- Conclusions papers are not law; the FSTB and SFC aim to put a bill for the dealing regime into LegCo in 2026, and the Budget said the same for dealing and custodian regimes. [S:6186c01c6649, p.4, Next step]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]
- The conclusions state no plan for a deeming arrangement and encourage early SFC/HKMA engagement. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 33-34]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong's path runs from consultation to conclusions, bill, commencement and transition; for stablecoins, consultation began on 27 December 2023 and the Ordinance commenced on 1 August 2025, about 19 months later. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- Budget items such as planned bills are stated intentions, not obligations. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]

**To Risk / CRO (Chief Risk Officer)**
- The negative-vetting period for the cryptoasset capital rules expired without extension, and the rules apply from 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, paras 1-2]
- HKMA letters can change how capital guidance applies with immediate effect, as in June 2026. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]

## Common mix-ups

- "Should in HKMA guidance is best practice." In the AML Guideline it is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- "All SPM modules have the same force." SB-1 is statutory; CRP-1 is non-statutory and yields to the BCR. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- "The June 2026 CRP-1 letter tightened Group 1 tests." It widened how para 2.6.4 can be met. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, para 3]
- "Passage means in force." AMLO amendments passed in December 2022; the HKMA said the relevant changes would start in June 2023. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2]
- "Existing players will be grandfathered into new VA regimes." The dealing conclusions state no plan for a deeming arrangement. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

## Read these first

1. **Guideline on AML/CFT (For Authorized Institutions), revised May 2023** — HKMA, 25 May 2023. Read Chapter 1, paras 1.1-1.8 and footnote 1. Defines how binding the text is and who it binds. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20230525-4-EN/AML-2.pdf
2. **SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025 (V.1, effective 1 Jan 2026). Read the cover page and paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1-1.4.2. Shows how a guidance note sits under statutory rules. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251125-15-EN/CRP-1.pdf
3. **Rules on cryptoassets standard and other updates** — HKMA, 15 Aug 2025. Read paras 1-2 of the letter. A short view of negative vetting and commencement. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20250815-1-EN

**How to use paragraph references.** Cite HKMA SPM modules and guidelines by paragraph (e.g. CRP-1 para 2.1.2). HKMA circulars often have no numbered paragraphs, so cite heading plus page (e.g. Implementation, p.2). SFC circulars number paragraphs (e.g. joint circular para 31). BRDR landing pages (brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/…) link the PDF and related documents; SFC circulars open from apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb by reference number (e.g. 23EC66). [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

## Open items

- No FAQ, code of practice or SFC Code of Conduct text on how SFO s.399 guidelines are weighed in proceedings is in the documents reviewed for this guide; this module does not state their legal effect beyond what the documents say.
- The CRP-1 text itself had not been updated for the June 2026 clarification as of the letter. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, para 4]
- As of their conclusions, the Government and the SFC were still to decide commencement dates for the VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 49]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
- The CARF bill had its First and Second Readings on 3 June 2026 with the Second Reading debate adjourned; its passage is not recorded in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2]

title: Where policy is heading
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can say what the government, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) have officially said they will do next, and by when, using only their own words and dates.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong's digital-asset direction is set out in a short stack of official strategy papers. The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) issued a 2022 Policy Statement that set out its founding regulatory principle (quoted in Key facts below). [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4] Its 2025 Policy Statement 2.0 added the LEAP framework and proposed the SFC as the lead licensing authority for digital-asset dealing and custody, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] The SFC's ASPIRe roadmap (Feb 2025) lists 12 initiatives; half of them are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary; Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11] The HKMA closed Fintech 2025 and launched Fintech 2030, then published a Fintech Promotion Blueprint (Feb 2026) and asked bank boards to endorse a business-model plan. [S:1131a8814d96, photo caption; S:b0607b779270, para 1; S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] The 2026-27 Budget and the 16 Sep 2026 Policy Address add dated targets, including a digital-asset licensing bill in 2026, EnsembleTX upgrades and tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 109]; [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii), 50]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Policy Statement on Development of Virtual Assets in Hong Kong | FSTB | 31 Oct 2022 | Superseded | Market-wide (PS 2.0 is the next phase) | [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 3] |
| Fintech 2025 | HKMA | 8 Jun 2021 | Superseded | Banks (concluded when Fintech 2030 was unveiled) | [S:f8eed6b2e069, para 1]; [S:1131a8814d96, photo caption] |
| ASPIRe roadmap | SFC | 19 Feb 2025 | Exploratory | VA service providers and SFC-regulated intermediaries (only the custody legislative timeline is dated) | [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary; Pillar A, Initiative 1] |
| Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) | FSTB | 26 Jun 2025 | Stated target | Market-wide; banks via HKMA | [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] |
| Fintech 2030 (DART) | HKMA | 3 Nov 2025 | Stated target | Banks | [S:1131a8814d96, para 3] |
| Fintech Promotion Blueprint | HKMA | 3 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Banks, fintech providers | [S:b0607b779270, paras 2-8] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models circular | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] |
| 2026-27 Budget | Financial Secretary | 25 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Market-wide | [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104-114] |
| Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address | Chief Executive | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target | Market-wide | [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35, 49-51] |

VA = virtual asset. AI = authorized institution (a bank or other deposit-taker authorized by the HKMA).

## Key facts

- The 2022 Policy Statement said the government would follow the "same activity, same risks, same regulation" principle, and that its next step was a licensing regime for VA service providers. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6]
- It also named stablecoins as another key area of focus and listed three pilots: NFT (non-fungible token) issuance, tokenised government green bonds, and e-HKD (a possible retail central bank digital currency). [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 9-10]
- Policy Statement 2.0 (PS 2.0) says the government will use *digital assets* instead of *virtual assets*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] The legal term in the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) is still *virtual asset* (section 53ZRA). [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1]
- LEAP stands for Legal and regulatory streamlining, Expanding the suite of tokenised products, Advancing use cases and cross-sectoral collaboration, and People and partnership development. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 4]
- PS 2.0 proposes the SFC as the lead authority for licensing and registering digital-asset dealing and custodian service providers, with the HKMA as frontline regulator supervising banks' dealing and custodian activities. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- PS 2.0 also said the government would propose laws to extend profits tax concessions for family-owned investment holding vehicles and privately offered funds to specified digital assets, from year of assessment 2025/26, subject to Legislative Council (LegCo) approval. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- ASPIRe has five pillars (Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure, Relationships) and 12 initiatives. [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary] Government-led legislative preparations for a custodian licensing regime were aimed for completion by end-2025. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]
- ASPIRe says the SFC will explore moving away from set hardware and cold-storage ratios towards technology-neutral, outcome-based custody standards. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
- Fintech 2030 has four pillars, known as DART (Data and payment infrastructure, Artificial intelligence, Resilience, Tokenisation), and over 40 initiatives, including regular tokenised government bond issuance and the Project Ensemble pilot. [S:1131a8814d96, paras 3-7]
- The Fintech Promotion Blueprint announced four flagship projects, including a Quantum Preparedness Index and a Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline for fintech solution providers using AI (artificial intelligence) and DLT (distributed ledger technology). [S:b0607b779270, paras 3, 4, 6]
- The HKMA expects each AI's board to oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan within six months of the 9 March 2026 circular, addressing DLT and other technology change. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- The 2025 Policy Address set a target to introduce a bill into LegCo in 2026 to license digital-asset dealing and custody providers. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22]
- The 2026-27 Budget repeated the plan for a licensing bill in 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104] It also said the government would change the Inland Revenue Ordinance to put into effect the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) over the coming two years, with a bill in the first half of 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108]
- The Budget also said CMU OmniClear (the HKMA's Central Moneymarkets Unit operator) would set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for digital bond issuance and settlement. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end, to help banks use more than $1.3 trillion of these bills more efficiently and around the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The HKMA plans to add settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC), and round-the-clock operation, to EnsembleTX by around end-2026, and to keep exploring tokenised-deposit use cases. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- The SFC will enhance VA licensing regimes, promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms, and start running its digital-asset custody monitoring system in the second half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49(i), 49(iii), 51(iii)]
- The Customs and Excise Department (C&ED) aims to launch a Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex, New Indicators, item 209]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Have the board oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan addressing DLT and related technology within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the 2026 bill target for digital-asset dealing and custody licensing. PS 2.0 proposes the SFC as lead licensing and registration authority, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- [ ] Track the start dates proposed in the CARF bill: 1 Jan 2027 for the CARF part and 1 Jan 2028 for the amended CRS part. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Discuss any new digital-asset activity with the HKMA before launch, as the March 2026 circular restates. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- [ ] Be ready to submit the business plan via the HKMA Survey Tool if invited. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] None set by the policy documents in this module; see B2 and B3 for the current rules.

## Talking points

**To the CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)**
- The 2026 licensing regime is still a target: the bill has to be introduced into LegCo. The business-model circular, by contrast, already sets a board expectation for every AI. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22]; [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- Government now says *digital assets*, but AMLO still uses *virtual asset*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]; [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1]

**To business heads**
- The SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms and their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- EnsembleTX is to add CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA says banks have an opportunity to act as a key intermediary between traditional finance and digital assets, and expects a board-endorsed plan. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2]
- The government's stated 2026 target is a bill for digital-asset dealing and custody licensing. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22]

**To Risk / CRO (Chief Risk Officer)**
- The Blueprint's Quantum Preparedness Index assesses banks' readiness for post-quantum cryptography; the first index reading was 2.3 out of 10. [S:b0607b779270, para 4]; [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
- ASPIRe may shift custody rules toward outcome-based standards, but that is still exploratory. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]

## Common mix-ups

- "Policy Statement 2.0 changed the law." It sets directions; the tax concessions, for example, need LegCo approval. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- "ASPIRe items are rules." Half of the 12 initiatives are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11]
- "The first stablecoin licences came in March 2026 as the Budget said." The Budget (25 Feb 2026) said the first licences would come the next month; the HKMA granted them on 10 April 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 105]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1]
- "The business-model circular is about crypto only." It covers DLT, agentic AI and cloud computing, with a reminder on discussing new digital-asset activities before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2]

## Read these first

1. **Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong** — FSTB, 26 Jun 2025. Read paras 3-6, 9-11, 15-16. The current government framework (LEAP) and regulator roles. https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf
2. **Strategic Review of Business Models amid Digital Transformation** — HKMA, 9 Mar 2026. Read the whole two pages. The one policy document here that asks something of your board. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260309-1-EN/20260309-1-EN.pdf
3. **The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address** — 16 Sep 2026. Read paras 35, 49-51 and 99 (PDF pp.22-23, 26-27, 33). The latest dated targets for the HKMA, the SFC and CMU OmniClear. https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

## Open items

- The 2026 VA licensing bill had not appeared in the documents reviewed for this guide by 25 Sep 2026. In June 2026 the government said it and the SFC would introduce it this year, covering VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management service providers. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- The Blueprint's Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline and Quantum Preparedness Index detail documents are not in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- The 2023 Policy Address does not mention virtual assets; its nearest items are blockchain-based e-licences and a green fintech subsidy scheme. [S:61458655f37b, paras 41, 72(iv)]
- Canon locator correction: the 2026 Policy Address digital-bond items are in para 35(ii)-(iv) on p.23, not para 34 as one canon entry states; this module uses the text.

title: Your bank's legal status for digital assets
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain which legal hat the bank wears for each digital-asset activity, who supervises it, and which rulebook binds which entity in the group.

## In 60 seconds

A bank in Hong Kong is an Authorized Institution (AI), authorized and supervised under the Banking Ordinance. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.1] When it carries on business in regulated activities (a term the Securities and Futures Ordinance, or SFO, defines), it must be registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) as a Registered Institution (RI). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is the RI's front-line supervisor, and its Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module SB-1 explains how. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] A company licensed by the SFC under SFO s.116 or s.117 is a Licensed Corporation (LC). [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1] The joint SFC–HKMA virtual-asset (VA) circulars address intermediaries, a term that covers both LCs and RIs. [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1; S:8a016a912528, para 31] Under the proposed VA dealing and custody regimes, banks would register with the SFC while the HKMA would be their frontline regulator; VA custodians that are subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks would be regulated by the SFC. [S:f673ef6dcb63, paras 1.10, 2.36; S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)] Some May 2026 HKMA circulars are addressed to all AIs and others only to RIs, so scope checks matter. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1; S:a0bd48559762, p.1]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPM SB-1 (V.4) Supervision of SFC-registered AIs | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Application] |
| AML/CFT (anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism) Guideline for AIs | HKMA | 25 May 2023 | In force | All AIs incl. RIs | [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3] |
| Joint circular on VA-related activities + supplement | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023; 30 Sep 2025 | In force (changed for Relevant Stablecoins by the 27 May 2026 RI circular) | LCs; RIs | [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:b79266f3da51, para 4]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.2] |
| RI circular: Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (formulated jointly with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs only | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2] |
| AI letter: Relevant Stablecoin-related activities | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| RI circular: VA financing, shared order book, withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs only | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1] |
| Custody guidance (updated) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs + subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] |
| VA dealing regime (banks register; HKMA frontline) | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks and stored value facilities (SVFs) register; LCs, RIs and SFC-licensed VA trading platforms (VATPs) get expedited approval | [S:f673ef6dcb63, paras 1.10, 2.36]; [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36] |
| VA custodian regime | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks, bank subsidiaries, custodians | [S:30b60438f017, paras 2.12(a), 2.48]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 41] |
| VA advisory and management regimes | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 (proposal); 26 May 2026 (conclusions) | Conclusions published | Proposal: only banks could register (others licensed) | [S:6186c01c6649, footnotes 9-10]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, Introduction, p.3] |

## Key facts

- An AI carrying on business in regulated activities is required to be registered with the SFC as an RI; the SFC registers AIs under SFO s.119. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2, 2.2.1]
- The SFC holds ultimate responsibility, but the HKMA is the RI's front-line supervisor, and the SFC may rely on HKMA supervision under SFO s.5(3). [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- Each RI needs at least two executive officers to supervise each regulated activity directly. Each needs the Monetary Authority's (MA's) written consent, and at least one of them must be on hand at all times. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 1.1.1, 2.2.4]
- Only individuals entered on the HKMA Register may perform a regulated function for an RI, so they should be submitted before they start. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.1, 4.3.5]
- An associated entity of an RI is a company in a controlling-entity relationship with it that receives or holds the RI's client assets in Hong Kong. [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1]
- An RI should notify the SFC and HKMA if it intends to engage in any VA activity or change it, including the type of clients served. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline applies to all AIs, including RIs; RIs and associated entities that are AIs must also have regard to the SFC AML/CFT guideline, including its Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and footnote 1]
- The joint circular addresses intermediaries (LCs and RIs) and reminds them to give the SFC (and, where relevant, the HKMA) advance notice before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1]
- The Sep 2025 supplement lets LCs and RIs offer staking to clients they deal in VAs for, only through segregated accounts with an SFC-licensed platform or an AI (or a subsidiary of a locally incorporated AI). [S:b79266f3da51, paras 4-5]
- The May 2026 Relevant Stablecoin circular is addressed to RIs. It states that the VA dealing, advisory and asset management requirements in the joint circulars and in it do not apply to AIs that are not RIs, nor to an HKMA-licensed issuer for its own coin; those are expected to meet similar standards the HKMA issues separately. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]
- A separate HKMA letter says all AIs doing Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management should follow the RI standards, and reminds them to discuss with the HKMA in advance. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1; Implementation, p.2]
- Under the Stablecoins Ordinance, only specified licensed institutions may offer a fiat-referenced stablecoin in Hong Kong. [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 3]
- The HKMA register of licensed stablecoin issuers lists The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited under licence FRS02, effective 10 Apr 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- For a licensed issuer that is an AI, the para 7.1.3 board expectations (including one-third independent non-executive directors) do not apply; it should follow the Banking Ordinance and related guidance instead. [S:240be6833157, para 7.1.3]
- The June 2025 VA dealing proposal said banks would have to register with the SFC, with the HKMA consulted. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]
- It proposed that the HKMA be frontline regulator for banks' VA dealing, with powers to inspect premises and investigate suspected non-compliance. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 2.36]
- For VA custody, the proposal made the HKMA frontline regulator for banks, while VA custodians that are subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks would be regulated by the SFC. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
- The Dec 2025 custody conclusions exempt banks, which are subject to existing HKMA capital requirements, from the HK$10m paid-up capital and HK$3m liquid capital custodian baseline. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42]
- The Dec 2025 further consultation proposed that only banks could register with the SFC (rather than be licensed) for VA advisory or VA management services. [S:6186c01c6649, footnotes 9-10]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Hold SFC registration for each regulated activity carried on, with at least two HKMA-consented executive officers per activity. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.1, 2.2.4]
- [ ] Register relevant individuals on the HKMA Register before they start. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.1, 4.3.5]
- [ ] Apply the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline bank-wide; for the RI and any associated entities that are AIs, also have regard to SFC AML/CFT guideline Chapter 12. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- [ ] If the bank is locally incorporated, make sure its subsidiaries that provide digital-asset custody, or staking from custody, meet the HKMA standards. [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Map every digital-asset activity to its entity and capacity (AI, RI, LC subsidiary, associated entity) before applying a circular. [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2]
- [ ] Keep the relevant-individual database current; notify Register changes and specified fitness information within 7 business days. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.3, 4.3.6, 5.5]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the SFC and HKMA before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- [ ] Notify the HKMA in advance of an intended SFC registration application. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.3]
- [ ] Consider early pre-application contact with the SFC or HKMA for the coming dealing regime, which the conclusions encourage. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Confirm a stablecoin issuer counterparty is on the HKMA register. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register note]
- [ ] Confirm VA dealing partners are SFC-licensed VATPs or, for Relevant Stablecoins only, the HKMA-licensed issuer of that coin. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]; [S:a0bd48559762, para (1), p.3]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- Our VA conduct rules reach us as an RI; the HKMA supervises, the SFC keeps ultimate responsibility. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- Scope matters: the May 2026 Relevant Stablecoin circular is addressed to RIs, while the separate stablecoin-activity letter covers all AIs. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

**To business heads**
- As an RI, we should notify the SFC and HKMA when we intend to start or change VA services. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- Under the proposed custodian regime, a custody subsidiary would be regulated by the SFC, while the HKMA would be frontline regulator for the bank itself. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]

**To the CEO**
- Under the proposed dealing and custody regimes, the SFC would license and register providers, while the HKMA would be frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- The MA can withdraw or suspend an executive officer's consent for misconduct, and each regulated activity must always have at least one executive officer on hand. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 6.3]

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- A bank VA custodian would use existing HKMA capital rules, not the custodian capital baseline. [S:f41a543388bc, para 41]
- The RI financing circular requires loans secured solely by VAs to be handled as clean loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

## Common mix-ups

- "SFC AML Chapter 12 binds the whole bank." It applies to RIs and associated entities that are AIs on a have-regard basis only. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- "The joint circular is an SFC rule aimed at brokers, not us." It addresses RIs too, and reaches banks through HKMA frontline supervision. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:8934af8cc884, paras 1.1.1, 2.1.3]
- "The May 2026 RI stablecoin circular covers all AIs." It is addressed to RIs; AIs that are not RIs are covered by a separate HKMA letter. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- "A bank subsidiary custodian is supervised like the bank." Under the proposal it would be regulated by the SFC. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
- "VA financing rules apply to every AI." The May 2026 financing circular is addressed to RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1-2]

## Read these first

1. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)** — HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 1.1.1, 2.1-2.2, 4.3, 4.16.1, 5.6. The rulebook for your RI status. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
2. **Public Consultation on Legislative Proposal to Regulate Dealing in Virtual Assets** — FSTB/SFC, 27 Jun 2025. Read paras 1.10 and 2.36. How banks would be registered and supervised. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VADEALING_consultation_paper_en.pdf
3. **Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read footnote 3 (p.2), paras (1)-(4) and Implementation (p.9). A worked example of RI-only scope. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- On 24 Jun 2026 the Government said it would introduce a bill to the Legislative Council (LegCo) this year for VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes; The documents reviewed hold no bill text, so final bank registration mechanics are not yet in statute. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- No document reviewed for this guide has a HKMA or SFC text on how registration under the new VA regimes will interact with an RI's existing SFO registration, beyond expedited approval. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 67]
- The documents reviewed for this guide lack the Banking Ordinance and SFO text on executive officers; SB-1 is the only source used.

## Related modules

title: Engaging the HKMA and SFC
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can list the main talk-to-the-regulator-first duties that apply to a bank's digital-asset plans, and explain the HKMA's engagement channels: the Supervisory Incubator, the 2026 business-model review and the earlier (now superseded) stablecoin issuer sandbox.

## In 60 seconds

Since January 2022 the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has expected any bank that plans a virtual-asset (VA) activity to discuss it with the HKMA and get feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5] Later circulars repeat that step for tokenised products, custody, staking and services in HKMA-licensed (Relevant) stablecoins. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6; S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2; S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation; S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2] When the bank acts as a Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) Registered Institution (RI), it should also tell both regulators ahead of time before starting or changing VA dealing, advice or asset management. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] The capital rules add a separate trigger: a bank must notify the HKMA when it acquires a new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] For distributed ledger technology (DLT) projects, the HKMA runs a Supervisory Incubator with a dedicated team and optional live trials. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] In March 2026 the HKMA said it expects every bank's board to endorse a strategic business plan on digital change within six months. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIs' interface with VAs and VA service providers (VASPs) | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | All Authorized Institutions (AIs) | [S:642680fa4467, p.5] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | Licensed corporations (LCs); RIs via HKMA | [S:8a016a912528, para 31] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6] |
| Custody circular (first version) | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Updated custody guidance and Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Staking from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation] |
| Supervisory Incubator for DLT | HKMA | 8 Jan 2025 | Pilot | AIs | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] |
| Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) SB-1 (V.4) | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] |
| Supplemental joint circular | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs; RIs | [S:b79266f3da51, para 10] |
| SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 (applies from 1 Jan 2026) | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] |
| SPM CR-L-5 Major Acquisitions (V.3) | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 | In force | Locally incorporated AIs | [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |
| RI circular and AI letter on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs; all AIs | [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2] |
| SFC circular 26EC26 on Relevant Stablecoin services | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VA trading platforms (VATPs); LCs | [S:19d52ade6849, para 12] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox | HKMA | 12 Mar 2024 | Superseded | Would-be issuers | [S:28616d929735, opening para] |

## Key facts

- A bank planning any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA (and other regulators where relevant) and obtain feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5]
- Before selling or issuing tokenised products, a bank should have policies and controls in place and discuss its plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6]
- A bank, or a local bank's subsidiary, that intends to offer digital-asset custody should discuss it with the HKMA first and show, to the HKMA's satisfaction, that it meets the Annex standards. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- The February 2024 circular asked existing custodians to confirm compliance to the HKMA within six months; the May 2026 letter supersedes it and simply asks existing custodians to review and revise their controls. [S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- Before launching staking from custody, a bank should have adequate policies and controls and discuss its plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation]
- Intermediaries, including RIs, should give the SFC, and where relevant the HKMA, advance notice before starting VA activities or changing them, including a change in client type. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- The September 2025 supplement lists changes needing prior notice: client type; first VA deposits or withdrawals; first staking service; first subscriptions or redemptions paid in VAs; other material changes. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
- SB-1 expects an RI to tell the SFC and the HKMA when it plans to start, or change, VA activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- An RI needs at least two executive officers per regulated activity, and each executive officer needs the Monetary Authority's (MA's) written consent, applied for through the HKMA. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9-4.3.10]
- RIs should give the HKMA and SFC advance notice before distributing Relevant Stablecoin-related products, dealing in, advising on or managing Relevant Stablecoins, or materially changing those arrangements. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- All AIs (not only RIs) should discuss Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
- Under CRP-1, a bank that acquires a new type of cryptoasset must notify the HKMA and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees to the bank's own classification assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- A locally incorporated AI needs the Monetary Authority's written consent to acquire shares worth 5% or more of its Tier 1 capital; equity-like cryptoassets count as shares. [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1]
- The Supervisory Incubator, launched on 8 January 2025, gives banks one supervisory contact point to confirm DLT risk controls before full launch, with optional live trials; tokenised deposits were an initial focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]
- Incubator participants may get some supervisory flexibility, decided case by case. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and fn 2]
- The HKMA expects each bank's board to oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan on these technology shifts within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- That circular repeats that new digital-asset activities should be discussed with the HKMA before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]
- The stablecoin issuer sandbox (March 2024) let would-be issuers test in a limited way; admission did not mean HKMA endorsement or regulation, and a licence would need a separate application. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, paras 1-2]
- The HKMA later said sandbox participation is neither a precondition for nor a guarantee of a licence. [S:e0b249a7eb8c, Licensing regime section, para 5]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Discuss each new VA product or service with the HKMA and obtain its feedback on risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- [ ] Have the board oversee and endorse the strategic business plan the March 2026 circular asks for. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- [ ] Get the MA's written consent for each RI executive officer, applying through the HKMA. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the changes that trigger prior notice: client type, first VA deposits or withdrawals, first staking, first VA-funded subscriptions, other material changes. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
- [ ] If the bank already offers custody, review and revise controls against the 2026 Annex. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] If a cryptoasset with an HKMA-agreed Group 1a, 1b or 2a classification stops meeting the conditions, move it to Group 2b at once; any later move to another group needs HKMA agreement. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.1.3, 2.1.5]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Tokenised products, custody, staking: discuss with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.6]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3]
- [ ] RI VA activities and changes: notify the SFC and the HKMA in advance. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]; [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- [ ] Relevant Stablecoin activities: RIs notify the HKMA and SFC; all AIs discuss with the HKMA. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]
- [ ] New cryptoasset type: notify the HKMA on acquisition. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Equity-like token stakes at or above 5% of Tier 1: seek consent; other significant acquisitions: give at least one month's notice. [S:13365a31e794, paras 1.1, 2.9.1]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Do not treat a firm's sandbox status as a licence; check the HKMA's Register of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers instead. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, para 2]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Every VA, tokenisation, custody, staking or stablecoin launch starts with an HKMA discussion; for RI activities the SFC and HKMA also expect advance notice. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- The 2026 custody letter dropped the six-month confirmation; existing custodians should review and revise their controls instead. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

**To business heads**
- The HKMA discussion comes before go-live for any new digital-asset activity, as the March 2026 circular restates. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]
- Changing client type, or first allowing VA deposits, staking or VA-funded subscriptions, should be flagged in advance to the SFC and, where relevant, the HKMA. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA asked each board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- The Supervisory Incubator gives banks a dedicated HKMA team for supervisory feedback, and optional live trials, before a full DLT launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- A new cryptoasset type must be notified to the HKMA on acquisition and sits in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees to the bank's classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Equity-like tokens count as shares for the 5%-of-Tier-1 consent test. [S:13365a31e794, fn 1]

## Common mix-ups

- "Telling the SFC is enough." SB-1 expects RIs to tell both regulators, and the HKMA's own circulars add a prior-discussion step. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]; [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- "The SFC's 26EC26 notice rule on admitting stablecoins binds us." It is addressed to VATPs and LCs; for RIs the HKMA's RI circular sets the advance-notice duty. [S:19d52ade6849, para 12]; [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- "Every crypto trade needs a CRP-1 notification." Only a new type does: a first Bitcoin position triggers it, but Bitcoin futures after existing spot exposure do not. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2 and fn 7]
- "The six-month custody confirmation still applies." It belonged to the superseded 2024 circular. [S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- "Incubator or sandbox entry means approval." Incubator flexibility is case by case; sandbox admission was not an endorsement. [S:fae36c380174, p.1]; [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, para 2]

## Read these first

1. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs**, HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3-5, ending with the AIs' VA-related proposals section. It is the root of the prior-discussion expectation. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
2. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)**, HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 2.1.3, 2.2.4, 4.3 and 5.6. Sets RI notification and executive-officer consent duties. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
3. **VA-related activities in relation to Relevant Stablecoins (RI circular)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read Background (pp.1-2) and Implementation (p.9). The newest advance-notice duty. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- No HKMA form, template or response timeline for prior discussion appears in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- The six-month window in the March 2026 business-model circular ran to about 9 September 2026; No document reviewed for this guide has a HKMA follow-up on submissions. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- No document reviewed for this guide has a public list of Supervisory Incubator participants.
- The December 2025 consultation conclusions on VA custodian services say banks, and subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks, that safekeep private keys for client VAs would need a licence or registration under the proposed regime; the stated aim is to introduce a bill into the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026. No bill text is in the documents reviewed for this guide (see A1). [S:f41a543388bc, paras 35(b), 65]

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [B1](#m-B1), [B3](#m-B3), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [C4](#m-C4)

title: Governance, risk and technology expectations
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain what the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) expects of the board, of new-product risk assessment, of distributed ledger technology (DLT) and vendor risk, and of private-key control, and point to the paragraph for each.

## In 60 seconds

The HKMA's Pillar 2 guideline for locally incorporated authorized institutions (AIs) says the board and senior management should understand the risks of new or complex activities, and names cryptoasset activities as an example. [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; para 4.2.8, p.63] Before any new product, new business practice or new technology goes live, the HKMA anti-money laundering (AML) guideline requires a money laundering and terrorist financing (ML/TF) risk assessment. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11] For DLT, the HKMA published ten non-binding risk considerations in April 2024 and a longer research study in March 2025. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]; [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4] Custody, staking and tokenised-product circulars add concrete vendor due-diligence and key-management expectations: keys in tamper-resistant devices, generated and backed up in Hong Kong, no single point of failure, and 98% of client virtual assets (VAs) in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i), (l) and fn 8]; [S:4641e6c404d2, section C, pp.2-3]; [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3] Where capital or risk management around cryptoassets falls short, the HKMA may consider capital add-ons, provisioning, limits or other measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPM CA-G-5 Supervisory Review Process (V.7) | HKMA | 19 Dec 2025 | In force | Locally incorporated AIs | [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; paras 3.6.6, 4.2.8] |
| AML/CFT Guideline for AIs (revised May 2023) | HKMA | 25 May 2023 | In force | AIs, including Registered Institutions (RIs) | [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.3, 2.10-2.11] |
| DLT risk-management considerations (cover letter + Annex) | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs (non-binding considerations) | [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]; [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction] |
| DLT in the Financial Sector: study | HKMA | 19 Mar 2025 | Exploratory | AIs (research, not a rule) | [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs (tokenised products not regulated under the Securities and Futures Ordinance) | [S:b2719f3dcb37, Coverage, p.1; Section A, p.3] |
| Staking from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] |
| Updated custody guidance Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 1, 11, 14-19] |
| SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, Application, p.1; para 2.1.1] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4] |

## Key facts

- Directors and senior managers of a locally incorporated AI should understand, across the whole firm, the risks of new or complex products and activities; CA-G-5 names cryptoasset activities as an example. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8, p.63]
- CA-G-5 notes, "Cryptoasset activities and associated risks are relatively new and evolving." For related gaps in capital adequacy or risk management, the HKMA may consider capital add-ons, provisioning for foreseeable and estimable cryptoasset losses, limits or other measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6, p.53]
- The HKMA expects each AI's board to oversee and endorse, within six months of the 9 March 2026 circular, a formal strategic business plan that looks at adapting products, revenue models, customer engagement, risk management and operations. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4]
- A bank should spot and weigh the ML/TF risks of new products, new business practices (including delivery mechanisms) and new or developing technologies, do so before launch, and take measures to manage and mitigate them. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
- In the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline, the word should signals a mandatory requirement, just as must does. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- The April 2024 DLT considerations are non-binding and non-exhaustive; in line with a risk-based, technology-neutral approach, the HKMA checks whether a bank has adequate systems and controls for the extra risks DLT may bring. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, pp.1-2]
- The board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption; the bank should update technology-risk, business-continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT factors as needed, and have enough staff with DLT expertise. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1]
- A bank should choose a DLT network type that suits the nature and risks of the application, and consider whether node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse; a permissionless network would likely be inappropriate for highly critical or sensitive functions without adequate compensating controls. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 2 and 5]
- Where DLT supports critical functions, business continuity plans should include DLT test scenarios such as cyberattacks, loss or theft of private keys and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]
- The March 2025 study drew on input from the Insurance Authority, the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), surveyed 113 financial institutions, and builds on the 2024 circular; it is research, not a new rule. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Foreword, p.3; Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48]
- For outsourced DLT work, the study suggests assessing vendors at every stage, contract terms on performance and data security, and predefined backup vendors or failover plans. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Section 4.2.4, item 1, p.48]
- Before launching custody, a bank should complete a comprehensive risk assessment, with effective board and senior-management oversight before and after launch. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
- As a general principle, VA custody may be delegated or outsourced only to another AI (including a locally incorporated AI's subsidiary), an SFC-licensed VA trading platform, or an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer that has HKMA consent to hold the stablecoins it issues. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- Due diligence on a custody delegate covers, among other things, independent code reviews and the provider's software release process, followed by ongoing review of its security controls and disaster-recovery testing; ultimate responsibility stays with the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 15, 19]
- Key management expectations for client VAs: tamper-resistant devices such as hardware security modules (HSMs), with HSM vendor due diligence; seeds and keys generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong; key sharding or similar against single points of failure; transaction details shown in human-readable form for signers. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i)]
- Where the client assets in custody are VAs, 98% should sit in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]
- For tokenised products outside the Securities and Futures Ordinance, due diligence on issuers and their technology vendors should cover key management, theft and hacking safeguards, smart-contract audits and contingency plans for DLT failures. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- For staking, the bank should keep possession or control of the means to unstake client VAs (for example, withdrawal-address private keys), do due diligence on each blockchain protocol, and vet and monitor any third-party staking provider. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.2, section A and fn 2; pp.2-3, section C]
- CRP-1 says AIs must have policies, governance, staff and IT able to assess cryptoasset risk, and must document the basis for each classification and make it available to the HKMA on request. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Run the ML/TF risk assessment before launching any new product (for example, a VA, tokenisation or stablecoin service), new business practice or new technology. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
- [ ] Brief the board so it understands cryptoasset risks firm-wide and sets limits within risk appetite. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8, pp.63-64]
- [ ] Complete a comprehensive risk assessment before custody launch, under board oversight. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT factors. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1]
- [ ] Apply the para 11 key controls to client VAs, including 98% cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8]
- [ ] Monitor custody security 24/7, test system changes before deployment and monitor dependencies. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23-25]
- [ ] Keep documented classification evidence for each cryptoasset exposure. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Take the DLT considerations into account when preparing DLT-related submissions, as the HKMA encourages. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]
- [ ] Obtain HKMA consent before appointing an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer to hold the stablecoins it issues; its keys must be kept in Hong Kong or a location the HKMA accepts. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Document due diligence on custody delegates and HSM vendors, and review them regularly. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 11(a), 15]
- [ ] Vet tokenisation platforms and staking providers before use and monitor them after. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]; [S:4641e6c404d2, section C, p.3]
- [ ] Consider whether DLT node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline requires an ML/TF risk assessment before any new product, practice or technology launch; should there is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11]
- The DLT considerations are non-binding, but the HKMA encourages banks to take them into account in DLT-related submissions. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]

**To business heads**
- As a general principle, VA custody can only be outsourced to another AI, an SFC-licensed platform, or a licensed stablecoin issuer (its own coins, with HKMA consent). [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- Tokenised-product sales need issuer and technology-vendor due diligence before offering to customers. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA expects the board to understand cryptoasset risks and to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8]; [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4]
- Crypto-related gaps in capital or risk management may lead the HKMA to consider capital add-ons, provisioning or limits. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Custody keys: HSMs, Hong Kong location, sharding, anti-blind-signing, 98% cold storage for client VAs. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8]
- DLT continuity plans should test key loss, cyberattacks and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]

## Common mix-ups

- "The DLT considerations are rules with deadlines." They are non-binding and set no deadline; the custody Annex is where the firm numbers sit. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 8]
- "The March 2025 DLT study sets new rules." It is a research study that builds on the 2024 circular. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48]
- "Outsourcing custody moves the risk away." Ultimate responsibility stays with the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 19]
- "Insurance must cover 100% of hot-wallet assets." That fixed cover (50% cold, 100% hot and other storage) came from the February 2024 guidance, which the May 2026 circular superseded; the 2026 Annex instead makes the bank liable for losses attributable to it and requires adequate financial resources, which may include insurance. [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- "SFC's VA AML chapter sets our new-product rule." For a bank, the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline governs; RIs must also have regard to the SFC guideline, including its VA chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and fn 1]

## Read these first

1. **Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT (Annex)**, HKMA, 16 Apr 2024. Read all ten items. The HKMA's DLT checklist. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240416-2-EN/20240416-2-EN.pdf
2. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Custodial Services (Annex)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 1, 10-11, 14-19 and 23-25. Governance, keys and outsourcing in one place. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
3. **SPM CA-G-5 Supervisory Review Process (V.7)**, HKMA, 19 Dec 2025. Read paras 3.6.6 (p.53) and 4.2.8 (pp.63-64). The board-understanding and Pillar 2 hooks. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251217-2-EN/CA-G-5.pdf

## Open items

- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline for AIs has no stablecoin, unhosted-wallet or VA red-flag provisions; it mentions VAs only in passing (VA transfers as occasional transactions, VA service providers in correspondent-type relationships). See D3 for how the gap is handled. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1, 11.23]
- No general HKMA outsourcing or technology-risk module is among the documents reviewed for this guide; only DLT- and custody-specific outsourcing text is covered.
- Two CA-G-5 V.7 copies exist: one dated 27 November 2025 with a placeholder header date (xx.12.2025) and the 19 December 2025 version. This module cites the 19 December 2025 text; the crypto paragraphs match. [S:04bbb675089e, p.1]; [S:349a543ae2f0, p.1]

## Related modules

[B2](#m-B2), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3), [D4](#m-D4)

title: Selling, dealing and advising on virtual assets
md:
