For the Head of Compliance at a bank that is also a Registered Institution (RI) of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC): after this module you can explain what the joint regime of the SFC and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) lets the bank sell, deal in, advise on and stake, and what it must check first.

## In 60 seconds

Since January 2022 the SFC and the HKMA have set their expectations for intermediaries, including banks registered with the SFC, in a joint circular on virtual-asset (VA) activities [S:e4828fcba126, p.1]. The current base text is dated 22 December 2023 and replaced the two earlier versions [S:8a016a912528, para 3]. A supplemental circular of 30 September 2025 brought in refinements and relaxations [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 2], and HKMA guidance of 27 May 2026 eased the rules for licensed stablecoins and allowed VA financing [S:a0bd48559762, Background; S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2]. VA-related products are very likely complex, and complex ones should generally go to professional investors (PIs) only [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1]. Clients other than institutional and qualified corporate PIs should be assessed for VA knowledge, and dealing should be done through SFC-licensed platforms (or, for licensed stablecoins, the licensed issuer) [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 17; S:a0bd48559762, para (1)]. The detailed conduct rules are imposed as conditions on the bank's SFC registration, and the SFC (and the HKMA where applicable) should be told in advance of new VA activities or changes [S:8a016a912528, paras 19, 31].

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities | SFC + HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | Superseded | LCs, RIs | [S:e4828fcba126, p.1] |
| Joint circular (revised) | SFC + HKMA | 20 Oct 2023 | Superseded | LCs, RIs | [S:a37d28d879cf, p.1; S:8a016a912528, para 3] |
| Joint circular (current base) + Appendices 1–7 | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:8a016a912528, p.1], [S:0027a8747112, landing page] |
| Supplemental joint circular (staking, off-platform trades, in-kind flows) | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:d5ebca32c92b, p.1] |
| HKMA circular on Relevant Stablecoin activities + Appendix A1 (dealing/advice T&Cs) and A2 (portfolio management T&Cs) | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:a0bd48559762, pp.1–2], [S:31b4f67e0233, p.1] |
| Letter on Relevant Stablecoin-related activities | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| Circular on Relevant Stablecoin services (26EC26) | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VATPs, LCs (bank's counterparties) | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] |
| Guidance on VA financing, shared order book and client VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1] |
| Standalone licensing regimes for VA dealing, advisory and management | FSTB + SFC | Dec 2025 / May 2026 | Conclusions published | Banks would register with the SFC for VA advisory and management | [S:6186c01c6649, p.1, paras 52, 58 and fns 9–10], [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] |

LC = SFC-licensed corporation. AI = authorized institution (a bank licensed under the Banking Ordinance). VATP = SFC-licensed VA trading platform. FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau. T&Cs = terms and conditions.

## Key facts

- The 22 December 2023 circular replaced both earlier joint circulars in full [S:8a016a912528, para 3].
- VA-related products are those that mainly invest in VAs, get their value mainly from VAs, or track VA returns. The regulators say such products are very likely complex, so suitability applies even without a solicitation or recommendation, apart from the exchange-traded products in paras 7 and 9 [S:8a016a912528, para 5].
- Complex VA-related products should be offered to PIs only, apart from a limited set of products [S:8a016a912528, para 6.1]. These are certain VA derivatives traded on exchanges specified by the SFC and SFC-authorised VA funds. For those traded on exchange (the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) for the funds), an order placed without solicitation or recommendation can be executed without a suitability check, but the knowledge test still applies [S:8a016a912528, paras 7, 9, 9.1].
- Everyone except institutional PIs and qualified corporate PIs should be assessed for VA knowledge. A one-off test is acceptable. A client without the knowledge may trade only after the firm has trained them [S:8a016a912528, para 6.2 and fn 10].
- Firms should partner only with SFC-licensed platforms for VA dealing, either by introducing clients or through an omnibus account, and should offer VA dealing only to clients of their Type 1 (dealing in securities) business [S:8a016a912528, paras 17–18].
- Before serving retail dealing clients, a firm should set an exposure limit for each client with reference to the client's financial situation, including net worth, and should restrict them to tokens the platform offers to retail investors [S:8a016a912528, para 20(a)(ii), (iv)].
- Advice on VAs is limited to Type 1 or Type 4 (advising on securities) clients. Any VA recommended to a retail client should be included in at least two acceptable indices from at least two different index providers [S:8a016a912528, paras 26, 28(a)].
- A portfolio triggers the Appendix 7 (RA9, asset management) terms if it has a stated VA objective or plans to put 10% or more of gross asset value (GAV) into VAs. Ancillary discretionary VA dealing under Type 1 should stay below 10% of GAV [S:8a016a912528, paras 23–24].
- The September 2025 supplement allows staking for clients the firm already deals VAs for. Staking should go only through segregated accounts at an SFC-licensed platform or an AI [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4–5].
- The same supplement allows trades through a licensed platform's off-platform trading services. Subscribing for or redeeming products with VAs, including in-kind fund flows, is not treated as providing VA dealing services [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 6–7].
- The net-worth check and the VA-futures risk disclosure do not apply to institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 8–9].
- From May 2026, RIs may partner with the licensed issuer of a Relevant Stablecoin (a specified stablecoin issued under a Stablecoins Ordinance licence) as well as with VATPs. Paragraph 20(a)(iii) is removed, so retail omnibus dealing may go through a PI-only VATP if retail clients trade only tokens that VATP has admitted for retail trading [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (1)].
- For clients whose accounts are clearly marked as Relevant-Stablecoin-only, no knowledge test or exposure limit is needed. Relevant Stablecoin holdings also need not be counted when setting any client's exposure limit [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)–(b); S:31b4f67e0233, paras 6.2A, 6.4, 6.4A].
- RIs providing VA dealing may now offer VA financing (credit for VA dealing), but only to their securities margin clients. Where VA collateral is relied on, only bitcoin, ether and Relevant Stablecoins are eligible, with a haircut of at least 60% on bitcoin and ether [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (1), (2), (4) and fn 5].
- In January 2026 the SFC reprimanded and fined a licensed broker HK$4 million. Between November 2018 and November 2022 it let retail clients trade VA products that the 2018 and 2022 circulars limited to PIs. The 1,446 trades involved 32 VA products. It did not assess VA knowledge or give VA-specific warnings, and had no specific product due diligence procedures for VA products [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–5].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Classify every VA-linked product and apply the PI-only, suitability and knowledge-test rules that follow from that classification [S:8a016a912528, paras 5–10].
- Carry out extra due diligence on any VA fund that is not SFC-authorised, using Appendix 4 [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].
- Give VA risk disclosures and warning statements to clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:8a016a912528, para 15].
- Receive or withdraw client VAs only through segregated accounts at the partner platform or at an AI that meets HKMA custody standards [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)].
- For Relevant Stablecoins, disclose material information on the coin's stabilisation mechanism and redemption arrangements. Commission rebates or other benefits should not be the main basis for soliciting or recommending one [S:a0bd48559762, paras (5), (8), (10)].

**Controls & monitoring**
- Have adequate policies, procedures and controls, and train staff, for Relevant Stablecoin activities [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9].
- Keep Relevant-Stablecoin-only clients to Relevant Stablecoins. Before dealing in any other VA for them, apply the full rules, including the knowledge test [S:a0bd48559762, fn 4].
- Keep the listed records on client VAs, staking and VA financing for at least seven years. Records of orders and instructions on client VAs need be kept for at least two years [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 9.6–9.8].
- Obtain an executed staking-risk acknowledgement from clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs before staking [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.7(b), 8.8].
- When relying on VA collateral, monitor its volatility in real time. Treat loans secured only by VAs as clean loans, because the Banking (Capital) Rules do not recognise VA collateral [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Tell the SFC in advance, and the HKMA where applicable, about any new VA activity or change to one, including a change in the type of client served [S:8a016a912528, para 31].
- Notify before the first client VA deposit or withdrawal, the first staking service, or the first VA-funded subscription or redemption [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 10].
- A bank that is an AI but not an RI should follow the same standards and discuss any Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting [S:1babdb609fc8, pp.1–2].
- Report any material breach of the terms, whether actual or suspected, to the SFC and the HKMA as soon as practicable [S:31b4f67e0233, para 12.1].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Confirm that the platform holds an actual SFC licence. Platforms that are only deemed licensed under AMLO Schedule 3G do not count (AMLO = Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance) [S:8a016a912528, para 17 and fn 20].
- Use only an SFC-licensed platform or an AI as the staking service provider. Confirm it has SFC approval or has discussed the service with the HKMA [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.2–8.3].
- For in-kind or VA-funded subscriptions, hold the VAs only at SFC-licensed platforms or AIs, and comply with the VA chapter (Chapter 12) of the SFC's anti-money-laundering (AML) guideline for those transfers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The regime reaches us as an RI through registration conditions that the SFC imposes, consulting the HKMA where applicable. The HKMA is our frontline, day-to-day supervisor [S:8a016a912528, para 19; S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3].
- Our AML baseline is the HKMA AML Guideline. As an RI we are also required to have regard to the SFC guideline's VA chapter (Chapter 12) [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 fn 1].

**To business heads**
- SFC-authorised VA funds are not PI-only, and retail can buy listed ones on SEHK. We should still assess VA knowledge first. Overseas non-derivative VA exchange-traded products remain PI-only [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 6.2, 9, 9.1].
- Since May 2026, clearly ring-fenced Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no knowledge test and no exposure limit. The coin must come from an HKMA-licensed issuer [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (3)].

**To the CEO**
- Parts of the regime were relaxed in December 2023, September 2025 and May 2026 [S:8a016a912528, para 9; S:d5ebca32c92b, para 2; S:a0bd48559762, Background]. Complex-product rules, knowledge tests and licensed venues remain [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.2, 17].
- In January 2026 the SFC fined a broker HK$4 million for VA distribution failures that ran from 2018 to 2022 [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–2].

**To Risk / CRO**
- Margin clients can get VA financing. Eligible VA collateral is limited to bitcoin, ether and Relevant Stablecoins, with at least a 60% haircut on bitcoin and ether. VA collateral gets no capital recognition [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5].
- Discretionary VA exposure under Type 1 should stay below 10% of the client account's GAV [S:31b4f67e0233, para 4.7].

## Common mix-ups

- "All VA products are PI-only." Not so. SFC-authorised VA funds are not PI-only, and certain VA derivatives traded on specified exchanges are exempt. A knowledge test is still needed [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 7, 9].
- "VA financing is banned." For RIs that was true until May 2026. RIs providing VA dealing may now offer it to their securities margin clients under HKMA conditions [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background and paras (1)–(2)].
- "The 2026 stablecoin relief covers any stablecoin and any bank." It covers only Relevant Stablecoins and only RIs. It does not cover a licensed issuer for its own coin [S:a0bd48559762, p.2 and fn 3]. AIs that are not RIs are told by a separate letter to follow the same standards [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1].
- "Deleting para 20(a)(iii) only matters for stablecoins." The deletion lets RIs serve retail clients in any VA through PI-only VATPs, as long as each token has been admitted for retail trading [S:a0bd48559762, para (1)].
- "The 2022 circular still sets the rules." Not so. The December 2023 circular replaced the 2022 and October 2023 circulars [S:8a016a912528, para 3]. Existing clients found to have VA knowledge by tests done before 22 December 2023 could continue to be served [S:8a016a912528, fn 40].

## Read these first

1. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities**, SFC + HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 5–15 (distribution), 16–22 (dealing), 23–29 (management and advice) and 30–31 (implementation). This is the base rulebook. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66
2. **Supplemental joint circular**, SFC + HKMA, 30 Sep 2025. Read paras 4–10 (staking, off-platform trades, in-kind flows, PI carve-outs, notifications). https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC50
3. **VA-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins**, HKMA to RIs, 27 May 2026. Read Sections I–IV, paras (1)–(17), fn 3–4 and Implementation (p.9). This is the current bank-specific relief and removes para 20(a)(iii). https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The standalone VA dealing, advisory and management licensing regimes are at the conclusions stage. The conclusions state that they will replace the current approach of imposing terms and conditions on SFC registrations [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]. No deeming arrangement is planned for existing VA advisory or management providers, but an expedited approval process is planned for LCs and RIs already providing those services [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 63, 67]. No bill text or commencement date is in the sources reviewed.
- A June 2026 reply to a Legislative Council (LegCo) question said a bill to set up VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes would go to LegCo within 2026 [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]. The sources reviewed do not show that it has been introduced.
- The SFC's Statement of Disciplinary Action behind the January 2026 fine is referenced in the press release but has not been reviewed here [S:415e4629a80f, Notes 3 and 5].
- Footnote 25 of the 2023 circular says firms should not provide financial accommodation for clients to acquire VAs [S:8a016a912528, fn 25]. For RIs, the May 2026 terms now allow it where the firm engages in securities margin financing [S:31b4f67e0233, para 4.3; S:e64b7b0267b2, p.5]. Registry summaries of the 2023 circular that still describe financing as prohibited are out of date.

## Related modules

[C2](#m-C2) (VA funds and ETFs), [C3](#m-C3) (Custody and key management), [C4](#m-C4) (Stablecoins), plus the AML/CFT and VATP modules.

title: VA funds and ETFs
md:
For the Head of Compliance at a bank that distributes funds or acts as participating dealer: after this module you can explain which crypto funds and tokenised funds may be sold in Hong Kong, on what terms, and what the bank checks before it sells, creates or redeems units.

## In 60 seconds

In October 2022 the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) began accepting applications to authorise exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that get exposure to virtual assets (VAs) mainly through futures [S:51dac2cabe78, para 6; S:c79c4686c5e0, para 5]. A December 2023 circular let authorised funds invest in spot VAs directly [S:5b6530666cc2, paras 2, 5]. A revised version in April 2025 added staking and other VA-related activities [S:353535602a83, paras 1–2, 27]. That version was in turn replaced on 27 May 2026 (26EC31) [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 3]. A fund seeking more than 10% of its net asset value (NAV) in VAs needs prior SFC consultation and approval [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 31]. It should invest only in tokens the Hong Kong public can trade on virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) licensed by the SFC, and should not have leveraged VA exposure at fund level [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 15]. Its trustee may delegate VA custody only to a licensed VATP, to an authorized institution (AI, such as a bank) that meets Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) custody standards, or to another entity the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 20]. Separate SFC circulars allow tokenised versions of authorised products, including tokenised fund classes [S:58ea8520974d, para 5 and fn 8]. Since the 20 April 2026 revision, these may also be traded on the secondary market on licensed VATPs [S:58ea8520974d, para 6; S:a64e364fd912, para 8]. When a bank distributes SFC-authorised VA funds, the joint SFC–HKMA circular sets the selling rules [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, para 9]. Participating dealers (PDs) for spot VA ETFs should be SFC-licensed corporations (LCs) or registered institutions (RIs), subject to any extra SFC terms [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8].

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circular on VA futures ETFs (22EC60) | SFC | 31 Oct 2022 | Superseded | Fund managers, distributors | [S:51dac2cabe78, p.1] |
| Circular on SFC-authorised funds with VA exposure (23EC65) | SFC | 22 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Funds, LCs, RIs | [S:5b6530666cc2, p.1] |
| Same circular, revised to add staking (25EC21) | SFC | 7 Apr 2025 | Superseded | Funds | [S:353535602a83, p.1] |
| Same circular, revised (26EC31) | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | Funds, managers, PDs, custodians | [S:c79c4686c5e0, p.1] |
| Tokenisation of SFC-authorised products (26EC22, revising 23EC53 of 2 Nov 2023) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | Product providers, distributors | [S:58ea8520974d, p.1], [S:d422282a262d, p.1] |
| Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products (26EC23) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | VATPs, LCs, RIs, product providers | [S:a64e364fd912, p.1] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] |
| Joint circular (distribution rules) + Sep 2025 supplement | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 / 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:8a016a912528, p.1], [S:d5ebca32c92b, p.1] |

## Key facts

- The first VA ETFs allowed were futures-based. At first only bitcoin and ether futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange were allowed, and the manager needed at least three years' track record in managing ETFs [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 10, 12].
- The 2022 circular also capped net derivative exposure at 100% of NAV and required intermediaries to apply the VA-knowledge test when serving clients in these ETFs [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 14, 16].
- Under the December 2023 circular, funds could invest directly in spot VAs [S:5b6530666cc2, para 5]. The first spot VA ETFs listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange on 30 April 2024 [S:e4236ed2600f, para 1].
- The current circular (26EC31) applies to public funds with more than 10% of NAV in VAs. It replaced the April 2025 version [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 1, 3].
- 26EC31 does not cover fund exposure to Relevant Stablecoins (fiat-referenced stablecoins issued under a licence granted under the Stablecoins Ordinance) or tokenised deposits. For those, the SFC points to question 20G of its FAQs on its code for unit trusts and mutual funds (UT Code) [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2 and fn 4].
- Eligible VAs are limited to tokens the Hong Kong public can trade on SFC-licensed VATPs. VA futures must trade on conventional regulated futures exchanges, and funds should not have leveraged VA exposure at fund level [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 13, 15].
- Funds should buy and sell spot VAs through SFC-licensed VATPs (on or off platform), or through AIs (or subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs) that comply with HKMA requirements [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 17 and fn 7].
- Spot ETFs may create and redeem units either in cash or in kind. For in-kind creations, PDs are expected to move VAs into the ETF's custody account at a VATP or an AI. The VAs may have been held locally or overseas [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18].
- PDs for spot VA ETFs should be LCs or RIs, and are subject to extra terms the SFC's Intermediaries Division may impose, set out in Appendix 6 of the joint circular [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8].
- The trustee may delegate VA custody only to an SFC-licensed VATP, to an AI (or a locally incorporated AI's subsidiary) that meets HKMA custody standards, or to another entity the SFC accepts. Custodians should keep most VA holdings in cold wallets, and store seeds and private keys securely in Hong Kong [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21].
- The SFC may allow VA funds to stake through licensed VATPs or, where applicable, AIs. Conditions include disclosing how much may be used, reporting in interim and annual reports, and prior SFC consultation and approval [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(d), 28(f), 31]. When it added staking in April 2025, the SFC said fund staking is capped to manage liquidity risk [S:36753b22e10a, para 4].
- On distribution, SFC-authorised VA funds are not restricted to professional investors (PIs). For units listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK), with no solicitation or recommendation, on-exchange orders can be executed without suitability or warning statements, but a VA-knowledge test still applies. Unlisted classes, or trades off exchange, need suitability, warnings and the knowledge test [S:8a016a912528, paras 9, 9.1–9.2 and fn 14].
- The tokenisation circular uses a see-through approach, looking past the token to the underlying product. It permits primary dealing in tokenised authorised products. Product providers should not use public permissionless blockchains unless they add proper controls [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 13].
- Retail investors may be offered secondary trading in tokenised products through on-screen matching on SFC-licensed VATPs. Controls include a price-deviation alert against the indicative NAV [S:a64e364fd912, paras 8, 12(a)].
- In March 2026 the Hong Kong public could buy 13 tokenised products, with tokenised-class assets of about $10.7 billion. The SFC expects the first secondary-trading batch to be mainly tokenised money market funds [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 3, 6].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Apply the joint circular's selling rules when distributing any SFC-authorised VA fund, including the knowledge test for all clients except institutional and qualified corporate PIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 9].
- Offer VA-related products that are complex products, such as VA funds not authorised by the SFC, only to PIs. For non-authorised VA funds, first do the Appendix 4 due diligence on the fund, its manager and its trading and custody counterparties [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1, 12.3; S:8a016a912528, appendices, Appendix 4].
- As a distributor of tokenised authorised products, be an LC or RI and apply the usual onboarding and suitability rules [S:58ea8520974d, para 18].
- For tokenised products that fall outside the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO) regime, and for tokenised deposits placed by customers, the HKMA expects the selling rules for the underlying product to apply. It also expects AIs to understand and control the extra risks from tokenisation [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. RIs selling tokenised products other than tokenised securities should follow this HKMA guidance [S:d5ebca32c92b, fn 2].

**Controls & monitoring**
- As a Connecting Broker (an LC or RI routing clients' trades to a VATP), show the price-deviation alert, tell clients they can subscribe or redeem at NAV instead, and get their confirmation of the risks before onboarding [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4].
- Keep an online interface showing indicative NAV, usually refreshed at least every 15 seconds while trading is open, plus the last NAV [S:a64e364fd912, para 20(b)].
- Where VA-related products are sold online, design the platform with access rights and controls that enforce selling restrictions [S:8a016a912528, para 11].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Give the SFC advance notice, and the HKMA too where relevant, before first letting clients subscribe or redeem with VAs, including in-kind flows [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 7(a), 10(d)].
- Before first engaging in secondary trading of tokenised products, notify the SFC. RIs are reminded to notify the HKMA too [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13].
- Before starting activities covered by the HKMA tokenised-products circular, discuss them with the HKMA [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- For in-kind flows, hold the VAs only in accounts with SFC-licensed platforms or AIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)]. The supplemental joint circular also points to Chapter 12 of the SFC's anti-money laundering (AML) guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VA service providers when handling these VA transfers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)].
- Do product due diligence on each VA-related product: its risks and features, target investors and selling restrictions, and regulatory status [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].
- On tokenised products covered by the HKMA circular, do due diligence on the issuer and its technology vendors, including smart-contract audits, private key management and distributed ledger technology (DLT) contingency plans [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The VA fund circular is written for product providers. The bank's own duties as distributor or PD come from the joint circular and any extra SFC terms for PDs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 8, 19, 27].
- For tokenised secondary trading, intermediaries notify the SFC first, and RIs are reminded to notify the HKMA as well [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13].

**To business heads**
- SEHK-listed VA ETFs can be traded on exchange for retail clients without solicitation, with a knowledge test. Unlisted classes of the same ETF need full suitability [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14].
- In-kind creation is allowed, and the VAs may come from overseas holdings. PDs are expected to move them into custody at a VATP or AI [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18].

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong has moved from futures-only VA ETFs (2022) to spot VA funds (2023), fund staking (2025) and a pilot of 24/7 secondary trading of tokenised funds (2026) [S:51dac2cabe78, para 12; S:5b6530666cc2, para 5; S:353535602a83, para 27; S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4].
- Tokenised-class assets were about $10.7 billion across 13 products as of March 2026 [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 3].

**To Risk / CRO**
- VA funds should not have leveraged VA exposure at fund level, and custody delegates are limited to VATPs, qualifying AIs, or entities the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 15, 20].
- Staking by funds needs prior SFC consultation and approval. Interim and annual reports should show staked holdings as a share of NAV, along with revenue and costs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(f), 31].

## Common mix-ups

- "Hong Kong only has futures VA ETFs." Direct spot exposure has been allowed since the December 2023 circular [S:5b6530666cc2, para 5].
- "A fund holding licensed stablecoins is a VA fund." 26EC31 excludes Relevant Stablecoins and tokenised deposits [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2].
- "The 2023 or 2025 fund circular still applies." Each was replaced, most recently by 26EC31 on 27 May 2026 [S:353535602a83, para 2; S:c79c4686c5e0, para 3].
- "Tokenised funds can only be subscribed and redeemed." The 20 April 2026 revision allows secondary trading on VATPs; the 2023 version had called for more caution [S:58ea8520974d, para 6; S:d422282a262d, para 6].
- "In-kind subscription makes the bank a VA dealer." The regulators say it is not treated as VA dealing, but notification, custody and AML conditions apply [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7].

## Read these first

1. **Circular on SFC-authorised funds with exposure to virtual assets (26EC31)**, SFC, revised 27 May 2026. Read paras 2, 11–22, 27–31. These set eligibility, PDs, custody, staking and consultation. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC31
2. **Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (26EC23)**, SFC, 20 Apr 2026. Read paras 8–16, 19–27 and fn 13. These cover trading channels, Connecting Broker duties and RI notification to the HKMA. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC23
3. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities**, SFC + HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 5–15 and Appendix 4. These give the distributor's selling rules and fund due diligence. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66

## Open items

- The detailed staking requirements for VA funds sit in question 20F of the UT Code FAQs, and question 20G covers stablecoin and tokenised-deposit exposure. Neither is in the documents reviewed for this guide [S:c79c4686c5e0, fn 4, fn 11].
- The supplemental joint circular cites the SFC's AML guideline for LCs and VA service providers for in-kind VA transfers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)]. How this maps onto the HKMA's own AML guideline for AIs is not stated in the circular.
- The SFC says it will review the first secondary-trading products and consider widening the product scope in due course. No timeline has been given [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6].
- The 2026 Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed VATPs and their use in settling tokenised money market funds [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)].

## Related modules

[C1](#m-C1) (Selling, dealing and advising), [C3](#m-C3) (Custody and key management), [C4](#m-C4) (Stablecoins), plus the tokenisation and Project Ensemble modules.

title: Custody of digital assets and key management
md:
For the Head of Compliance at a bank that holds, or plans to hold, clients' crypto or tokenised assets: after this module you can explain what the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA's) May 2026 custody standards expect, what changed from 2024, how staking fits in, and how the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and stablecoin rules set the benchmark for counterparties.

## In 60 seconds

In virtual asset (VA) custody, the core risk sits with whoever safekeeps the private keys, or similar instruments, that can move the assets [S:f41a543388bc, para 7]. Much of the rulebook is therefore about key management [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11]. The HKMA set custody standards for banks (authorized institutions, or AIs) in February 2024 and replaced them on 27 May 2026 with an updated annex of 26 paragraphs [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2; S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 1–26]. The new annex keeps the 98% cold-storage rule for client VAs and the rule that keys are kept in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8]. It adds detailed controls on how wallets are operated, drops the fixed insurance percentages, and, with HKMA consent, lets a bank appoint a licensed stablecoin issuer to hold that issuer's own coins [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11, fn 7, para 14(iii); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. The SFC sets its own custody rules for licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) [S:f1bbafccd556, Part X]. It says the standards in its August 2025 custody circular will also be core expectations for future VA custodians [S:562c0f8addce, p.2]. The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) published, with the SFC, consultation conclusions on a custodian licensing regime in December 2025, with a stated aim of introducing a bill into the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026 [S:f41a543388bc, Introduction, p.3].

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets + Annex | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:6bccca749ac2, p.1], [S:86e064b2a8d0, p.1] |
| Updated Guidance on Custodial Services + Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2], [S:ce05e67bcdce, p.1] |
| Staking services for VAs from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] |
| Staking services by VATPs + terms and conditions | SFC | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | VATPs and their associated entities | [S:50bf95ba3143, paras 1–2] |
| VATP Guidelines, Part X (custody) | SFC | Jun 2023 | In force | VATPs | [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.1–10.23] |
| Circular on custody of VAs (25EC44) | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | VATPs and associated entities | [S:562c0f8addce, p.1] |
| Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers, para 6.5.7 (keys) | HKMA | Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed stablecoin issuers | [S:240be6833157, p.1] |
| VA custodian services licensing regime | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | VA custodians, including banks that safekeep keys (licence or registration) | [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6, 35(b)] |

## Key facts

- The 2026 annex applies to client digital assets held by AIs and by subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs. Examples of digital assets it covers are VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets. Limited purpose digital tokens and the bank's or its group's own holdings are outside it [S:ce05e67bcdce, preamble and fn 1–4].
- The 2026 letter replaces the February 2024 circular. Existing providers should review and revise their systems and controls to meet the latest standards. Unlike 2024, it sets no six-month deadline for notifying the HKMA and confirming compliance [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2; S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2].
- For client VAs, the annex's key controls are generally required. For other digital assets the bank may take a risk-based approach, but tokens on public permissionless chains call for extra caution [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 chapeau].
- The 98% cold-storage rule for client VAs has not changed [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8; S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 6].
- **Compensation changed.** The 2024 annex asked for insurance or compensation covering 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot and other storage [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. The 2026 annex instead expects the bank to be liable for losses from incidents attributable to it, backed by adequate financial resources, which may include insurance [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]. The 50%/100% figure remains in the SFC's rule for VATPs, as an SFC-approved compensation arrangement [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22].
- **Key location.** Seeds and private keys should still be generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong. There is one new exception. With HKMA consent, a bank may appoint an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer to hold that issuer's own coins, with keys in Hong Kong or another location the HKMA accepts [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14(iii)].
- **New operating controls.** These include cold-wallet whitelists with a system check on every transfer, and detection of intrusions into vaults, signing devices and code repositories [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]. The annex also sets out due diligence on hardware security module (HSM) vendors, no smart contracts in cold wallets on public chains, segregation of duties over wallet code, dedicated approval devices, air-gapped integrity checks, and prevention of blind signing [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (c), (f), (g), (i)]. Security monitoring should run 24/7 [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23].
- **AML section removed.** The 2024 annex had a separate anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) paragraph [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23]. The 2026 annex has none. The cover letter reminds AIs to also comply with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2].
- Transfers to third parties are now allowed to support payment services or carry out client settlement instructions, if effective controls are in place. The definition of client now also covers clients of SFC-licensed VATPs [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m) and fn 9].
- For staking from custody, the annex points to the HKMA's April 2025 staking guidance and asks banks to have due regard to the SFC's staking terms for VATPs [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26]. Under the HKMA guidance, the bank should keep control of everything needed to unstake, disclose staking risks such as slashing, and discuss its plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B, Implementation p.3]. VATPs may not use third-party custody for staked assets [S:50bf95ba3143, para 6].
- The SFC's August 2025 circular took effect immediately. It says the overseas incidents it describes point to potential weaknesses whatever custody solution is used, whether HSM, multi-party computation (MPC) or multi-signature. Its standards will also be core expectations for future VA custodians [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2, Way forward p.7].
- Under the custodian regime conclusions, the licence will cover custodians that safekeep private keys or similar instruments that enable VAs to be transferred. Custodians of tokenised securities that do not hold VAs fall outside the regime [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6–8, 12]. The SFC will set baseline requirements of HK$10 million paid-up share capital and HK$3 million liquid capital; banks remain subject to HKMA capital requirements [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41–42]. No deeming arrangement is planned for existing providers, but banks already assessed by the HKMA and already providing VA custody get an expedited process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].
- The consultation paper proposed that the SFC license and register VA custodians and set standards, with the HKMA as frontline regulator supervising banks' VA custodian activities [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]. The conclusions list banks and subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks that safekeep keys among those needing a licence or registration [S:f41a543388bc, para 35(b)].

**Key-management terms, as the documents use them**

- **Hot and cold wallets.** In a hot wallet the private keys sit online, which makes them easier to attack. In a cold wallet they are kept offline [S:8a016a912528, fn 19].
- **HSM (hardware security module).** A secure, tamper-resistant device for generating and storing seeds and keys. Banks should check that the vendor keeps up patching and re-certification [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)].
- **Key sharding and multi-signature.** With sharding, a key is split among several authorised staff so that no one person holds all of it, and a set number of shard-holders must act together to sign [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)]. With multi-signature, several keys are involved; for stablecoin issuers, those keys should be stored in separate, isolated environments [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(iv)].
- **MPC (multi-party computation).** Another way of distributing signing power. For licensing, a key question is whether the provider can move client assets on its own [S:f41a543388bc, para 11].
- **Blind signing.** Approving a transaction without reviewing its contents. Banks should show signers every detail in human-readable form before they sign [S:562c0f8addce, fn 6; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)].
- **Whitelisting.** Deposits and withdrawals go only to whitelisted addresses shown to belong to the client, for example by message signing or a micropayment test, subject to the third-party transfer exception. Changes to a cold-wallet whitelist are tightly controlled [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(m)].
- **Air-gapped devices.** Devices kept off networks, stored in a cold vault and changed only with physical access. Banks should use them for integrity checks on critical transaction data [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(g)]. Stablecoin issuers should generate, and use, their most significant keys in air-gapped environments [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(ii), (vii)].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Keep client assets and wallet addresses segregated from the bank's own. Do not lend, pledge or encumber client assets except for settlement or fees owed, with prior explicit written consent, or where the law requires it [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6].
- Be liable for losses attributable to the bank, and hold adequate financial resources to cover them [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- Disclose the custody arrangements to clients fully and fairly. This covers rights on insolvency, segregation, insurance or compensation, commingling, and how forks and airdrops are handled [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20].

**Controls & monitoring**
- Keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage, and keep seeds, keys and backups in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8].
- Train transaction signers in depth and run drills of the business continuity plan [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 3, 5].
- Reconcile each client's holdings regularly against both on-chain and off-chain records, and escalate discrepancies to senior management [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21].
- Monitor security 24/7, covering dependencies such as vendors, blockchain protocols, encryption algorithms and common libraries [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss plans with the HKMA before launching custody, and show that the bank meets the standards [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- Discuss staking plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, Implementation, p.3].
- Provide custody records to the HKMA promptly when asked [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 22].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- As a general principle, delegate VA custody only to another AI (or a local AI's subsidiary), to an SFC-licensed VATP, or, with HKMA consent, to a licensed stablecoin issuer for the coins it issues [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14].
- Before onboarding a custodian, include independent code reviews and understand how it develops and releases software. After onboarding, regularly evaluate its security controls, require timely incident reporting, and test its disaster recovery [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15].
- For a VATP counterparty, the SFC's own custody standards are in the VATP Guidelines, for example paras 10.6–10.8 (cold storage, whitelisted addresses, key management) and 10.22 (compensation arrangement), as elaborated in 25EC44 [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22; S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2]. The HKMA annex cites the VATP Guidelines for reference on delegation [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 10].

## Talking points

**To the CCO (chief compliance officer)**
- The 2026 annex replaced the 2024 one. An existing service should review and revise its systems and controls to meet the latest standards; the letter sets no transition period [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- The custody annex no longer has an AML/CFT section, but the cover letter reminds AIs to comply with all applicable requirements, and the HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline sets the standards AIs should meet [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2; S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3].

**To business heads**
- With HKMA consent, a bank may now delegate custody of a licensed stablecoin to its issuer [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14(iii)].
- Transfers to third parties for payments and settlement are now allowed if effective controls are in place [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m)].

**To the CEO**
- The fixed insurance percentages have been replaced by bank liability plus adequate financial resources; the annex sets no fixed percentage [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8].
- The FSTB and SFC conclusions propose a statutory custodian licence with no deeming arrangement. Banks already assessed by the HKMA get an expedited process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].

**To Risk / CRO (chief risk officer)**
- The SFC says the weaknesses shown by overseas incidents can arise whichever custody solution is used, whether HSM, MPC or multi-signature [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].
- The HKMA lists slashing, lock-up and validator inactivity among staking risks to disclose. The bank should keep control of the means to unstake [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B].

## Common mix-ups

- "Banks need 50%/100% insurance cover." That was the 2024 rule for banks and remains the rule for VATPs, not for banks from 2026 [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8; S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- "The February 2024 annex is still current." It was superseded on 27 May 2026 [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- "Keys may never leave Hong Kong." The general rule stands, but an issuer delegated to hold its own coins may keep keys elsewhere if the HKMA accepts the location [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 7].
- "The custodian regime covers tokenised securities." It does not, because the statutory VA definition excludes securities [S:f41a543388bc, para 12].
- "MPC or HSM equals compliance." The SFC says weaknesses can exist whichever custody solution is used [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].

## Read these first

1. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets by Authorized Institutions (Annex)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 6–13 (segregation and safeguarding), 14–19 (delegation) and 23–26 (monitoring and staking). These are the HKMA's current custody standards for AIs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
2. **Circular to licensed virtual asset trading platform operators on custody of virtual assets (25EC44)**, SFC, 15 Aug 2025. Read Sections I–VI (paras 1–28) and the good-practice boxes. The SFC says these standards will be core expectations for future VA custodians. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC44
3. **Consultation Conclusions: Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Custodian Services**, FSTB + SFC, December 2025. Read paras 5–16 (scope), 25–26 (individuals), 35 (who needs a licence) and 41–52 (capital and transition). https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/Custodian_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf

## Open items

- The custodian bill had a stated aim of introduction into LegCo in 2026 [S:f41a543388bc, Introduction, p.3]. The documents reviewed do not show it has been introduced, and no commencement date is set [S:f41a543388bc, para 49].
- The SFC said it would consult, in a separate paper issued the same day, on whether VA management service providers must use SFC-regulated custodians for private funds' VAs [S:f41a543388bc, para 32].
- The 2024 annex referred to AML/CFT guidance from the HKMA on custodial activities of digital assets [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23]. The documents reviewed do not show whether such separate guidance exists.

## Related modules

[C1](#m-C1) (Selling, dealing and advising), [C2](#m-C2) (VA funds and ETFs), [C4](#m-C4) (Stablecoins), plus the cyber/technology risk and AML/CFT modules.

title: Stablecoins
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain Hong Kong's stablecoin law, what a licensed issuer must do, and every role a bank can play: issuer, offeror, dealer or adviser, custodian, or holder on its own balance sheet.

## In 60 seconds

The Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) took effect on 1 August 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] In the course of business, issuing a fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) in Hong Kong, or issuing one referenced to the Hong Kong dollar in or outside Hong Kong, needs a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) licence. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] Licensed issuers must back each coin type in full with segregated reserves and must not pay interest; the HKMA expects valid redemptions at par, normally within one business day, and strict private-key controls. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1, 3.3.3, 6.5.7]; [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1] Only permitted offerors, including authorized institutions (AIs), may offer these coins, and only coins issued by licensed issuers may be offered to retail investors. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]; [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1] The first two licences took effect on 10 April 2026; the HKMA says that if more are granted, the overall number will remain very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, Follow-up work section, para 3] On 27 May 2026 the HKMA (for registered institutions, RIs) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) relaxed how virtual asset (VA) conduct requirements apply to these Relevant Stablecoins, while keeping advance-notification duties. [S:a0bd48559762, pp.1-2, 9]; [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] For its own holdings, a bank classifies stablecoins under the capital module CRP-1 and treats them under the liquidity module LM-1. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2]; [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026. Abbreviations: FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau; LegCo = Legislative Council; AML/CFT = anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism; LC = SFC-licensed corporation; VATP = SFC-licensed virtual asset trading platform.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Discussion Paper on Crypto-assets and Stablecoins | HKMA | 12 Jan 2022 | Superseded | Public; AIs | [S:2b888e600616, Section 6] |
| Consultation paper on stablecoin issuer regime | FSTB + HKMA | 27 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Public | [S:167649d1bc28, para 3] |
| Consultation conclusions | FSTB + HKMA | 17 Jul 2024 | Superseded | Public | [S:54aa01e7396e, para 12.1] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox | HKMA | 12 Mar 2024 | Superseded | Would-be issuers | [S:28616d929735, para 1] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | LegCo / HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Issuers; offerors incl. AIs | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Supervisory Guideline and AML/CFT Guideline for licensed issuers | HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed issuers, incl. an AI licensee | [S:6c3f349e4f90, para 1] |
| Explanatory Note on Licensing | HKMA | Jul 2025 | In force | Applicants | [S:fe4baea8dd7d, Chapter 3] |
| Stablecoin Review Tribunal (current membership) | FSTB | 1 Nov 2025 | In force | Parties aggrieved by HKMA decisions | [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3] |
| Register of licensed issuers | HKMA | 10 Apr 2026 | In force | Public; counterparties | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] |
| Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) CRP-1 and LM-1 (V.5) cryptoasset treatment | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026; 19 Dec 2025 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.1]; [S:69600121310a, Annex 3] |
| RI circular and AI letter on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs; all AIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| SFC circular 26EC26 | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VATPs; LCs | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1, opening paragraph] |

## Key facts

- History: HKMA discussion paper (January 2022; its January 2023 conclusions reported 58 submissions); FSTB-HKMA consultation (27 Dec 2023 to 29 Feb 2024); consultation conclusions (17 Jul 2024, 108 submissions). [S:c72a4b732293, para 1.4]; [S:167649d1bc28, para 3]; [S:54aa01e7396e, paras 1-2]
- The Bill was gazetted on 6 December 2024, passed on 21 May 2025, and the Ordinance commenced on 1 August 2025. [S:a9a82f2b38ce, para 1]; [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- A licence is required to issue, in the course of business, an FRS in Hong Kong, or an FRS referenced to the Hong Kong dollar in or outside Hong Kong. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]
- Only FRS count as specified stablecoins for now; bank deposits, stored value facility (SVF) float and securities are outside the definition. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 2.1.2, 2.2.1-2.2.2]
- Permitted offerors are: a licensee, an AI, an SVF licensee, an SFC-licensed VATP, or an LC licensed for SFC Type 1 (dealing in securities). [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]
- Permitted offerors may offer licensed-issuer coins to anyone; other specified stablecoins only to professional investors; VA over-the-counter shops are not permitted offerors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), paras 1-2]
- Only adverts for licensed FRS issuance may be published; the rule applied during the six-month non-contravention period too. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 3]
- An overseas-incorporated AI may apply without a local subsidiary. The financial-resources and business-activity criteria do not apply to AI applicants. No HKMA consent is needed for someone to become an AI applicant's controller, chief executive or director. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 6, 8]
- A licensee must keep paid-up capital of at least HK$25 million; an AI licensee is exempt and follows the Banking Ordinance instead. [S:240be6833157, paras 5.1.1, 5.1.3]
- Reserves must be worth at least the par value of coins in circulation at all times and must be kept segregated; the HKMA expects an effective trust arrangement and a qualified custodian. Reserve deposits should have a term of no more than three months, and debt securities a residual maturity of no more than one year. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.5.1-2.5.4]
- Valid redemptions must be honoured at par without unreasonable fees or unduly burdensome conditions; unless otherwise approved, they should be processed within one business day. [S:240be6833157, paras 3.3.3, 3.3.5]
- Licensees may not pay interest or yield tied to holding a coin. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1]
- Private-key controls should cover the whole key lifecycle. Significant keys should be generated offline in an air-gapped setting. Keys should be stored in Hong Kong or another HKMA-accepted location. [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7 and items (ii), (iv)]
- The issuer AML/CFT Guideline uses a HK$8,000 threshold for customer due diligence on occasional transactions and for the fuller data set on stablecoin transfers. Unless a licensee shows the HKMA that its risk controls are effective, each holder's identity should be verified (by the licensee, a supervised institution or a reliable third party). [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 4.4, 6.5-6.6, 5.11]
- A pre-existing issuer wishing to be licensed had to apply by 31 October 2025; one that did was not barred from carrying on its activity until 31 January 2026, unless it had entered a closing-down period. [S:6c3f349e4f90, Explanatory Note on Transitional Provisions, paras 3.3, 4.1]
- The HKMA received 36 first-batch applications and licensed Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02), effective 10 April 2026. [S:193316443831, paras 1, 3]; [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- In June 2026 the Government said that, if more licences are granted, the overall number will remain very limited; it expected the first regulated stablecoin launch as early as mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)-(2)]
- Complaints: the issuer should acknowledge within 7 calendar days and give a full or interim response within 30 calendar days (a full response generally within 60). The HKMA may take complaints the issuer has not properly addressed, but generally does not order compensation. [S:240be6833157, para 8.4.3]; [S:d3e75db3ddb3, Lodging Complaint with the HKMA section]
- The current Stablecoin Review Tribunal panel holds a three-year term running to 31 October 2028; a person aggrieved may refer a decision in writing within 30 days after the HKMA makes it, or within a period the Tribunal permits. [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3]
- On 28 April 2026 the HKMA warned that tokens using the tickers HKDAP or HSBC were not issued by, or associated with, the licensed issuers, and that both licensees had confirmed they had not yet issued any regulated stablecoins. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] As an offeror, offer only licensed-issuer coins to retail; offer other specified stablecoins only to professional investors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 4]
- [ ] For Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice and portfolio management, follow the RI standards and the Appendix A1 and A2 terms; the HKMA expects this of all AIs. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- [ ] Disclose material information on each Relevant Stablecoin's stabilisation and redemption arrangements when dealing or advising. [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5 and para (10), p.7]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] To use the Relevant-Stablecoin-only relief, clearly demarcate those client accounts and deal no other VAs for those clients; dealing other VAs for a client brings back the full VA requirements, including the knowledge assessment. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
- [ ] Keep advice grounded in the client's use case, not commission rebates. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- [ ] Classify stablecoin holdings under CRP-1 (Group 1b only if classification conditions 1-4 are met; full redeemability means redemption within five calendar days). [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2, 2.3.2]
- [ ] For liquidity (category 1 institutions), treat held stablecoins as non-HQLA (high-quality liquid assets) debt securities: generally a 0% inflow under the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) and an 85% required stable funding factor under the net stable funding ratio (NSFR). An issuing bank must apply a 100% LCR outflow if the coin is redeemable within the LCR period, with lower rates possible where the backing assets are HQLA-eligible. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] RIs: notify the HKMA and SFC before any Relevant Stablecoin activity or material change. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- [ ] All AIs: discuss Relevant Stablecoin services with the HKMA first. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Notify the HKMA on acquiring a new type of cryptoasset, and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Check a claimed issuer against the HKMA Register of licensees; the HKMA points the public to the Register to verify licensees. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]
- [ ] An AI may delegate custody of stablecoins to a licensed issuer only for that issuer's own coins, and only if the issuer has the HKMA's consent to provide that custody. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14 and fn 7]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- Banks are permitted offerors; only licensed-issuer coins may be offered to retail investors. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]; [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]
- RIs notify the HKMA and SFC before Relevant Stablecoin activity; other AIs discuss with the HKMA first. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]

**To business heads**
- Two issuers are licensed (effective 10 April 2026); the HKMA says any further licences would keep the overall number very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, Follow-up work section, para 3]
- Relevant-Stablecoin-only dealing is not limited to RIs registered for Type 1, and needs no VA knowledge assessment for clearly demarcated Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts; Appendix A1 conditions still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, paras (2), (3)(a)]

**To the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**
- An AI can apply to issue, and the financial-resources and business-activities minimum criteria do not apply to an AI applicant. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.2.1; fns 1, 8]
- In June 2026 the Government expected the first regulated stablecoin launch as early as mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)]

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- A held stablecoin is treated as a non-HQLA debt security for liquidity; an issuing bank must apply a 100% LCR outflow if the coin is redeemable within the LCR period (lower rates possible with HQLA-eligible backing). [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
- HKMA-licensed coins can be deemed to meet CRP-1's extra permissionless-chain measures, but Group 1 still needs conditions 1-4. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.6.3]

## Common mix-ups

- "A Relevant Stablecoin is an investment product." The HKMA letter says its guidance should not be read that way. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- "Sandbox firms are licensed." Sandbox admission was not a licence; the HKMA later said it is neither a precondition nor a guarantee. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, para 2]; [S:e0b249a7eb8c, Licensing regime section, para 5]
- "A licence means coins are live." Both licensees confirmed on 28 April 2026 they had not yet issued. [S:275e7319a841, para 3]
- "The SFC's 26EC26 governs our bank." It covers VATPs and LCs; for RIs it points to the HKMA RI circular. [S:19d52ade6849, p.1, opening paragraph and fn 2]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]
- "Only Hong Kong firms are caught." A business that issues Hong Kong dollar-referenced coins needs a licence wherever the issue takes place. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]
- "The HKMA will get my client compensated." It generally does not order issuers to pay compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, Lodging Complaint with the HKMA section]

## Read these first

1. **Explanatory Note on Licensing of Stablecoin Issuers**, HKMA, Jul 2025. Read Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 (especially 3.2-3.5 and 3.13). Scope, offerors, criteria and AI carve-outs. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Explanatory_Notes_on_Licensing_of_Stablecoin_Issuers_eng.pdf
2. **Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers**, HKMA, 1 Aug 2025. Read sections 2-3, 6.5 and 8.4. Reserves, redemption, keys and complaints. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Guideline_on_supervision_of_licensed_stablecoin_issuers_eng.pdf
3. **VA-related activities in relation to Relevant Stablecoins (RI circular)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read all nine pages. How a bank deals, advises and distributes. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- No document reviewed for this guide has a official confirmation that either licensee had launched a regulated stablecoin by 25 Sep 2026.
- The HKMA has told applicants it has no definitive inclination on the direction and timing of further licensing. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]
- On 3 June 2026 the HKMA clarified (loosened) CRP-1 para 2.6.4 for tokenised traditional assets, not stablecoins, effective immediately, and said the CRP-1 wording will be updated in due course; No document reviewed for this guide has a updated CRP-1 text. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed VA trading platforms and their use in settling tokenised money market funds; no detailed measures are in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- Statutory text of Cap. 656 on e-Legislation is not in the documents reviewed for this guide; section numbers here come from HKMA documents.

## Related modules

[B2](#m-B2), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3)

title: Tokenisation: tokenised products, deposits and bonds
md:
For a bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After reading, you can explain which tokenisation rules bind the bank today, which HKMA projects the bank may join, and what is still only a stated plan.

## In 60 seconds

Tokenisation records a claim on an asset (such as a bond, fund unit, gold or a bank deposit) on a distributed ledger (DLT) or similar technology. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 2, 5; S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1] Hong Kong regulators apply the rules for the underlying product to its tokenised form, and add expectations on technology, ownership and custody risks. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-3; S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 7-8] For authorized institutions (AIs, i.e. banks), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) set these expectations in a February 2024 circular. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has circulars on tokenised securities and on tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. They reach licensed corporations (LCs) and banks acting as registered institutions (RIs). [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8; S:58ea8520974d, para 18] On infrastructure, the HKMA's Project Ensemble entered a real-value pilot, EnsembleTX, in November 2025. Seven named Tokenised Deposit Banks are to offer tokenised deposits and settle interbank transactions through it. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3; S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A] The Government has made three tokenised bond issues (2023, 2024 and 2025), and the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) priced its first digital bond in June 2026. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5; S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1] The 2026 Policy Address lists next steps: settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) and round-the-clock (24/7) operation for EnsembleTX, a digital asset platform at CMU OmniClear (operator of the Central Moneymarkets Unit, CMU), tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills, and a second-phase legal review with the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB). These are stated targets, not rules. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii)-(iv), 37(i), 50]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products (circular) | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | All AIs (incl. customers' placing of tokenised deposits) | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1] |
| Circular on intermediaries engaging in tokenised securities-related activities | SFC | 2 Nov 2023 | In force | LCs; RIs (notify HKMA too) | [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8] |
| Circular on tokenisation of SFC-authorised investment products (original) | SFC | 2 Nov 2023 | Superseded | Product providers, distributors | [S:d422282a262d, p.1 banner] |
| Circular on tokenisation of SFC-authorised investment products (revised) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | Product providers; LC/RI distributors | [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5-6, 8, 18] |
| Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | SFC-licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs), product providers, LC/RI distributors and connecting brokers | [S:a64e364fd912, paras 1, 13, 15-16, 27] |
| Project Ensemble launch (Mar 2024), Architecture Community (May 2024), Sandbox (Aug 2024) | HKMA | 7 Mar-28 Aug 2024 | Historical (Sandbox phase followed by EnsembleTX pilot) | Architecture Community members; Sandbox participants | [S:5a9cad53f2be, paras 1-2]; [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1, 3]; [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1-2]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] |
| EnsembleTX (real-value pilot) | HKMA | 13 Nov 2025 | Pilot (to operate throughout 2026) | 7 Tokenised Deposit Banks + 13 other industry pioneers | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3]; [S:d193f12a5f78, Annexes A-B] |
| CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation under EnsembleTX | HKMA (via Policy Address) | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target (around end-2026) | EnsembleTX participants | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| Government tokenised green bond (HK$800m, 365-day) | HKSAR Govt / HKMA | 16 Feb 2023 | Issued (one-off) | Investors, syndicate banks | [S:a0841967c871, para 1 and summary terms] |
| Government digital green bonds: ~HK$6bn (Feb 2024); ~HK$10bn with e-HKD/e-CNY settlement option for HKD and RMB tranches (Nov 2025) | HKSAR Govt / HKMA | 7 Feb 2024; priced 10 Nov 2025 | Issued (Feb 2024); priced (Nov 2025) | Investors | [S:4290ec1111e3, para 1 and key features]; [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 1-5] |
| HKMC inaugural digital bond (~HK$12bn) | HKMC | priced 10 Jun 2026; issue date 15 Jun 2026 | Issued (one-off) | Investors; 16 arranging financial institutions | [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 8; Annex] |
| Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS) | HKMA | 28 Nov 2024 | Open for applications (initial 3-year period) | Issuers of digital bonds (applications also by lead arrangers or DLT platform providers) | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 and fn 1; s.5] |
| Tokenised Bond Expert Group (TBEG) | HKMA | 5 Jun 2026 | Exploratory | Industry members | [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-3] |
| FSTB/HKMA DLT fixed-income review, phase 1 (incl. Companies Registry FAQs on DLT debenture registers) | FSTB + HKMA | 29 Jun 2026 | Conclusions published | Bond issuers, arrangers | [S:279f10054c6e, 'Issuing clarifications' section] |
| Phase 2 legal review (e-execution, possession/transfer of tokenised instruments) | FSTB + HKMA (TBEG involved) | H2 2026 | Stated target | Market | [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase']; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |
| CMU OmniClear digital asset platform | CMU OmniClear (via Policy Address) | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target (this year) | Digital bond issuance and settlement | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)] |
| Tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests | HKMA (via Policy Address) | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target (by year-end) | Banks | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] |

Note: 'Issued' on bond rows marks a completed one-off transaction, not a rule.

## Key facts

- The HKMA circular covers tokenised real-world assets (e.g. non-SFO structured investment products, spot precious metal). It excludes stablecoins and products covered by the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO). AIs should also meet its standards when customers place tokenised deposits. It expects due diligence on issuers and vendors, plain-language risk disclosure, HKMA custody standards where relevant, and prior discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1; Sections A-D; p.6]
- General principle: the existing selling and investor-protection rules for a product also apply to its tokenised form. AIs should still assess whether tokenisation changes the product's nature (e.g. fractional interests becoming a collective investment scheme). [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.2]
- The SFC treats tokenised securities as traditional securities in a tokenisation wrapper. Whether one is a complex product is judged on the underlying security, provided the technology risks are effectively mitigated. The SFC no longer imposes the 2019 mandatory professional-investor (PI)-only restriction, though public-offering rules still apply. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 7, 21, 24, 26-27]
- RIs planning digital-securities activity should notify the SFC and the HKMA in advance. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8]
- For tokenised SFC-authorised investment products, primary dealing is allowed. Product providers remain responsible for the tokenisation arrangement, and should not use public-permissionless chains without extra controls such as a permissioned token. [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 10, 13]
- Since 20 April 2026, the SFC allows secondary trading of these products on SFC-licensed VATPs, subject to fair-pricing and other controls. RIs taking part should also notify the HKMA. [S:a64e364fd912, paras 4, 8, 12, 27 and fn 13]
- Project Ensemble initially focused on tokenised deposits (digital representations of commercial bank deposits). [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] EnsembleTX moved Ensemble from proof-of-concept to real-value transactions. Its initial focus is tokenised money market fund and treasury use cases, with interbank settlement first running on HKD Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS). [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3]
- The HKMA lists seven Tokenised Deposit Banks for EnsembleTX: Bank of China (Hong Kong), China Construction Bank (Asia), Fubon Bank (Hong Kong), Fusion Bank, Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong), The Bank of East Asia and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]
- Under the HKMA liquidity guideline LM-1 (V.5, Dec 2025), a category 1 bank may treat tokenised deposits it issues (a legally binding claim on the bank, redeemable at par in fiat) as deposits or unsecured funding for the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR). They get no stable-deposit or stable-funding treatment, whether held by retail or small business customers. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4]
- The DBGS covers 50% of eligible expenses: up to HK$1.25m (Half Grant) or HK$2.5m (Full Grant), for at most two issuances per issuer and its associates. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1]
- For the Full Grant, the DLT platform provider must not be an associate of the issuer. The issue must also be at least HK$1bn, go to five or more investors not associated with the issuer or platform provider, and be listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) or an SFC-licensed VATP. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3]
- The FSTB/HKMA phase-1 review found that Hong Kong's legal and regulatory framework is already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. The Companies Registry's FAQs affirm that a DLT register of debenture holders can be deemed to meet Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) record-keeping rules. [S:279f10054c6e, opening para and 'Issuing clarifications' section]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Apply existing product-selling rules to tokenised products, plus the tokenisation-specific expectations. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-3]
- Apply the circular's standards when customers place tokenised deposits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1]
- As a distributor of tokenised SFC-authorised products, the bank should be a regulated intermediary (e.g. an RI) and follow existing onboarding and suitability rules. [S:58ea8520974d, para 18]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Carry out due diligence before offering and at intervals after, on the product, its issuer and third-party vendors, including key management and audits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- Give customers plain-language tokenisation risk disclosures. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section B, pp.4-5]
- If providing custody of tokenised products, meet the HKMA's digital asset custody standards. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section D, p.6]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss tokenised-product plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Implementation', p.6]
- As an RI, notify the SFC and the HKMA before digital-securities activity. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8]
- As an RI in secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products, also notify the HKMA. [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]
- Optional: use the HKMA's Supervisory Incubator for DLT to reaffirm risk controls before a full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Assess the issuer's and tokenisation platform's track record, key-management and ownership-record controls. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- For tokenised bonds, consider the product's legal status and whether settlement is final. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.4; Section B, p.5] For example, the HKMA states that CMU settlement of the Government digital green bonds has finality protected by statute. [S:4290ec1111e3, fn 2]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Existing product rules apply to tokenised products, plus HKMA expectations on due diligence and disclosure, and advance discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-6]
- As an RI, the bank should tell both the SFC and the HKMA before digital-securities work, and notify the HKMA too before secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, fn 8]; [S:a64e364fd912, fn 13]

**To business heads**
- EnsembleTX is to operate throughout 2026 with real-value tokenised-deposit settlement. The HKMA invites stakeholders with real-value tokenised-deposit use cases to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3 and CE remarks]
- The DBGS Full Grant (up to HK$2.5m per issue) is not available if the DLT platform provider is an associate of the issuer. A Half Grant of up to HK$1.25m may still apply. [S:5a0563de8142, ss.1, 3]

**To the CEO**
- The Government has made three tokenised bond issues; the latest raised about HK$10bn. The HKMC priced about HK$12bn in June 2026. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:ac6cd085a325, para 1]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]
- The Policy Address targets CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation for EnsembleTX around end-2026, and a CMU OmniClear digital asset platform this year. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(iv), 50]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Tokenised deposits the bank issues cannot get stable-deposit treatment in the LCR. If the bank cannot always identify holders, it must treat them as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4]
- The HKMA's non-binding DLT risk considerations (April 2024) cover network choice, smart contracts, legal risks such as settlement finality, third parties, interoperability, cybersecurity and private-key security. [S:1884530ff235, Introduction and items 2-8]

## Common mix-ups

- 'Tokenised securities are automatically complex or professional-investor-only.' They are not. The SFC looks through to the underlying security and no longer imposes a mandatory PI-only restriction. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 24, 26]
- 'The HKMA tokenised-products circular covers stablecoins.' It expressly does not. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1]
- 'Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products is still barred.' That was the 2023 position. The revised April 2026 framework allows it on SFC-licensed VATPs, subject to conditions. [S:d422282a262d, paras 6-7]; [S:58ea8520974d, para 6]
- 'EnsembleTX is not an official name.' The HKMA uses it in its own November 2025 announcement and annex. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1]; [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]

## Read these first

1. **Sale and distribution of tokenised products**, HKMA, 20 Feb 2024. Read the whole circular (6 pages), especially Sections A-D and 'Implementation'. It is the bank's baseline for tokenised products. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240220-10-EN/20240220-10-EN.pdf
2. **Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products**, SFC, 20 Apr 2026. Read paras 8-27 and footnotes 13-14 for connecting-broker, distributor and RI duties. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC23
3. **EnsembleTX announcement and Annexes A/B**, HKMA, 13 Nov 2025. Read the full release and both annexes to see pilot scope and participants. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251113-3/ and https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251113e3a1.pdf

## Open items

- No dedicated HKMA framework for issuing tokenised deposits was found among the sources reviewed. The current anchors are the February 2024 circular, the LM-1 liquidity treatment and the Supervisory Incubator, which has tokenised deposits as a core focus. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1; S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4; S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2]
- The HKMA said it would soon publish an Ensemble Use Case Report and an Ensemble Taxonomy. Neither was found among the sources reviewed as of 25 Sep 2026. [S:3e5e256be485, Project Ensemble passage and 'The Road Ahead' section]
- Phase-2 legal review findings (e-execution, possession/transfer of tokenised instruments) are not yet published. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase']
