title: Financing, shared order books and client withdrawals
md:
For a bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets) whose Registered Institution (RI) offers, or plans to offer, virtual asset (VA) dealing. After reading, you can explain what the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) changed in February 2026, how the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) applied it to banks in May 2026, and which controls the regulators expect.

## In 60 seconds

Under the omnibus-account terms and conditions, licensed corporations (LCs) and RIs dealing in VAs for clients could not provide financing for clients to buy VAs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background, p.1] On 11 February 2026 the SFC let VA brokers that already do securities margin financing extend VA financing to their securities margin clients. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 3, 5] If a broker relies on VA collateral, the SFC expects it to be limited to bitcoin and ether, with a haircut of 60% or more. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 7] On 27 May 2026 the HKMA let RIs offer VA financing if they observe similar standards. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2] It also allowed stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers as collateral, and said loans secured only by VA must be treated as clean loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)] The same circulars let brokers and RIs trade for clients on a VA trading platform's (VATP's) shared order book, which pools orders with affiliated platforms abroad. Retail clients get access only after a clear risk explanation and an express election. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 15-17]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6] They also set anti-fraud standards where clients can withdraw VAs. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 18-20] The SFC circular is addressed to LCs; the HKMA applies the standards to RIs. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.2, 6]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circular on shared liquidity by VATPs (25EC56) + Shared Order Book terms and conditions | SFC | 3 Nov 2025 | In force | SFC-licensed VATPs (prior written SFC approval needed) | [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 3, 26]; [S:fda3c03f239d, para 3] |
| Circular on VA brokers: financing, shared order book, client VA withdrawals (26EC5) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | LCs dealing in VA via omnibus accounts | [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1] |
| Circular permitting VATPs to accept affiliated market makers (26EC6) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | SFC-licensed VATPs | [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] |
| Guidance on offering of financing for VA dealing, shared order book and client VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All RIs; financing for RIs providing VA dealing | [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.1-2] |
| VA-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins (with revised terms and conditions, Appendices A1 and A2) | HKMA (formulated jointly with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:553c7d718bec, landing page]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| SFC consultation on capital requirements for VA activities incl. VA financing | SFC | not dated | Stated target ('in due course') | LCs | [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14] |

## Key facts

- Before the SFC's 11 February 2026 circular, neither LCs nor RIs could give clients financial accommodation to acquire VA under the omnibus-account terms and conditions. [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background, p.1]
- The revised terms of 27 May 2026 keep the ban, with an exception. An LC or RI may give such financing only if it engages in securities margin financing and holds a Type 1 licence or registration carrying these terms. [S:31b4f67e0233, Part I para 4.3, p.10]
- The SFC framed VA financing as a first step under Pillar P of its ASPIRe roadmap. It is limited to VA brokers that already provide securities margin financing. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 3-5]
- The HKMA allows RIs providing VA dealing to offer VA financing if they observe standards similar to the SFC's. It sets out the standards for RIs as items (1)-(9). [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', p.2]
- Eligible borrowers are limited to the RI's securities margin financing clients. The RI is not expected to raise a client's credit limit just because VA financing is available. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3), p.2]
- Where an RI counts a client's VA holdings toward financial capability, its assessment should cover seven risk factors. These include price-gap risk, digital-asset sector concentration and correlation with equities under stress. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3)(a)-(g), p.3]
- If an RI chooses to rely on VA collateral, only bitcoin, ether and stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers should count as eligible collateral ('Relevant Stablecoins'), with a prudent haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), pp.3-4]
- The haircut for bitcoin and ether should be 60% or more. The HKMA may revise the haircut on prior notice. No numeric haircut is set for Relevant Stablecoins. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5, p.4]
- The RI is generally expected to value VA collateral at prices on the VATP where the client's orders execute. For Relevant Stablecoins it may instead use the licensed issuer's prices. RIs should keep a contingency plan for VATP outages. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6) and footnote 6, p.4]
- VA financing counts as part of the margin loan. Concentration controls should cover VA collateral, and the RI should not repledge or reuse VA collateral except to enforce it on client default. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(a)-(c), pp.4-5]
- If the loan exceeds collateral value, or a client has an outstanding margin call and a poor record of meeting them, the RI should suspend advances, stop VA purchases on margin and review the client's credit and trading limits. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8), p.5]
- Because the Banking (Capital) Rules do not recognise VA collateral, loans secured solely by VA must be treated as clean loans to the client. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]
- Until the SFC revises capital requirements, the Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules (FRR) apply a 100% haircut to VA collateral held by LCs. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14]
- Tokenised products fall outside the HKMA circular, because the financing ban does not apply to acquiring them. On their sale and distribution, RIs should refer to HKMA guidance such as its 20 February 2024 tokenised-products circular. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4, p.2]
- A shared order book lets an SFC-licensed VATP combine its order book with those of affiliated platforms abroad. The overseas platform should operate in a Financial Action Task Force (FATF) or FATF-style regional body member jurisdiction with substantially aligned regulation. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 7]
- A shared order book should accept only fully pre-funded orders, with delivery-versus-payment settlement at the centre. The VATP is required to hold, on trust in Hong Kong, a client-compensation reserve no smaller than the Unsettled Trade Limit. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 10, 13, 15, 17]
- RIs doing agency trading on a shared order book, or offering retail access, should follow SFC 26EC5 paras 15-17. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6] Before trading, a broker should assess conflicts, settlement, default handling, reserve funds and insurance, and client recourse. Retail access needs a prominently communicated risk explanation and an express election. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 16-17]
- Where client VAs stay in custody at the VATP, a broker's withdrawal function adds cyber and operational risk: a compromised broker system could let an impostor send fraudulent withdrawal instructions. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 19]
- SFC 26EC5 paras 18-20 also apply to RIs that permit client VA withdrawals, on top of HKMA requirements such as e-banking and technology risk management. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6] These expect robust authentication, continuous monitoring with suspension inside and outside office hours, and working with VATPs on withdrawal limits. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20]
- 26EC6 lets a VATP accept an affiliated market maker, subject to conditions. These include functional independence, client-order priority at the same price, post-trade identification and disclosure. The VATP must notify the SFC first with an independent firm's report. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9-10]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Offer VA financing only to securities margin financing clients, based on financial capability and posted collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2), p.2]
- Treat loans secured solely by VA as clean loans for capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]
- Do not repledge, reuse or encumber VA collateral except to enforce it on client default. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(c), p.5]

**Controls & monitoring**
- If relying on VA collateral, document VA risk-assessment methods in the margin lending policy, and monitor vulnerable VA exposures on an ongoing basis. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(a), p.4]
- If relying on VA collateral, keep the ability to monitor its volatility in real time and act promptly. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(b), p.4]
- Set prudent margin-call and stop-advance triggers, and act on them. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8), p.5]
- For withdrawals: monitor continuously, with escalation and suspension also outside office hours. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(b)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- The HKMA circular sets no separate notification step. For new digital-asset activity, the HKMA's existing expectation is that banks discuss plans with it before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body para 5, p.2]
- Contacts for queries are named in the circular, by topic. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Before shared order book trading, assess the operators' conflicts of interest, the settlement mechanism, failure and default processes, reserve fund and insurance, and client recourse. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 16]
- Work with the partner VATP as needed on withdrawal limits and blocking suspicious withdrawals. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(c)]
- Keep an outage contingency plan for the VATP used to value collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6), p.4]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- The HKMA's 27 May 2026 circular lets our RI offer VA margin financing if we observe standards similar to the SFC's. If we rely on VA collateral, it should be limited to bitcoin, ether and stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(4), pp.2-4]
- Withdrawal and shared-order-book standards come from SFC 26EC5 paras 15-20, applied to RIs by the HKMA. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]

**To business heads**
- Only securities margin financing clients qualify, and limits are not expected to rise just because VA financing exists. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3), p.2]
- Retail clients can use a shared order book only after a prominent explanation of the overseas risks and an express election. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 17]

**To the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**
- The SFC calls this a first step to bring margin trading into VA, aimed at liquidity in a risk-controlled setting. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 3]
- The Banking (Capital) Rules give VA collateral no recognition, so loans secured solely by VA are treated as clean loans. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- Bitcoin and ether collateral should get a haircut of 60% or more. For stablecoins the HKMA asks only for a prudent haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), footnote 5, pp.3-4]
- The HKMA notes that VAs have a limited track record in major systemic shocks, and even the most traded VA has seen large falls within a day and over several days. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3), closing paragraph, p.3]

## Common mix-ups

- 'The SFC circular binds banks directly.' It is addressed to LCs. Banks, as RIs, are brought in by the HKMA's 27 May 2026 circular. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2]
- 'Bank collateral rules are identical to the SFC's.' The HKMA adds Relevant Stablecoins as eligible collateral and uses Banking (Capital) Rules clean-loan treatment rather than the FRR 100% haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)]; [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 7, 14]
- 'The financing ban covered tokenised products.' The HKMA says the prohibition does not apply to acquiring tokenised products. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4, p.2]
- 'A shared order book can link to any overseas exchange.' As a first step it is limited to intra-group platforms. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 3]

## Read these first

1. **Guidance on Offering of Financing for VA Dealing, Shared Order Book, and Client VA Withdrawals**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read all six pages, especially items (1)-(9) and page 6. It is the text addressed to RIs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-1-EN/20260527-1-EN.pdf
2. **Circular on licensed corporations providing VA dealing services (26EC5)**, SFC, 11 Feb 2026. Read paras 4-11, which the HKMA restates, and paras 15-20, which it applies to RIs. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC5
3. **Circular on shared liquidity by VATPs (25EC56)**, SFC, 3 Nov 2025. Read paras 3-18 and 25-26 to understand the partner platform's settlement risk. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC56

## Open items

- Paragraph-number difference: SFC 26EC5 cites the financing ban as para 4.4 of the omnibus terms and conditions. The HKMA cites para 4.3 'as renumbered on 30 September 2025', and the revised terms of 27 May 2026 also number it 4.3. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 2]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1 footnote 3]; [S:31b4f67e0233, Part I para 4.3, p.10]
- Date discrepancy: the HKMA's footnote 4 dates the joint circular 23 December 2023. The SFC's version, and the HKMA's own stablecoin circular of 27 May 2026, give 22 December 2023. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4]; [S:8a016a912528, p.1]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]
- The SFC capital-requirements consultation for VA activities has no published date. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14]
- Of the revised terms and conditions (Appendices A1 and A2 to the HKMA's 27 May 2026 stablecoin circular), only para 4.3 of Appendix A1 was reviewed for this module. [S:553c7d718bec, landing page]
- No numeric haircut is specified for Relevant Stablecoin collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5, p.4]

## Related modules

title: VATP counterparties and the SFC platform regime
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain how the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licenses virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs), what the rulebook requires of them, and how to use that rulebook when a platform is your bank's partner, customer or counterparty.

## In 60 seconds

Since 1 June 2023, any platform running a virtual asset (VA) exchange in Hong Kong, or actively marketing one to Hong Kong investors, needs an SFC licence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] Before that, the SFC only had an opt-in route for platforms that offered at least one security token. [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32] The SFC's VATP Guidelines are the platforms' rulebook: token admission, retail gates, 98% cold storage, compensation cover and key prohibitions. They apply to platform operators, not banks. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 1.2, 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22] But the SFC and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) require intermediaries, including banks, to partner only with SFC-licensed platforms for VA dealing, so the Guidelines become your due-diligence benchmark. [S:8a016a912528, para 17] Since November 2025 the SFC has widened what licensed platforms may do, and in May 2026 the HKMA told registered institutions (RIs) which related SFC standards it expects them to follow. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 3; S:f009f1a6d615, para 3; S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.1, 6]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Position paper: opt-in regulation of VATPs | SFC | 6 Nov 2019 | Superseded | Platforms listing a security token | [S:024089b01825, paras 32, 82] |
| AMLO VATP licensing regime | AMLO (statute); SFC licenses | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | All VATPs in or marketing to Hong Kong | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] |
| Guidelines for VATP Operators | SFC | Jun 2023 | In force | Licensed VATPs; bank uses as benchmark | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2] |
| Lists of VATPs (licensed, applicants, removed, closing-down) | SFC | live; update 29 May 2026 | In force | Public; counterparty checks | [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table] |
| Inspection findings on deemed applicants (circular 25EC3) | SFC | 16 Jan 2025 | In force | Platform Operators and applicants | [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] |
| Custody circular for licensed VATPs | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed VATPs | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7] |
| Expansion of products and services; shared liquidity | SFC | 3 Nov 2025 | In force | Licensed VATPs | [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5]; [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26] |
| Affiliated market makers (AFMM) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | Licensed VATPs | [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] |
| High-level framework for perpetual contracts | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | Issued (initial framework; SFC invites proposals) | Licensed VATPs; professional investors only | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors' and 'Way forward' sections] |
| Guidance to RIs on VA financing, shared order book, VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs (banks) | [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.1-2, 6] |
| Phishing-resistant authentication circular | SFC | 9 Jul 2026 | Issued; phishing-resistant authentication due by 8 Jul 2027 | Internet brokers and SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers (VASPs) | [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 1, 21] |

## Key facts

- In 2018 the SFC chose to observe selected platforms in its Regulatory Sandbox before deciding whether to license any. [S:e7f89463ceae, Section II]
- Under the 2019 position paper, the SFC could only license a centralised Hong Kong platform that traded at least one security token; platforms trading only non-security tokens sat outside its powers. [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32]
- The SFC granted the first VATP licence in December 2020, for Type 1 and Type 7 regulated activities, limited to professional investors. [S:60682e9fd7fa, main text and Note 1]
- The AMLO regime started on 1 June 2023 and requires every platform running a VA exchange in Hong Kong, or actively marketing one to Hong Kong investors, to be SFC-licensed. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
- Pre-existing platforms could keep operating until 31 May 2024; those that applied by 29 February 2024 and met the deeming conditions could be deemed licensed from 1 June 2024. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 12]
- Deemed status is not a licence. In the SFC's words, such platforms are "NOT formally licensed by the SFC", and they should not onboard new retail clients before proving their controls. [S:c787f990209d, 'Reminder for investors' and 'Reminder for deemed-to-be-licensed VATP applicants']
- The SFC publishes lists of licensed platforms, applicants, removed applicants and closing-down platforms; at 29 May 2026 the licensed list showed 13 platforms, and listing does not guarantee creditworthiness. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table and note]
- Token admission: a platform should run a token admission and review committee and do documented due diligence before listing any token. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.6]
- Retail access: a token offered to retail clients should be highly liquid; at a minimum, it should be included in at least two acceptable indices from at least two different index providers. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.7-7.8]
- Custody: a platform and its Associated Entity should keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage, and hold an SFC-approved compensation arrangement covering 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% of those in hot and other storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
- Prohibitions: the June 2023 Guidelines say platforms should not, outside narrow exceptions, finance client VA purchases, deal in VA futures or derivatives, provide algorithmic trading services to clients, use client VAs to generate returns, trade for their own account, or make markets on a proprietary basis. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.23-7.26, 13.2-13.4] Two later SFC documents open limited routes: the February 2026 perpetuals framework invites platforms to propose perpetual contracts, and the February 2026 circular lets an affiliated company make markets on a platform under conditions. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Background'; S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 4, 7]
- After inspecting all deemed applicants on cybersecurity, client-asset safeguarding and know-your-client (KYC) processes, the SFC told every Platform Operator to review its systems and fix gaps at once. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]
- In November 2025 the SFC dropped the 12-month track record for tokens offered to professional investors, and for stablecoins from licensed issuers offered to retail; it still applies to other retail tokens. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5]
- Shared liquidity: licensed platforms may, with prior written SFC approval, share an order book with affiliated overseas platforms, starting with intra-group liquidity only. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 26]
- Since February 2026 a platform may let an affiliated market maker trade on it, after notifying the SFC and filing an independent firm's report; client orders keep priority at the same price. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9]
- The SFC's perpetual-contracts framework says these products should be offered only to professional investors, and margin collateral should be fiat, or stablecoins or tokenised deposits regulated by the HKMA. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets' and 'Margin arrangements' sections]
- The SFC named JPEX as unregulated, said it was placed on the SFC Alert List in July 2022, said it never applied for a licence, and referred the matter to the Police on suspicion of fraud. [S:c8dcca119dab, main text, paras 3, 5-6]
- The SFC expects SFC-licensed VASPs to adopt phishing-resistant login and device binding by 8 July 2027; it does not treat one-time passwords (OTPs) as phishing-resistant. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] If the bank offers VA dealing, partner only with SFC-licensed platforms, via an omnibus account or by introducing clients. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- [ ] Offer VA dealing only to clients of the bank's Type 1 (dealing in securities) business. [S:8a016a912528, para 18]
- [ ] As an RI, the HKMA expects you to follow the SFC's shared-order-book guidance for brokers when trading for clients on such a book or giving retail clients access. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]
- [ ] As an RI permitting client VA withdrawals, apply the SFC's withdrawal safeguards on top of HKMA e-banking and technology rules. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Re-check a platform's status on the live SFC lists before onboarding and at review; the lists can lag between updates. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 1]; [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section Note 1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Give the SFC, and the HKMA where relevant, advance notice before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] When banking a VASP, run a risk-based anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) assessment; depending on the relationship, the HKMA says extra correspondent-style checks may be needed, such as understanding its business, its licensing status and its AML/CFT controls. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4]
- [ ] For a VASP located outside Hong Kong, find out whether the account serves its own use or its clients; if clients, apply the correspondent-banking measures. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]
- [ ] Benchmark a partner platform against the VATP Guidelines: token committee, retail index test, 98% cold storage, compensation cover. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22]
- [ ] Ask whether the platform has fixed the gaps in the SFC's inspection findings. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1 and Appendix 2]

## Talking points

**To the chief compliance officer (CCO)**
- The VATP Guidelines bind platforms, not the bank. For us they are a due-diligence yardstick, because our VA dealing must run through SFC-licensed platforms. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2]; [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- On our own AML duties for VASP customers, we follow the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline, including correspondent-style checks on overseas VASPs. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]

**To business heads**
- Shared order books and affiliated market makers are now allowed for platforms, with SFC approval or notice; the SFC's perpetuals framework says those should go to professional investors only. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26]; [S:84b3c1a0cee1, para 9]; [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
- If we give clients access to a platform's shared order book, the HKMA expects us to follow the SFC's broker guidance. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong moved from an opt-in, professional-only model (2019-2020) to mandatory licensing for all platforms from June 2023. [S:024089b01825, para 32]; [S:60682e9fd7fa, Note 1]; [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
- The SFC’s licensed list showed 13 platforms at 29 May 2026. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]

**To Risk / chief risk officer (CRO)**
- The Guidelines say licensed platforms should hold 98% of client VAs cold and carry compensation cover of 50% of cold-stored and 100% of hot-stored client VAs. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
- The SFC's inspections of deemed applicants covered cybersecurity, client assets and KYC; it said platforms should act at once to fix gaps. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]

## Common mix-ups

- "Deemed licensed means vetted." No: the SFC said in 2023 that it had not vetted the fitness and properness of deemed platforms, and that they may never get a licence. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 4]
- "The 50%/100% compensation rule applies to our custody." It is a VATP rule; the HKMA's May 2026 custody guidance for banks instead expects the bank to be liable for losses attributable to it and to hold adequate financial resources. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- "Text-message (SMS) OTP is enough." The SFC does not consider OTP phishing-resistant for login or device binding. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 7]

## Read these first

1. **Guidelines for Virtual Asset Trading Platform Operators** — SFC, June 2023. Read paras 7.1-7.8 (token admission, retail test), 7.24-7.26, 10.6, 10.11, 10.22 and 13.2-13.4. This is your benchmark for any platform counterparty. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/Guidelines-for-Virtual-Asset-Trading-Platform-Operators/Guidelines-for-Virtual-Asset-Trading-Platform-Operators.pdf
2. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities** — SFC and HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 17-18 and 31. Explains why bank VA dealing must go through licensed platforms. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66
3. **Lists of virtual asset trading platforms** — SFC, live page (29 May 2026 update reviewed). Read the licensed table and the applicant-list notes. The SFC's own register of platform status. https://www.sfc.hk/en/Welcome-to-the-Fintech-Contact-Point/Virtual-assets/Virtual-asset-trading-platforms-operators/Lists-of-virtual-asset-trading-platforms

## Open items

- The perpetuals framework is an initial approach that the SFC says may be refined; no approvals of specific perpetual products appear in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Way forward']
- The SFC press release is dated 16 Dec 2020, while the licensed list shows a licence date of 15/12/2020 for the earliest platform; the documents reviewed do not explain the one-day gap. [S:60682e9fd7fa, dateline]; [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]
- The VATP list is live; counts here are a 29 May 2026 snapshot.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [B1](#m-B1), [C1](#m-C1), [C2](#m-C2), [C5](#m-C5), [C6](#m-C6), [D1](#m-D1)

title: Capital and prudential treatment of cryptoassets
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain how Hong Kong turned the Basel cryptoasset standard into binding capital, liquidity and exposure rules, how a cryptoasset gets classified, and what the bank must notify to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

## In 60 seconds

The global bank standard setter, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), published a standard on banks' cryptoasset exposures in December 2022 and amended it in July 2024. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.1] The HKMA consulted on it (CP 24.01, February 2024), sent draft rules to the banking associations in January 2025, and the government gazetted three sets of amendment rules in July 2025. [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 1-2; S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, p.1; S:277820235891, para 1] The rules, plus a new guidance module CRP-1 and nine revised Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) modules, took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, closing para; S:30b686db29f9, pp.1-2] Every cryptoasset a bank is exposed to is sorted into Group 1a (tokenised traditional assets), 1b (stablecoins with an effective stabilisation mechanism), 2a (Group 2 assets that meet hedging criteria, so limited hedging is recognised) or 2b (everything else, at a 1,250% risk weight). [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.2-1.3.3, 2.1.8; S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), pp.214-215] New cryptoasset types must be notified to the HKMA and sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] In June 2026 the HKMA clarified that one Group 1 condition for tokenised traditional assets on permissionless chains can also be met another way. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BCBS standard (Dec 2022) and amendments (Jul 2024) | BCBS, implemented by HKMA | Dec 2022; Jul 2024 | Implemented in Hong Kong rules | All authorized institutions (AIs) from 1 Jan 2026 | [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.1-1.1.2] |
| CP 24.01 Cryptoasset Exposures | HKMA | 7 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs | [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 2, 11] |
| Soft consultation on draft rule amendments | HKMA | 13 Jan 2025 | Closed (comments were due 20 Feb 2025; rules since gazetted) | AIs, via the Hong Kong Association of Banks and The DTC Association | [S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, pp.1-2] |
| Banking (Capital), (Disclosure) and (Exposure Limits) (Amendment) Rules 2025 | Government; tabled at the Legislative Council (LegCo) | Gazetted 11 Jul 2025 | In force (from 1 Jan 2026) | All AIs | [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para] |
| SPM CRP-1 plus nine revised modules and a code of practice | HKMA | Finalised 27 Nov 2025; eight revised modules and the code gazetted 19 Dec 2025 | In force (from 1 Jan 2026) | All AIs | [S:30b686db29f9, pp.1-2]; [S:54e0a69bd91f, pp.1-2] |
| CRP-1 para 2.6.4 clarification | HKMA | 3 Jun 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] |
| Guidance to registered institutions (RIs) on virtual asset (VA) financing (clean-loan treatment) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5] |
| Proposed Banking (Capital) Rules amendments | HKMA | 30 Apr 2026 | Consultation closed 1 Jun 2026; no final rules seen | AIs | [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page]; [S:1e9b351e81e7, p.1] |

## Key facts

- CP 24.01 proposed bringing the December 2022 Basel standard into Hong Kong rules no earlier than 1 July 2025, with comments due by 6 May 2024. [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 2, 4, 11]
- In January 2025 the HKMA sent draft rule amendments to the industry, asking for comments by 20 February 2025 and aiming for a 1 January 2026 start to match Basel. [S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, p.1]
- The three amendment rules were gazetted on 11 July 2025, were due to be tabled at LegCo on 16 July 2025, and took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para]
- The HKMA finalised CRP-1 and revisions to nine other modules and a code of practice on 27 November 2025, all effective 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, pp.1-2]
- CRP-1 is guidance; the binding classification rules sit in Part 12 of the Banking (Capital) Rules (BCR), which prevails if the two differ. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- Group 1 status needs all four classification conditions: same rights and risks as the traditional asset (or an effective stabilisation mechanism); clearly defined, legally enforceable rights and settlement finality; network risks that are sufficiently mitigated and managed; and entities performing key functions that are regulated and supervised (or subject to suitable risk management standards). [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1]
- Group 1a is tokenised traditional assets and Group 1b is stablecoins with an effective stabilisation mechanism; anything else is Group 2. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2]
- A Group 2 asset reaches Group 2a only if it meets three hedging criteria, including average market capitalisation of at least HKD 78 billion and 100 or more real price observations. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 3.1.1]
- Group 2b exposures take a 1,250% risk weight, which is also meant to cover their market risk and their credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), pp.214-215]; [S:5d845665ba83, para 4.3.2]
- Before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset, a bank must notify the HKMA and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's own classification assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Exposures held before 1 January 2026 must sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.2]
- If the HKMA disagrees with a bank's classification, it will override it. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6]
- On permissionless chains, stablecoins issued under the HKMA's licensing regime can be deemed to meet the extra measures; other stablecoins must be under a regime the HKMA considers comparable to the Stablecoins Ordinance. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.6.3]
- The June 2026 letter says the approval condition for tokenised traditional assets on permissionless chains can also be met where a financial market regulator supervises the tokenisation business. The letter took effect immediately. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- CA-G-1 section 8.7 says Group 1a banking-book exposures generally follow the underlying asset's rules, while Group 1b needs separate capital for the reference asset and the redeemer. [S:5d0c13e09312, paras 8.7.1-8.7.2]
- Group 2 exposure limit: a global or domestic systemically important bank (G-SIB or D-SIB) faces an add-on when its Group 2 exposure exceeds 1% of Tier 1 capital, and a different, heavier treatment above 2%. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)]; [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]
- Under LM-1 Annex 3, a category 1 institution may count a cryptoasset as high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) only if it is a Group 1a token of an HQLA-eligible asset class and meets the HQLA requirements; an issuer of a stablecoin redeemable within the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) period must generally apply a 100% outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 paras 1, 7]
- Market risk: any cryptoasset exposure removes the de-minimis exemption, the internal models approach cannot be used for instruments referencing Group 2 cryptoassets, and Group 2a position risk is 100% of the net position. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80, paras 6.1.9, 6.2.8]
- CR-G-8 values crypto exposures under new Division 5A of the Banking (Exposure Limits) Rules; exposures not linked to a counterparty's credit or default risk are disregarded when measuring large exposures to a counterparty or group. [S:0cd3c1a74e5e, paras 2.8.8-2.8.9 and footnote 13]
- CR-L-5 treats a token carrying the economics of equity as share capital for the major-acquisitions consent rules. [S:13365a31e794, footnote 1]
- CA-G-5 says the HKMA may respond to crypto-related weaknesses with capital add-ons, provisions, limits or other measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Classify every cryptoasset exposure under BCR Part 12 and CRP-1, and keep assessing it on an ongoing basis. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 2.1.1]
- [ ] Move an asset agreed as Group 1a, 1b or 2a to Group 2b at once if it stops meeting its conditions or criteria. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.3]
- [ ] As an RI, treat loans secured only by VA collateral as clean loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep policies, staff and IT able to assess cryptoasset risk, and document the evidence for each classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]
- [ ] For stablecoins, keep a monitoring framework that checks the stabilisation mechanism works as intended. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.2.4]
- [ ] If the bank is a G-SIB or D-SIB, track the Group 2 exposure ratio against the 1% and 2% thresholds used in disclosure. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the HKMA before acquiring any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Give the HKMA classification evidence on request. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For Group 1 assets, check that every entity redeeming, transferring, storing or settling the asset (or managing its reserves) is regulated and supervised or meets suitable risk standards, and discloses a governance framework. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The capital rules are law from 1 January 2026; CRP-1 is guidance, and the BCR wins if they differ. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]
- New cryptoasset types need HKMA notification before purchase. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

**To business heads**
- Until the HKMA agrees a classification, a new cryptoasset sits in Group 2b at a 1,250% risk weight. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]; [S:5d845665ba83, para 4.3.2]
- Stablecoins under the HKMA licensing regime can be deemed to meet the permissionless-chain measures, but the four classification conditions still apply. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.6.3]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong's rules started on 1 January 2026, matching the Basel timeline. [S:277820235891, closing para]
- The HKMA can override our classifications and add capital or limits if it sees weaknesses. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6]; [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Any crypto exposure ends our market-risk de-minimis exemption. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80]
- For a category 1 institution, a stablecoin it holds is generally treated as non-HQLA, with a 0% LCR inflow and an 85% required stable funding factor under the net stable funding ratio (NSFR). [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 7]

## Common mix-ups

- "The June 2026 CRP-1 letter tightened the rules." It clarified that the para 2.6.4 approval condition can also be met where a financial market regulator supervises the tokenisation business. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- "Internal models are only barred for Group 2a." MR-1 bars them for all instruments referencing Group 2 cryptoassets. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, para 6.1.9]
- "The 1%/2% Group 2 limit applies to every bank." The HKMA's return instructions have all Hong Kong-incorporated AIs report the ratio, but only G-SIBs and D-SIBs face the add-on. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)]; [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
- "Legacy holdings keep their old treatment." They sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.2]
- "CBDCs are cryptoassets." They sit outside the standard and are generally treated like the central bank's fiat. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.2.3 and footnote 4]

## Read these first

1. **SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets** — HKMA, V.1 effective 1 Jan 2026. Read paras 1.1.4, 1.4, 2.1, 2.6 and 3.1.1. Sets out how each cryptoasset is grouped. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251125-15-EN/CRP-1.pdf
2. **SPM CRP-1: update on cryptoassets classification conditions** — HKMA, 3 Jun 2026. Read p.1. Changes how para 2.6.4 is met. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260603-1-EN/20260603-1-EN.pdf
3. **Cryptoassets standard: SPM modules, code of practice, disclosure templates and returns** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025. Read pp.1-4. Lists every module changed and the reporting transition. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251127-1-EN/20251127-1-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The April 2026 BCR proposals (for example, removing cryptoassets from the Part 6 "cash item" definition, and rules on hedging counterparty credit risk for netting sets with Group 2b cryptoasset derivatives) closed for comment on 1 June 2026; no final rules are in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:1e9b351e81e7, Items 19, 45]; [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page]
- The June 2026 letter says CRP-1's wording will reflect the clarification in due course; The documents reviewed hold no updated CRP-1 text. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- The gazetted Banking (Capital) Rules Part 12 text itself is not in the documents reviewed for this guide; section references come from HKMA modules and templates.
- The copies reviewed of the HKMA's December 2022 BCBS relay letter and the July/August 2025 gazettal letters are catalogue pages only.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [C7](#m-C7), [D2](#m-D2), [D3](#m-D3), [D4](#m-D4)

title: Regulatory reporting and disclosure
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can say which Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) returns and public (Pillar 3) disclosures now carry cryptoasset data, from when they applied, and who could use the six-month transition.

## In 60 seconds

The amendment rules that bring the Basel cryptoasset standard into Hong Kong law took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, paras 1, 6] For reporting, the HKMA issued new or revised templates and instructions for seven returns: MA(BS)1E (liquidity), MA(BS)1F (compliance certificate), MA(BS)3 (capital, with a new Part IIIf for extra crypto risk-weighted amounts), MA(BS)3A (capital for market and credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk), MA(BS)26 (stable funding), MA(BS)27 (leverage) and MA(BS)28 (large exposures). [S:30b686db29f9, p.3; S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1] Authorized institutions (AIs) with no cryptoasset exposure on 1 January 2026 ('Transition AIs') could keep using the old templates for four of these returns until 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] For disclosure, a new Part XII adds one narrative table (CAEA) and three templates (CAE1-CAE3) to the Pillar 3 package. These apply to AIs with cryptoasset exposures, and CAE1 needs extra rows for material individual holdings. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218] Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module CA-D-1 gives the HKMA's guidance on applying the Banking (Disclosure) Rules (BDR). [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Banking (Disclosure) (Amendment) Rules 2025 | Government / LegCo | Gazetted 11 Jul 2025; in effect 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:277820235891, paras 1, 2, 6] |
| Consultation on return templates | HKMA | 13 Jun 2025 (closed 11 Jul 2025) | Closed; finalised 27 Nov 2025 | AIs | [S:64b1dc490633, landing page, Issue Date and Consultation Status]; [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] |
| Consultation on revised completion instructions | HKMA | 4 Sep 2025 (closed 3 Oct 2025) | Closed; finalised 27 Nov 2025 | AIs | [S:fc9efbf504f8, landing page, Issue Date and Consultation Status]; [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] |
| Final returns package and transition for Transition AIs | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 | In force | All AIs; Transition AIs to 30 Jun 2026 | [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4] |
| Standard disclosure templates, new Part XII (CAEA, CAE1-CAE3) | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 | In force | AIs with cryptoasset exposures | [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-219]; [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] |
| SPM CA-D-1 (V.5) | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:e10295e5fe20, para 12.2.4] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA listed seven returns with new templates or instructions: MA(BS)1E, MA(BS)1F(a)/(b), MA(BS)3, MA(BS)3A, MA(BS)26, MA(BS)27 and MA(BS)28. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, 'Banking returns' list (a)-(g)]
- The HKMA said the final templates would not differ materially from the consultation versions, apart from textual and formatting changes and changes agreed with the industry. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- A Transition AI is one with no cryptoasset exposure on 1 January 2026; it could keep filing MA(BS)26, MA(BS)1E, MA(BS)3 and MA(BS)3A on the old templates until 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- Even Transition AIs were expected to use the revised instructions for MA(BS)3 Part II and Part I paragraph 6 from 1 January 2026, for miscellaneous changes unrelated to crypto. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4]
- A bank with crypto exposure, or a Transition AI that later acquired some, could agree a temporary alternative arrangement with the HKMA for positions from 31 January to 30 June 2026 if its systems were not ready. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]
- The points below come from the September 2025 consultation versions of the completion instructions. The final versions went to AIs for download in December 2025, and the HKMA said they would not differ materially. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- MA(BS)3 Part IIIf is new; the instructions say every Hong Kong-incorporated AI should complete it to work out additional risk-weighted amounts for cryptoassets. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1]
- Part IIIf covers: an infrastructure add-on for banking-book Group 1 exposures set by HKMA written notice; redemption-related credit risk for trading-book Group 1b exposures and Group 2a stablecoins; each Group 2b cryptoasset; and the Group 2 exposure ratio (all Hong Kong-incorporated AIs) plus its add-on (global and domestic systemically important banks (G-SIBs and D-SIBs) only). [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
- The consultation version of the Part IIIf instructions carries a March 2026 version stamp (03/2026). [S:d1fbf6c0736a, header p.1]
- Parts IIIa and IIIb gain a separate Division A2 for cryptoasset exposures; both also ask for the top five Group 1 cryptoassets by risk-weighted amount. [S:2195417bfd31, para 4 and Section C.3, para 47]; [S:df1dbac9c51a, para 4 and Section C.3, para 60]
- Part IIIc (internal ratings-based approach) adds a memorandum form, IRB_CRYPTO, for banking-book Group 1 exposures. [S:4b2b2befa66f, Section C.6]
- MA(BS)1E is due no later than 14 days after each month-end; category 1 institutions report new memo items 1.7(a)-(b) on cryptoassets counted as high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) and on tokenised claims from customers or counterparties. [S:f4e64fda4011, paras 5, 13.14]
- In MA(BS)1E, tokenised deposits that meet the SPM LM-1 criteria may be treated like ordinary deposits, but they do not qualify for the 3% or 5% stable-deposit outflow rate. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]
- MA(BS)26 is quarterly, due within one month; category 1 institutions add items 3(a)-(b) on tokenised claims and cryptoassets for the net stable funding ratio (NSFR). [S:767a346fbcaa, paras 4, 14]
- MA(BS)27 includes cryptoassets in the leverage exposure measure at their financial-reporting value. [S:3955600d53f0, attached completion instructions, para 6.5, pp.10-11]
- MA(BS)28 is quarterly, due within one month of quarter-end; cryptoasset-related exposures not tied to a counterparty's credit or default risk need not be included when reporting exempted exposures. [S:527c897d3eed, paras 4, 12]
- Pillar 3: the revised disclosure package applies to any reporting period ending after 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- Table CAEA is annual and covers crypto activities, risks, and how the bank assessed each Group 1 classification condition, including public information used but not confidential or proprietary information. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA, pp.210-211]
- Template CAE1 (exposures and risk-weighted amounts by Group) and CAE2 (accounting classification) are semi-annual for Hong Kong-incorporated banks with crypto exposures. [S:9e8d84c87168, Templates CAE1 p.212, CAE2 p.216]
- CAE1 needs extra rows for each material stablecoin or unbacked cryptoasset; for Group 2 an exposure is material when the Group 2 ratio is at least 0.3% and the single asset exceeds 5% of total Group 2 exposure. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214]
- CAE1's narrative must state the market value of cryptoassets the bank holds in custody for clients, split by type. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]
- CAE3 (liquidity) is semi-annual and fixed-format, for category 1 institutions with crypto exposures, whether incorporated locally or overseas. [S:9e8d84c87168, Template CAE3, p.218]; [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, p.61-62]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] File the revised crypto items in MA(BS)1E, 3, 3A, 26, 27 and 28 on the stated schedules. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]; [S:f4e64fda4011, para 5]; [S:767a346fbcaa, para 4]; [S:527c897d3eed, para 4]
- [ ] If Hong Kong-incorporated, complete MA(BS)3 Part IIIf, including the Group 2 exposure ratio. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 1, 11]
- [ ] Publish Table CAEA and Templates CAE1-CAE3 as they apply to the bank. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, pp.61-62]; [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] In CAE1, use daily mean values over the period for the specified Group 2a columns (long, short) and Group 2b columns (total, long, short). [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (i), p.213]
- [ ] Run the 0.3% / 5% materiality test at each period end to decide which Group 2 assets need their own CAE1 row. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214]
- [ ] Refer to the HKMA's explanatory notes, alongside the BDR, when filling in each standard template and table. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] If systems are not ready for the revised returns, agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For each Group 1 asset, be ready to describe how the bank assessed the four classification conditions, including the public information used, as CAEA asks for this. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA point (f), p.211]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Crypto reporting started on 1 January 2026; the no-exposure transition window ended on 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- CA-D-1 is general guidance on the HKMA's approach; if it conflicts with the BDR, the BDR prevail. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

**To business heads**
- A Transition AI that acquired crypto exposure after 1 January 2026 was grouped with exposed banks: if its systems were not ready, it could agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4]
- The aggregate market value of cryptoassets held in custody for clients, split by type, goes into the public CAE1 narrative. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]

**To the CEO**
- If we have cryptoasset exposures, our public Pillar 3 report has a crypto section: an annual narrative plus semi-annual numbers. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, pp.61-62]
- Seven HKMA returns changed at once for the cryptoasset standard. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Every Hong Kong-incorporated AI reports its Group 2 exposure ratio in Part IIIf; only G-SIBs and D-SIBs report the add-on. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
- Tokenised deposits do not qualify for stable-deposit outflow rates in the liquidity return. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]

## Common mix-ups

- "No crypto, no reporting change." Transition AIs were still expected to apply revised MA(BS)3 instructions for non-crypto items from 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4]
- "The transition covered all seven returns." It covered only four: MA(BS)26, 1E, 3 and 3A. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- "Part IIIf redemption risk is a banking-book item." The instructions place Group 1b redemption-related credit risk on trading-book exposures (Banking (Capital) Rules (BCR) section 376). [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 5]; [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(a)]
- "Overseas-incorporated banks disclose nothing." CAEA (liquidity-risk activities) and CAE3 (if category 1) apply to them too. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA scope, p.210; CAE3 scope, p.218]
- "Every stablecoin needs its own row." Group 2 rows follow the 0.3% / 5% test; Group 1b follows general BDR materiality. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214-215]

## Read these first

1. **Cryptoassets standard: SPM modules, code of practice, disclosure templates and tables, and banking returns** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025. Read pp.3-4. The returns list and transition rules. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251127-1-EN/20251127-1-EN.pdf
2. **Standard Disclosure Templates and Tables (Annex 4), Part XII** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025. Read pp.210-219. The crypto Pillar 3 templates and their notes. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251027-8-EN/20251027-8-EN.pdf
3. **Completion Instructions, MA(BS)3 Part IIIf** — HKMA, consultation version stamped March 2026. Read paras 1-12. The new crypto capital add-on form. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250903-22-EN/20250903-22-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The documents reviewed hold the consultation versions of the completion instructions, not the December 2025 finals; the HKMA said there would be no material changes. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- The gazetted BDR amendment text is not in the documents reviewed for this guide; BDR section numbers (such as 16ZQH-16ZQK) come from the templates and CA-D-1. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII]; [S:e10295e5fe20, para 12.2.4]
- No HKMA statement in the documents reviewed for this guide says whether any bank used the temporary alternative reporting arrangement.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [D1](#m-D1), [D3](#m-D3), [D4](#m-D4)

title: AML/CFT for digital assets at a bank
md:
For the Head of Compliance (digital assets) at a Hong Kong bank: after this module you can say which anti-money laundering (AML) and countering the financing of terrorism (CFT) texts actually bind the bank for virtual-asset (VA) business, where the VA-specific hooks sit, and which Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and Financial Action Task Force (FATF) material is context or counterparty expectation only.

## In 60 seconds

The bank's AML rulebook for digital assets is the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) AML/CFT Guideline for Authorized Institutions (AIs), revised in May 2023 and effective 1 June 2023 — not the SFC's guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3; S:16fd7cfab136, Part III para 1] Its VA content is thin: a HK$8,000 trigger for customer due diligence (CDD) on one-off VA transfers for people with no business relationship with the bank, a footnote pointing to Schedule 2, section 13A of the AML Ordinance (AMLO), five-year record keeping, and correspondent-style checks on virtual asset service providers (VASPs) located outside Hong Kong. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1 fn 15, 8.4, 11.23] Other HKMA and SFC guidance describes the section 13A requirements as the travel rule. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.1–6.2; S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.1–12.11.2] The HKMA's January 2022 circular sets further expectations: watch customers' flows to and from VA platforms, risk-assess each VASP customer, and talk to the HKMA before launching VA products or services. [S:642680fa4467, pp.3–5] The SFC's AML guideline (with its Chapter 12 on VAs) applies to licensed corporations (LCs) and SFC-licensed VASPs; the bank's SFC-registered business (as a registered institution, RI) must have regard to it, and must comply with Chapter 12 when the RI handles client VA deposits or withdrawals. [S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2; S:7bfdad704174, fn 1; S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)] Recent SFC circulars describe live typologies — scam money layered through brokers and platforms, and misuse of simplified Electronic Direct Debit Authorisation (eDDA) deposits — and relay a March 2026 FATF report on stablecoins and unhosted wallets. [S:be46918f8aa2, paras 7–8; S:cfc4a0d9f1be, paras 1, 11; S:00c9fbd119bf, p.3]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AML/CFT Guideline (For AIs), revised May 2023 | HKMA | 25 May 2023 (effective 1 Jun 2023) | In force | All AIs, including RIs | [S:7bfdad704174, cover, para 1.3; S:16fd7cfab136, Part III para 1] |
| AMLO (Amendment) Bill 2022 — VASP licensing | Legislative Council (LegCo), relayed by HKMA | Passed 7 Dec 2022; banking-sector amendments in operation from 1 Jun 2023 | In force | VASPs; AIs via CDD changes | [S:b12bd88c7aee, pp.1–2; S:4bd22ccf481d, reply, opening paragraph] |
| Circular: managing VA and VASP risks of money laundering or terrorist financing (ML/TF) | HKMA | 16 Dec 2019 | In force (shown as current on the HKMA site; updated by the 2022 guidance) | AIs | [S:2b4123d71a07, landing page; S:642680fa4467, p.3 fn 4] |
| Circular: AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | AIs | [S:642680fa4467, pp.3–5] |
| SB-1 (supervision of RIs), AML cross-reference | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, para 4.16.1] |
| AML/CFT Guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VASPs (Chapter 12) | SFC | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | LCs, SFC-licensed VASPs; RIs have regard to it | [S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2; S:7bfdad704174, fn 1] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA activities, para 20(b) | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | LCs and RIs | [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)] |
| Supplemental joint circular, para 7(c) | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs and RIs | [S:b79266f3da51, para 7(c)] |
| AML/CFT Guideline for Licensed Stablecoin Issuers | HKMA | Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed stablecoin issuers | [S:4d98c6a80b4d, cover] |
| Circular on layering activities (25EC62) | SFC | 17 Nov 2025 | In force | LCs, SFC-licensed VASPs, associated entities | [S:be46918f8aa2, p.1, para 2] |
| FATF relay incl. stablecoins/unhosted wallets report (26EC13) | SFC | 13 Mar 2026 | In force | LCs, SFC-licensed VASPs, associated entities | [S:00c9fbd119bf, p.1; p.3 item (3)(c)] |
| Circular on simplified eDDA deposits (26EC51) | SFC | 20 Aug 2026 | In force | LCs, SFC-licensed VASPs, associated entities | [S:cfc4a0d9f1be, p.1, para 1] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA Guideline is the AML rulebook for every AI, including AIs registered with the SFC; the Guideline treats both must and should as signalling a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.3, 1.6]
- One-off VA transfers: an AI should complete CDD before carrying out an occasional VA transfer worth HK$8,000 or more, and should watch for linked smaller transfers that together reach that amount. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4]
- For VA transfers the Guideline refers readers to AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A (footnote 15); Chapter 10 on wire transfers does not mention VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1 fn 15; Chapter 10]
- The HKMA has stated that the AMLO does not stop AIs carrying out VA transfers for customers if section 13A requirements are met. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- Records for occasional VA transfers at or above HK$8,000 should be kept at least five years after the transaction; relationship records for the life of the relationship and at least five years after it ends. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]
- If the bank gives correspondent-like services to financial institutions (FIs) or VASPs located outside Hong Kong, it should apply the cross-border correspondent measures in paras 11.6 and 11.13 (where applicable); FIs as defined in the AMLO are carved out. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23, fn 78–79]
- For an overseas VASP customer the bank should establish whether the account is for the VASP's own use or for serving its clients, and could consider encouraging or requiring separate accounts for the two. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.24–11.25]
- RIs, and AIs that are associated entities of SFC licensees, are required to have regard to the SFC's AML Guideline, including Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 1 to para 1.3; S:8934af8cc884, para 4.16.1]
- The HKMA expects AIs to watch for customers who make frequent transfers to or from VA platforms, understand those flows, and file suspicious transaction reports (STRs) where grounds exist. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
- For VASP customers, risk assessments should tell individual VASPs apart; depending on the relationship, extra CDD may be needed, such as understanding the business model, checking licensing and whether overseas rules are comparable, and assessing the VASP's own AML controls. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- An AI planning VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA and get feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5]
- Intermediaries (LCs and RIs) that let clients deposit or withdraw VAs should comply with SFC Chapter 12 for those movements, and the same applies to VA-funded fund subscriptions and redemptions. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b); S:b79266f3da51, para 7(c)]
- SFC Chapter 12 requires the ordering firm to obtain, record and pass on originator and recipient details for VA transfers — the full set at HK$8,000 or more, a shorter set below that; for unhosted wallets it should collect similar details from its own customer. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5–12.11.10, 12.14.2]
- Licensed stablecoin issuers acting as ordering institutions must collect full originator and recipient details for transfers of HK$8,000 or more (fewer below); unless an issuer shows the HKMA its controls work, the HKMA expects every holder's identity to be verified. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.5–6.6, 5.11]
- The SFC, citing police intelligence, reports scam proceeds being layered through licensed firms, some converted to VAs and withdrawn to unhosted wallets. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 8]
- A Government reply to LegCo (21 Feb 2024) gave VA-related criminal cases of 1,397 (2021), 2,336 (2022) and 3,415 (2023), with sums involved of HK$824m, HK$1,704m and HK$4,398m. [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]
- An HKMA speaker noted that Hong Kong logged over 44,000 deception cases in 2024, a rise of close to 12% from the year before. [S:165d354a94bc, remarks on fraud and scams]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Complete CDD before any occasional VA transfer of HK$8,000 or more, and watch for linked transfers. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4–4.2.5]
- Meet AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A for VA transfers the bank carries out. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15; S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- Run an ML/TF risk assessment and put mitigants in place before launching any VA-related product, service or new technology. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10–2.11; S:642680fa4467, pp.2–3]
- Keep VA transfer and relationship records for the periods in para 8.4. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Monitor customers' VA-platform flows and look into their nature. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
- Keep transaction-monitoring parameters and thresholds documented, regularly reviewed and independently validated. [S:7bfdad704174, para 5.8]
- In the RI business, apply SFC Chapter 12 when handling client VA deposits and withdrawals. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5]
- For the RI: notify the SFC and HKMA when it intends to engage in VA activities (dealing, advisory, asset management) or to change them, including the type of clients served. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- File STRs with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) where suspicion is identified. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 5.10–5.12]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- For overseas VASPs receiving correspondent-like services: understand the business, check reputation and supervision, assess AML controls, get senior management approval. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23–11.24]
- Confirm with a VASP customer that its operations do not breach applicable laws in Hong Kong or elsewhere. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- Know that the SFC expects licensed firms to register client bank accounts used for deposits and withdrawals, and to whitelist client wallet addresses. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 20]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Our governing AML text for VAs is the HKMA AI Guideline; our RI business must have regard to SFC Chapter 12, and comply with it when handling client VA deposits or withdrawals. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3, fn 1; S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]
- For our own VA transfers the Guideline points to AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A, not the wire-transfer chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15]

**To business heads**
- Any VA product needs a documented ML/TF risk assessment and an HKMA conversation before launch. [S:7bfdad704174, para 2.11; S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- Giving correspondent-like services to an overseas VASP means correspondent-style due diligence and senior management approval. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23–11.24]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA has said the AMLO does not prohibit AIs from VA transfers for customers if section 13A requirements are met. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- A Government reply to LegCo put sums involved in VA-related crime at HK$4,398m in 2023, up from HK$824m in 2021. [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- SFC red flags for licensed firms include deposits and withdrawals with little or no trading, and a new eDDA setup followed by whitelisting a new wallet address. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 7; S:cfc4a0d9f1be, para 11]
- An SFC circular notes FATF published a focused report on stablecoin and unhosted-wallet risks on 3 March 2026. [S:00c9fbd119bf, p.3 item (3)(c)]

## Common mix-ups

- 'SFC Chapter 12 binds the bank.' It applies to LCs and SFC-licensed VASPs; the HKMA said AIs, including RIs, should continue to comply with its own Guideline, with RIs having regard to the SFC text. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.2; S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2]
- 'Chapter 10 of the HKMA Guideline is our crypto travel rule.' Chapter 10 covers wire transfers; the VA hook is footnote 15, pointing to s.13A. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15, Chapter 10]
- 'All VASP customers need correspondent-banking measures.' Para 11.23 targets VASPs located outside Hong Kong; for other VASP customers the HKMA expects a risk-based assessment, with extra CDD depending on the relationship. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23; S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- 'VASPs are automatically high-risk.' The HKMA asks banks to differentiate individual VASPs' risks; there is no single approach. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- 'The 2026 custody guidance removed AML duties.' The 2024 annex had its own AML paragraph and the 2026 text does not, but the AML Guideline still applies to all AIs. [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23; S:ce05e67bcdce, sections (A)–(H); S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3]

## Read these first

1. **Guideline on AML/CFT (For Authorized Institutions), revised May 2023** — HKMA, 25 May 2023. Read fn 1 (printed p.1), paras 2.10–2.11, 4.2.1–4.2.5 with fn 14–15, 8.4, 11.6, 11.23–11.25. Why: the bank's binding text. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20230525-4-EN/AML-2.pdf
2. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs** — HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3–5. Why: the HKMA's expectations on VA flows, VASP customers and pre-launch dialogue. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
3. **AML/CFT Guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VASPs, Chapter 12** — SFC, 1 Jun 2023. Read 12.1, 12.11, 12.13–12.14. Why: what the RI business must have regard to, and what counterparties must do. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/guideline-on-anti-money-laundering-and-counter-financing-of-terrorism-for-licensed-corporations/AML-Guideline-for-LCs-and-SFC-licensed-VASPs_Eng_1-Jun-2023.pdf

## Open items

- The HKMA circular of 27 April 2023 (cited in the 2023 consultation conclusions) is not in the documents reviewed for this guide; its content is unverified here. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- The text of AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A is not in the documents reviewed for this guide, so its detailed data fields for banks are not restated here.
- The HKMA said in May 2025 it was developing a supplementary AML/CFT guideline for digital-asset activities of AIs and stablecoin licensees and would consult later in 2025; no consultation or final version appears in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:0d6e6d0253ff, para 4.1]
- The HKMA's repository page still lists the 16 Dec 2019 circular as current. The AML guidance in the 28 Jan 2022 circular follows it, updated for the FATF guidance of October 2021. [S:2b4123d71a07, landing page; S:642680fa4467, p.3 fn 4]
- No official VA-crime statistics after 2023 were found in the documents reviewed for this guide; the FATF stablecoins/unhosted-wallets report itself is not in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- The SFC eDDA and layering circulars are addressed to LCs, SFC-licensed VASPs and associated entities; no matching HKMA circular for banks as payer banks was found in the documents reviewed for this guide.

## Related modules

B-series (HKMA supervision of VA activity), C-series (RI conduct and custody), [D4](#m-D4), [D5](#m-D5), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3).

title: Cyber, fraud and technology risk
md:
For the Head of Compliance (digital assets) at a Hong Kong bank: after this module you can separate the technology-risk expectations the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) sets for the bank from the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) rules for its platform and broker counterparties, name the dated SFC deadlines, and describe the scam patterns regulators have flagged.

## In 60 seconds

For a bank, the technology-risk texts for digital assets are HKMA ones: the April 2024 list of risk considerations for authorized institutions (AIs) using distributed ledger technology (DLT), and the custody standards, updated in May 2026 with detailed wallet and key-management controls. [S:1884530ff235, Annex; S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11] The SFC has a parallel, more prescriptive set for licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) and internet brokers: an August 2025 custody circular prompted by overseas platform incidents, a January 2025 circular on inspection findings, a June 2026 circular on cyberattacks enabled by artificial intelligence, and a July 2026 circular expecting firms to stop relying on one-time passwords (OTPs) when clients log in or bind devices, moving to phishing-resistant methods by 8 July 2027. [S:562c0f8addce, p.1; S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1; S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 1; S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)] Those SFC circulars are addressed to SFC-licensed firms, not to the bank, but they describe what the bank's VATP and broker counterparties are expected to have, and many controls in the HKMA's 2026 custody update use the same wording as the SFC's 2025 custody circular. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(c), (f), (i); S:562c0f8addce, paras 5, 14, 28] On fraud, the HKMA has warned the public about crypto firms calling themselves 'banks', tokens falsely linked to licensed stablecoin issuers, and entities falsely claiming to be part of its e-HKD Pilot Programme. [S:19c8611c621a, para 1; S:275e7319a841, para 2; S:5f67b02549b0, para 1]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:1884530ff235, Annex] |
| Updated custody expected standards (key management, wallet controls) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ce05e67bcdce, opening para; paras 10–11] |
| Inspection findings on deemed VATP applicants (25EC3) | SFC | 16 Jan 2025 | In force | VATPs | [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] |
| Cybersecurity webinar materials (25EC11) | SFC | 20 Feb 2025 | Superseded | Licensed corporations (LCs), licensed virtual asset service providers (VASPs), associated entities | [S:0fcb48929954, p.1] |
| Custody of virtual assets (25EC44) | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | VATPs | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7] |
| Cyberattacks enabled by artificial intelligence (26EC32) | SFC | 2 Jun 2026 | In force | LCs, VASPs, associated entities | [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 1] |
| Phishing-resistant authentication and surveillance (26EC35) | SFC | 9 Jul 2026 | Issued, effective 8 Jul 2027 (authentication deadline; other sections immediate or as soon as practicable) | Internet brokers, SFC-licensed VASPs | [S:724f4d9f786e, para 21] |
| Alert: crypto firms misusing 'bank' | HKMA | 15 Nov 2024 (updating 15 Sep 2023 alert) | In force | Public | [S:19c8611c621a, para 1; S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 1] |
| Alert: tokens using licensed issuers' names | HKMA | 28 Apr 2026 | In force | Public | [S:275e7319a841, para 2] |

Note: the SFC's own record ranks 25EC11 as historical webinar material; 'Superseded' is the closest chip. HKMA alerts are one-off public notices recorded as historical; 'In force' is shown only as the closest chip.

## Key facts

- The HKMA says an AI's board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks, and that the AI should update its technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT as needed. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- The HKMA expects banks to understand the types of DLT network and pick one suited to the application's risks; it sees permissionless networks as likely inappropriate for highly critical or sensitive functions unless adequate compensating controls exist. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2, 5]
- A bank acting as custodian would generally be expected to have more rigorous private-key procedures, covering secure generation, storage and backup, with measures such as limited access, cold storage and offsite backups. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 8]
- The May 2026 HKMA custody update includes system-based whitelists for cold-wallet transfers, no smart contracts in cold wallets on public blockchains, and measures to prevent 'blind signing'. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(c), 11(i)]
- Keys and seeds should be generated and stored in tamper-resistant devices such as hardware security modules (HSMs), and generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(b)]
- Where the assets in custody are virtual assets (VAs), a bank custodian should hold 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l), fn 8]
- Wallet code management needs strictly enforced segregation of duties, and administrator access should follow least privilege; the segregation line is the annex's only 'must'. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(f)]
- Custody security monitoring should run 24/7 including holidays and cover dependencies such as vendors, blockchain protocols and encryption algorithms. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24]
- The SFC's August 2025 custody circular took immediate effect for VATPs; it says overseas incidents showed potential critical weaknesses whatever custody solution was used, such as HSMs, multi-signature wallets or multi-party computation (MPC). [S:562c0f8addce, p.1; 'Way forward', p.7]
- SFC inspections of deemed VATP applicants found one hot wallet's keys kept partly outside Hong Kong, a cold wallet built as a multi-signature smart contract, outdated encryption algorithms, and errors in hot-wallet calculations under the 98/2 rule. [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 paras 6, 18, 22]
- The SFC's June 2026 circular reminds firms that senior managers, their Manager-in-Charge for information technology (MIC-IT) among them, bear ultimate responsibility for cybersecurity risk, and asks firms to review patching, access controls, detection, supply chain and incident response. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, paras 3, 9–15]
- HKCERT, Hong Kong's computer emergency response coordination centre, recorded 15,877 cybersecurity incidents in 2025, up from 12,536 in 2024, as cited by the SFC. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, fn 1]
- The SFC does not consider SMS or email OTPs phishing-resistant; internet brokers and VASPs are expected to adopt robust methods (examples include passkeys and bound devices) no later than 8 July 2027, and large internet brokers immediately. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7–8, 21(c)]
- If a firm lacks adequate measures to prevent, detect and halt large-scale unauthorised transactions through client accounts after hacking incidents, the SFC will hold it accountable for clients' losses. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 25]
- In February 2025 the SFC had only strongly urged licensed corporations to drop OTPs for login and device binding; the July 2026 circular goes further. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Note 4]
- Under the Banking Ordinance only AIs may take deposits, and anyone other than a bank using the word 'bank' in its business name without the Monetary Authority's written consent commits an offence (section 97). [S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 3, Notes 1–2]
- In April 2026 the HKMA warned that tokens with the tickers 'HKDAP' and 'HSBC' were not issued by or associated with licensed stablecoin issuers; both licensed issuers had confirmed they had not issued any regulated stablecoins. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3]
- An HKMA presentation of 25 September 2026 gives the sector's first Quantum Preparedness Index score as 2.3 out of 10, with an objective of full sectoral readiness by 2030. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Keep board and senior management ownership of DLT risk and update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- For custody: run a comprehensive risk assessment before launch, with board and senior management oversight before and during the activity. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
- For client VAs, meet the key-management controls in para 11 (HSMs, keys in Hong Kong, no smart contracts in cold wallets on public blockchains, anti-blind-signing, 98% cold storage). [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11, fn 8]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Use system controls and whitelists to stop unauthorised cold-wallet transfers, and verify each transaction systematically. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]
- Run 24/7 security monitoring, and test system changes thoroughly before deployment. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23]
- Build DLT-specific scenarios (cyberattacks, key loss or theft, forks) into continuity plans for critical functions. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 10]
- An HKMA speech says banks should secure their own and critical service providers' cyber fundamentals, and that frontier artificial intelligence risks should not be underestimated. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 10]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss VA activity with the HKMA, and get its feedback on risk controls, before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- SFC-licensed firms in the bank's group should promptly report material cyber incidents to the SFC, and internet brokers or VASPs should notify their case officer at once if they expect difficulty meeting the July 2027 authentication deadline. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 18; S:724f4d9f786e, para 23]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Assess whether node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse before relying on a DLT network. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 5]
- For custody delegates: independent code reviews, understanding of release processes, and regular evaluation of security controls and disaster-recovery testing. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]
