- A bank may delegate VA custody to an SFC-licensed VATP after due diligence; the SFC's own VATP custody standards (HSMs, air-gapped signing devices, a security operations centre, 24/7 monitoring) show what such a platform is expected to have. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 14–15; S:562c0f8addce, paras 2, 7, 10, 18, 24]

## Talking points

**To the chief compliance officer (CCO)**
- The SFC OTP circular is addressed to internet brokers and VASPs, not the bank; our own custody baseline is the HKMA custody annex. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11]
- Several wallet controls in the HKMA 2026 custody annex use the same wording as the SFC's 2025 custody circular. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11; S:562c0f8addce, Sections II–III]

**To business heads**
- Custody keys are to be kept in Hong Kong in tamper-resistant devices such as HSMs; smart contracts are out for cold wallets on public blockchains. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(c)]
- Counterparty platforms and internet brokers are expected to move client login and device binding off OTPs by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA places responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks with the board and senior management. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- Phishing made up 57% of security incidents reported to HKCERT in 2025, as cited by the SFC. [S:724f4d9f786e, fn 5]

**To Risk / chief risk officer (CRO)**
- The HKMA's first quantum readiness score for the sector is 2.3 of 10, with 2030 as the objective for full readiness. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
- The HKMA has warned about crypto firms presenting themselves as 'banks' and about tokens falsely linked to licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:19c8611c621a, para 2; S:275e7319a841, para 2]

## Common mix-ups

- 'MPC or multi-signature makes custody safe.' The SFC says overseas incidents pointed to potential critical weaknesses whatever the custody solution. [S:562c0f8addce, p.1]
- 'The 50%/100% compensation cover applies to bank custodians.' That is the SFC VATP requirement (cover for potential loss of 50% of client VAs in cold wallets and 100% in hot wallets, under VATP Guidelines para 10.22); the 2026 HKMA annex instead makes the bank liable for losses attributable to it and requires adequate financial resources, which may include insurance. [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 para 33; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- 'OTP is fine for client login.' Not for SFC-licensed internet brokers and VASPs, which are expected to stop using it for login and device binding by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]
- 'The HKMA DLT considerations are hard rules.' The HKMA calls them non-binding and non-exhaustive, with detailed expectations discussed bilaterally. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction]
- 'A licensed issuer's name on a token means it is regulated.' The HKMA warned that such tokens were not issued by or associated with the licensed issuers. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3]

## Read these first

1. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets by AIs** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 10–11, 14–15, 23–25. Why: the bank's own key and wallet control baseline. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
2. **Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT** — HKMA, 16 Apr 2024. Read all ten items. Why: how the HKMA reviews bank DLT projects. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240416-2-EN/20240416-2-EN.pdf
3. **Circular 26EC35 on robust authentication and surveillance** — SFC, 9 Jul 2026. Read paras 5–13, 21–25. Why: the counterparty deadline and liability line. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC35

## Open items

- No HKMA circular on phishing-resistant authentication for banks is in the documents reviewed for this guide; the 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA is driving adoption of 'iAM Smart' step-up authentication in banks, with first-phase testing on remote account opening under way. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(i)]
- The SFC cybersecurity circular of 6 February 2025 is referred to but not itself in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Note 4]
- The HKMA custody annex's cross-referenced staking guidance and the SFC's November 2024 generative-AI circular are outside this module.

## Related modules

[D3](#m-D3), [D5](#m-D5), [E1](#m-E1), [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3).

title: Tax and information reporting
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain what the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) bill would require, where it overlaps with the bank's existing Common Reporting Standard (CRS) duties, and what the government has said about tax concessions for digital-asset funds.

## In 60 seconds

CARF is an Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) standard for yearly exchange of crypto-asset tax data. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] Hong Kong committed to it in December 2024 and consulted on it in December 2025. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 1]; [S:252a7f86684e, para 1] The Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 appeared in the Gazette on 22 May 2026 and had its First Reading in the Legislative Council (LegCo) on 3 June 2026; the documents reviewed show no passage as of 25 September 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] If passed, CARF duties would start on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS duties on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)] A business that carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers would be a Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (RCASP). With a Hong Kong link, it would have to register, run due diligence, report and keep records, with fines for failure. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50M, 50O-50Q, 80R] Bank accounts are already covered by CRS, and the amended CRS brings in crypto-linked assets and digital money products. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5] Separately, the government said it would extend fund and family-office tax concessions to digital assets, aiming at year of assessment 2025/26. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

Acronyms: FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau; IRD = Inland Revenue Department; HKMA = Hong Kong Monetary Authority; SFC = Securities and Futures Commission.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commitment to implement CARF (first exchanges from 2028) | FSTB | 13 Dec 2024 | Stated target | Hong Kong government | [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] |
| CARF and amended CRS consultation paper | FSTB + IRD | 9 Dec 2025 | Consultation closed 6 Feb 2026; followed by the bill | Proposed RCASPs; CRS financial institutions | [S:275d5cc93a88, para 8 and Chapter 6, PDF p.8, 48-49]; [S:252a7f86684e, para 7] |
| Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 | LegCo / FSTB / IRD | Gazetted 22 May 2026; First Reading 3 Jun 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Hong Kong RCASPs (Part 2); reporting financial institutions (Part 3) | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] |
| IRD CARF web guidance | IRD | Undated (reflects bill) | Bill before LegCo | RCASPs | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Fund / family-owned investment holding vehicle (FIHV) tax concessions to cover digital assets | FSTB / Financial Secretary | 26 Jun 2025; 25 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Privately offered funds; FIHVs; single-family offices | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] |

## Key facts

- On 13 December 2024 the government told the OECD Global Forum it would implement CARF, aiming for local law by 2026 and first exchanges from 2028, on a reciprocal basis with partners that protect data. [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4]
- The December 2025 consultation paper proposed amending the Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO, Cap. 112) for both CARF and the amended CRS; comments closed on 6 February 2026. [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7]
- The consultation called CARF and the amended CRS finalised global standards and sought views only on local implementation choices. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 8, PDF p.8 (printed p.4)]
- The bill appeared in the Gazette on 22 May 2026 and was put to LegCo for First Reading on 3 June 2026. LegCo's notice for that sitting said the Second Reading debate would be adjourned. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]
- If passed, Part 2 (CARF) would commence on 1 January 2027 and Part 3 (amended CRS) on 1 January 2028; the rest would start on the day the enacted Ordinance is published in the Gazette. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]
- The bill defines an RCASP as any individual or entity whose business carries out crypto exchange transactions on customers' behalf, whether by acting as the other side of the trade, by brokering it, or by running a trading venue. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"]
- Under the bill, an RCASP would be a Hong Kong RCASP (HKRCASP) through Hong Kong tax residence, Hong Kong incorporation (with legal personality or a duty to file tax returns with the IRD), management from Hong Kong, a regular Hong Kong place of business, or a Hong Kong branch through which relevant transactions are carried out. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- The bill would require an HKRCASP to register with the Commissioner by 31 January of the year after it first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)]
- Three kinds of transaction are reportable: crypto-to-fiat exchanges, crypto-to-crypto exchanges, and transfers. Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and specified electronic money products are outside the relevant crypto-assets CARF covers. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Scope of crypto-assets covered' and 'Transactions subject to reporting']
- RCASPs would have to get tax-residence self-certifications from new customers and check they are reasonable. For existing users they would have 12 months after the rules start. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- The bill proposes that records be kept for six years after the related return's due date. If a former RCASP entity is dissolved, its last directors would have to make sure the records are still kept. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
- Failing to register, do due diligence or file a return without reasonable excuse would be an offence, with a fine at level 3 on conviction. Using a service provider would not, on its own, be a reasonable excuse. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(1)-(3)]
- Extra fines would apply: $500 a day while a registration, return or notice failure continues after conviction. A due-diligence breach could instead be fined $1,000 per affected user or controlling person, if that is higher than the level 3 fine. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]
- The bill also proposes a financial penalty, set by the Commissioner, in place of prosecution, with written representations and appeal to the Board of Review. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Penalty provisions']; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.82E-82F]
- Under the amended CRS, CBDCs and specified electronic money products join the depository-account concept. Derivatives referencing crypto-assets become financial assets, and crypto-assets become eligible investments for investment entities. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5]
- The consultation proposed that an entity that is both a CRS reporting financial institution (RFI) and an RCASP report crypto sale or redemption proceeds under both regimes, not once. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.14-4.17]
- Policy Statement 2.0 said the government would propose adding specified digital assets to the qualifying transactions for profits tax concessions of privately offered funds and FIHVs, effective from year of assessment 2025/26 if LegCo approves. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- The 2026-27 Budget said a bill to be introduced in the first half of 2026 would class digital assets as qualifying investments for these concessions, aiming at year of assessment 2025/26. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98]

## What your bank must do

These duties bind only once the bill passes and commences. The bill is not yet law.

**Obligations**
- [ ] Map whether any group entity, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers, including as intermediary. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- [ ] Test each such entity against the Hong Kong nexus rules, including branches. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- [ ] Plan registration by 31 January of the year after nexus is first met. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
- [ ] Plan for due diligence from 1 January 2027, including self-certifications for existing users within 12 months. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- [ ] Prepare CRS systems for amended CRS due diligence from 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)]; [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep CARF due-diligence evidence and reporting records for six years after each return's due date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
- [ ] If CARF work is outsourced, keep oversight; under the bill, using a service provider would not in itself be a reasonable excuse. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]
- [ ] If using self-developed software, plan to submit test data files to the IRD for validation; the consultation's plan set the fourth quarter of 2027 for this. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(c)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] CARF registration and returns would go to the IRD through its planned CARF Portal, not to the HKMA or SFC; watch for the portal and data schema. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Where the bank partners with a crypto trading platform or broker, note that the counterparty may itself be an RCASP with its own reporting. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Individuals and entities subject to due diligence and reporting requirements']

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The CARF bill had its First Reading on 3 June 2026. If passed, CARF duties would start on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS on 1 January 2028. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
- Outsourcing CARF work to a vendor is not, in itself, a reasonable excuse for failing to register, do due diligence or report. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

**To business heads**
- Providing crypto exchange services for customers as a business, even as intermediary, could make the entity an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- New crypto customers will need a tax-residence self-certification; existing ones within 12 months of start. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024, with first data exchanges targeted from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
- The government linked CARF to Hong Kong's reputation as a financial centre. [S:ab980a841782, para 3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Under the bill, fines could scale: $500 a day for failures that continue after conviction, or $1,000 per affected user or controlling person for due-diligence breaches. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]
- The consultation proposed dual CARF and CRS reporting of crypto proceeds for entities in both regimes. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.17]

## Common mix-ups

- "CARF is already law." It is a bill before LegCo; the IRD says the dates apply subject to passage. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
- "Registration is due by 31 December of the year nexus is first met." That was the consultation's main proposal. The bill sets 31 January of the year after nexus is first met. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(b) and footnote 45]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
- "Amended CRS starts in 2029." Duties start on 1 January 2028; 2029 is the first amended-CRS exchange. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)]
- "CARF covers CBDCs and e-money." Those are excluded from CARF but brought into the amended CRS. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3]
- "The HKMA or SFC supervises CARF." The IRD runs registration, returns and penalties. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal' and 'Penalty provisions']

## Read these first

1. **Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026** — LegCo / IRD, gazetted 22 May 2026. Read Clause 1 (commencement), ss.50M-50R (definitions, nexus, registration, due diligence, returns) and ss.80R, 82E-82F (offences, financial penalty). The operative text. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/carf/Inland%20Revenue%20(Amendment)%20(Crypto-Asset%20Reporting%20Framework%20and%20Amended%20Common%20Reporting%20Standard)%20Bill%202026(eng).pdf
2. **IRD: Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework page** — IRD. Read the Overview, nexus, due diligence, registration and penalty sections. Plain-language summary of the bill's proposals. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/dta_carf.htm
3. **Implementation of CARF and Amendments in Relation to CRS (consultation paper)** — FSTB/IRD, 9 Dec 2025. Read paras 4.3-4.18 (amended CRS and dual reporting) and Chapter 6 (timeline). Sets out the CRS changes relevant to banks. https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/government/publication/consultation/docs/2026/crypto-framework.pdf

## Open items

- Passage of the CARF bill is not recorded in the documents reviewed for this guide as of 25 September 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]
- The consultation also proposed mandatory CRS registration for all RFIs from January 2027 and heavier CRS penalties. The bill's list of provisions in the documents reviewed for this guide shows no RFI registration clause. Whether that proposal moved to other legislation is not stated. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 5.3, 5.9-5.12, 5.15, Chapter 6 item (2)(a)]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Contents]
- Whether the final bill keeps the proposed dual-reporting default is not stated on the IRD page.
- The IRD page says the lists of reportable and partner jurisdictions, the CARF Portal and the data schema will come in due course. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Lists of reportable jurisdictions' and 'Reporting portal']
- Fund/FIHV concessions: the 2026 Policy Address says a bill easing taxes on fund vehicles, single-family offices and carried-interest earners has already passed. No document reviewed for this guide has a bill text confirming how digital assets are treated in the enacted version. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 40]
- The documents reviewed do not say whether tokenised deposits count as specified electronic money products for CRS.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A3](#m-A3), [C1](#m-C1), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3)

title: What's coming: the pipeline
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can list what is still coming in Hong Kong digital assets, say how far along each item is, and quote only the targets the government and regulators have stated.

## In 60 seconds

Four new licensing regimes for virtual assets (VAs) are coming: dealing, custody, advisory and management. [S:4a0342268bf2, paras 2, 4] All four have consultation conclusions, and the government says one bill will go to the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026. [S:ff3df4326e0f, para 2]; [S:4a0342268bf2, para 3]; [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] The earlier plan for an over-the-counter (OTC) licence run by Customs was revised into the wider dealing proposal under Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licensing. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.10] On the market side, the SFC has set out a framework for licensed platforms to propose perpetual contracts for professional investors, a pilot for secondary trading of tokenised funds, and standards for platforms dealing in stablecoins from Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)-licensed issuers. [S:089ec86e2407, para 3]; [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 1-2]; [S:19d52ade6849, paras 2, 4-5] The HKMA plans central bank money settlement and 24/7 operation in EnsembleTX by around end-2026, and tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end; CMU OmniClear is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii), 35(iv), 50] The Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) bill sets its CARF part to start on 1 January 2027; the bill is before LegCo. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] Customs plans digital-asset analytics systems by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026. Dates are those stated in the source; targets are the government's or regulator's own words, not forecasts.

Acronyms in this table: FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau; CCE = Commissioner of Customs and Excise; AI = authorized institution (a bank under the Banking Ordinance); VATP = VA trading platform; LC = SFC-licensed corporation; RI = registered institution (a bank registered with the SFC); HKEX = Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing; CMU = Central Moneymarkets Unit; C&ED = Customs and Excise Department; RCASP = Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider; CRS = Common Reporting Standard; FATF = Financial Action Task Force; VASP = VA service provider; DeFi = decentralised finance; AML = anti-money laundering.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VA OTC licensing by CCE | FSTB | 8 Feb 2024 | Superseded | VA OTC shops, ATMs and online platforms (AIs, LCs, VATPs proposed exempt) | [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23]; [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9] |
| VA dealing + VA custodian regimes | FSTB + SFC | Consulted 27 Jun 2025; conclusions 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Dealers, custodians; banks register, HKMA frontline | [S:7395a53cc85a, paras 1, 4]; [S:ff3df4326e0f, para 2] |
| VA advisory + VA management regimes | FSTB + SFC | Consulted 24 Dec 2025; conclusions 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Advisers, managers; only banks may register | [S:4a0342268bf2, paras 1-3]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10] |
| Single bill for the four regimes | Government + SFC | This year (stated 24 Jun 2026) | Stated target | As above | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| VATP perpetual contracts framework | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | Issued; VATPs submit proposals to SFC | Licensed VATPs; professional investors only | [S:089ec86e2407, para 3]; [S:49f642bdee28, 'Background'; 'Eligible investors and reference assets'] |
| Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | Issued (pilot framework) | Product issuers, intermediaries incl. VATPs | [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 1-2, 7] |
| Tokenised gold and other real-world-asset products on licensed platforms | SFC (per Policy Address) | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target | VATPs, product issuers | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(ii)] |
| Relevant (HKMA-licensed issuer) stablecoins on VATPs | SFC | 27 May 2026 | Issued | VATPs, LCs (RIs via HKMA circular) | [S:19d52ade6849, paras 2, 4-5, fn 2] |
| Stablecoin trading and use to settle tokenised money market funds | SFC (per Policy Address) | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target | VATPs, fund managers | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |
| EnsembleTX tokenised-deposit pilot | HKMA | 13 Nov 2025, through 2026 | Pilot | Participating banks | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2-3] |
| EnsembleTX central bank money settlement + 24/7 operation | HKMA | Around end-2026 | Stated target | Participating banks | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| Wholesale e-HKD payment solution for after-hours derivatives trading | HKEX with HKMA | Real-value transactions in 2026 | Stated target | HKEX after-hours derivatives trading | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |
| Tokenised Exchange Fund Bills operational tests | HKMA | By end-2026 | Stated target | Banks | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] |
| CMU OmniClear digital asset platform | CMU OmniClear | 2026 | Stated target | Digital bond issuance and settlement | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)] |
| Tokenised bond legal review, phase 2 | FSTB + HKMA | Second half of 2026 | Stated target | Fixed income market | [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase'] |
| SFC digital-asset custody surveillance system | SFC | Second half of 2026 | Stated target | SFC supervisory tool | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| CrypTech market and AML surveillance components | SFC | 2027 | Stated target | SFC supervisory tool | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| Tokenised-deposit Mainland trade-finance pilot transactions | HKMA | By end-2026 | Stated target | Not specified in source | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 99] |
| CARF (Part 2) / amended CRS (Part 3) commencement | Government bill before LegCo | 1 Jan 2027 / 1 Jan 2028 | Bill before LegCo | RCASPs; CRS financial institutions | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] |
| C&ED DATAS and AMLAS analytics systems | C&ED | Phase 2 by 2029 | Stated target | C&ED systems | [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209] |
| FATF 7th targeted update on VA/VASP standards + DeFi report | FATF (relayed by SFC) | Approved at June 2026 Plenary | Approved; publication pending | For information of LCs and VASPs | [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)] |

## Key facts

- The February 2024 OTC proposal would have created a CCE-run licence for businesses offering spot trading of VAs, with banks and other SFC- or HKMA-regulated firms proposed to be exempt. [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23]
- The June 2025 dealing paper widened that plan. It proposed covering simple conversions and more complex services such as brokerage and block trading, after the consultation found more varied business models. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.8-1.10]
- For dealing and custody, the SFC will be the standard setter; the HKMA will be frontline regulator for registered banks and stored value facilities. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]
- The December 2025 conclusions align VA dealing with Type 1 (dealing in securities). The SFC will require VA dealers to keep client VAs with SFC-regulated VA custodians. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3-5, 26]
- No deeming arrangement is planned for the dealing or custody regimes; each takes full effect on commencement. An expedited approval process is planned for VATPs, LCs and RIs already providing VA dealing, and for VATP associated entities and banks already assessed for VA custody. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
- Commencement dates are not set. The government and SFC will consider how long the market needs to adjust. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- VA advisory will align with Type 4 and VA management with Type 9. For these two services, banks alone could take the SFC registration route rather than a licence. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]
- VA management will have no de minimis threshold. Type 9 firms now managing portfolios with VA exposure below the current threshold will need a licence or registration, or should wind down that business by commencement. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68]
- In June 2026 the government said the bill for all four regimes, covering stablecoins among other VAs, would go to LegCo that year. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- Under the SFC framework, perpetual contracts on VATPs should be offered only to professional investors. Margin collateral should be fiat, or stablecoins or tokenised deposits regulated by the HKMA. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']
- The first products under the SFC's tokenised-fund trading framework are expected to be tokenised money market funds. The SFC will then assess how they operate before considering a wider product range. [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6]
- For Relevant Stablecoins, the SFC does not require VATPs and LCs to apply the retail liquidity and index requirements, but their disclosures should cover the stabilisation mechanism and redemption arrangements. [S:19d52ade6849, paras 4-5]
- EnsembleTX settles interbank tokenised deposit transactions at first via HKD RTGS (the Hong Kong dollar real-time gross settlement system), with planned upgrades to 24/7 settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end, to help banks use the more than $1.3 trillion of these bills round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The SFC plans to start running its digital-asset custody surveillance system starting in the second half of 2026 and to switch on CrypTech market and AML surveillance components in 2027. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
- C&ED plans to launch its Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System (DATAS) and AML Analytics System (AMLAS) by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]
- The FATF approved publication of a seventh targeted update on implementing its VA/VASP standards and a DeFi report at its June 2026 Plenary; both are to be published in due course. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Inventory current and planned VA dealing, custody, advisory and management activity. Intermediaries now doing VA activities under SFC licensing or registration conditions will need a licence or registration under the new regimes. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]
- [ ] Plan for a fixed start date with no transition: no deeming arrangement is planned, and dealers that have not contacted the SFC or HKMA may have to stop operations on that date. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31-32, 34]
- [ ] Note that, once in force, the regimes will prohibit actively marketing VA advisory or management services to the Hong Kong public without a licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 70]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Note the SFC's stated plan to start running its digital-asset custody surveillance system starting in the second half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
- [ ] Track the CARF start date (1 January 2027 in the bill) for any group entity that may be an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] The regulators encourage firms interested in VA dealing to approach the SFC (or the HKMA, where relevant) early to begin pre-application. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]
- [ ] Existing and would-be VA advisers and managers are strongly encouraged to start pre-application talks with the SFC early. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 7]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Under the dealing regime, check that VA custodians used for client assets are SFC-regulated. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
- [ ] The SFC's 27 May 2026 circular covers only Relevant Stablecoins: specified stablecoins issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer and authorised under its licence. It does not cover other stablecoins. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- All four VA intermediary regimes have conclusions; one bill is targeted for 2026, with no deeming arrangement. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63]
- For dealing and custody, banks register with the SFC and the HKMA is frontline regulator. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]; [S:27d27650e820, para 1.10]

**To business heads**
- VA management will have no de minimis threshold, so even a small VA portion of a managed portfolio will need a licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68]
- Under the SFC framework, VATP perpetuals may take HKMA-regulated tokenised deposits as margin collateral. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA plans EnsembleTX central bank money settlement and 24/7 operation by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- CMU OmniClear is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for digital bond issuance and settlement. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]

**To Risk / CRO**
- C&ED aims to launch digital-asset transaction analytics (DATAS) by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]
- The FATF's next VA/VASP update and a DeFi report are approved but not yet published. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## Common mix-ups

- "The Customs OTC licence is still coming." The 2025 dealing proposal revised that plan and put VA dealing under SFC licensing. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9-1.10]
- "Conclusions mean the regimes are law." A bill is still to be introduced; commencement dates are not set. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- "Retail clients can trade VATP perpetuals." Under the SFC framework, only professional investors should be offered them. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
- "VA managers can use any custodian, like dealers." It is the other way round: dealers will have to use SFC-regulated custodians, while private funds managed by VA managers keep the flexibility to appoint qualified custodians globally. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 56]
- "Policy Address items are rules with legal force." They are stated plans: the Policy Address says what the SFC and HKMA will do or are planning to do. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49-51]

## Read these first

1. **Consultation Conclusions on VA dealing and further consultation on VA advisory/management** — FSTB + SFC, 24 Dec 2025. Read paras 3-5, 26, 29-36 and footnotes 9-10. Core design, custody rule, transition and bank registration. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/consultation/doc?refNo=25CP12
2. **Consultation Conclusions: VA advisory and VA management** — FSTB + SFC, 26 May 2026. Read paras 6-12, 32, 56-57 and 62-70. Scope, no de minimis, custody choice and commencement. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VASPVAMSP_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf
3. **The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address** — HKSAR Government, 16 Sep 2026. Read paras 35-36, 49-51 and 99, and Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209. The latest official list of stated targets. https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

## Open items

- No bill text for the four VA regimes is in the documents reviewed for this guide as of 25 September 2026.
- Commencement dates for the VA regimes are not set. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
- The SFC intends to align custodian requirements with those now applied to SFC-licensed VATPs and will look at a flexible approach to custody technology and storage ratios; the detailed requirements are not in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:f41a543388bc, para 38]
- The CARF bill was introduced into LegCo on 3 June 2026 with the Second Reading debate adjourned; its passage is not recorded in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]
- The FATF seventh targeted update and DeFi report were not yet published as of the 14 July 2026 SFC circular. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A3](#m-A3), [C1](#m-C1), [C2](#m-C2), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D5](#m-D5), [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3)

title: Wholesale money, CBDC and cross-border projects
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) central bank digital currency (CBDC) work, from the digital Hong Kong dollar (e-HKD) to mBridge and Ensemble, and say what compliance role the published designs give to banks.

## In 60 seconds

The HKMA has worked on an e-HKD since 2017, and its first projects looked at use by financial institutions (wholesale, bank-to-bank money). [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] It ran two rounds of market consultation on a retail e-HKD in 2021-2022 and two industry pilot phases in 2023-2025. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'HKMA's Policy Stance on e-HKD used in retail applications' and 'e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 1' and 'Phase 2' sections] In October 2025 it said it would prioritise wholesale uses, and it has not yet made a policy decision on if or when it will introduce a retail e-HKD. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] Its cross-border work grew from Project Inthanon-LionRock with the Bank of Thailand (BoT) into mBridge, a multi-CBDC platform that reached minimum viable product (MVP) stage in June 2024. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section]; [S:db56d97e2206, para 1] Project Ensemble explores interbank settlement of tokenised deposits; its pilot phase, EnsembleTX, settles first through Hong Kong's Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system for HKD and is to move in stages to tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1 and 3] Ensemble has tie-ups with central banks in France, Thailand and Brazil and a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Shanghai bodies. [S:0ed273d6f63f, paras 2-3]; [S:aabff1db2350, paras 1 and 3]; [S:8d9f12b43ada, para 1]; [S:eb28508e5032, para 2] In the mBridge designs, each participating bank runs its own anti-money laundering (AML), know-your-customer (KYC) and sanctions checks off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]; [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retail e-HKD | HKMA | Study from Jun 2021; pilots 2023-2025 | Exploratory | Public, banks (no decision to issue) | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates' section and 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] |
| e-HKD for financial institutions (wholesale-first priority) | HKMA | 28 Oct 2025 | Stated target | Banks, financial market infrastructures | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] |
| Project mBridge (multi-CBDC platform) | HKMA with Bank of Thailand (BoT), People's Bank of China Digital Currency Institute (PBoC DCI), Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub (BISIH) Hong Kong Centre; Saudi Central Bank joined the MVP platform | MVP 5 Jun 2024 | Pilot | Participating banks | [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1 and 3, fn 1]; [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
| Project Ensemble / EnsembleTX | HKMA | 7 Mar 2024; EnsembleTX 13 Nov 2025 | Pilot | Participating banks | [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |
| Project Inthanon-LionRock | HKMA + BoT | 2019-2020 (renamed m-CBDC Bridge, Feb 2021) | Superseded | Participating banks | [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section] |
| Project Aurum (retail CBDC prototype) | HKMA + BISIH + Hong Kong Applied Science and Technology Research Institute | Report Oct 2022 | Exploratory | n/a (research) | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] |
| Project Sela (retail CBDC access) | HKMA + Bank of Israel + BISIH | Report Sep 2023 | Exploratory | n/a (research) | [S:f9000467b0ee, s.1 Introduction, p.5]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] |
| Project Genesis (green bond tokenisation proof of concept) | HKMA + BISIH | 2021 | Exploratory | n/a (research) | [S:98e6099623a7, para 17]; [S:5a9cad53f2be, fn 4] |
| Banque de France (BDF) collaboration: DL3S (Distributed Ledger for Securities Settlement System) and Ensemble Sandbox interoperability, under an MoU | HKMA + BDF | Announced 27 Jun 2024 | Exploratory | n/a | [S:0ed273d6f63f, paras 1-3, fn 2] |
| Bank of Thailand Ensemble–Project San proof of concept (PoC) | HKMA + BoT | 28 Oct 2024 | Exploratory | n/a | [S:aabff1db2350, para 3] |
| Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) Drex link | HKMA + BCB | 28 Oct 2024 | Exploratory | n/a | [S:8d9f12b43ada, para 1] |
| Cross-boundary e-CNY (digital renminbi) pilot | HKMA + People's Bank of China | Expanded 17 May 2024 | Pilot | Retail users; banks offering top-ups via the Faster Payment System (FPS) | [S:08caafe0cfe7, paras 1-2] |
| Shanghai–Hong Kong digitised cargo trade and finance MoU | HKMA + Shanghai Data Bureau + National Technology Innovation Center for Blockchain | 2 Mar 2026 | Exploratory | n/a | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA's e-HKD work began in 2017 with Project LionRock, a proof of concept with the three note-issuing banks and Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section]
- The October 2021 technical paper proposed a two-tier design: the central bank issues e-HKD, and banks distribute it. It said the design was not a blueprint. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4]
- The April 2022 policy paper noted that full anonymity is generally not seen as workable for a CBDC, given anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) duties, and pointed to tiered wallets as a common approach. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.3, p.34]
- In September 2022 the HKMA set out a three-rail approach and said initial legal research suggested existing law was not adequate to issue a digital legal tender with enough certainty. [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.10]
- Phase 1 of the pilot (16 firms, 14 pilots) found possible value in programmability, tokenisation and atomic settlement. [S:9f8886b0fb21, Executive Summary, p.6; s.3.1, p.11]
- In September 2024 the project became Project e-HKD+, covering both e-HKD and tokenised deposits; Phase 2 ran 11 pilot groups. [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2]
- On 28 October 2025 the HKMA made wholesale payments the priority for future e-HKD work, ahead of retail use. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- The HKMA's September 2026 CBDC page says it has not yet made a policy decision on if or when it will introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']
- Inthanon-LionRock was run in Q4 2019. In February 2021 the PBoC's Digital Currency Institute and the Central Bank of the UAE joined, and it was renamed the m-CBDC Bridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1]
- The HKMA page says the BISIH Hong Kong Centre gave 'strong support' as the project became mBridge. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section]
- In the 2022 pilot, 20 banks in four jurisdictions ran more than 160 payment and foreign exchange (FX) trades worth over US$22 million. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive Summary, p.4]
- At MVP in June 2024, the project team listed was BISIH Hong Kong Centre, Bank of Thailand, PBoC DCI, Central Bank of the UAE and the HKMA; the Saudi Central Bank was welcomed as the next full participant. [S:db56d97e2206, fn 1, para 3]
- In October 2025 the Government told the Legislative Council (LegCo) that mBridge had become part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure, and that participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- Aurum built a two-tier prototype with a wholesale interbank system and retail wallets; Sela tested a design in which private intermediaries (called access enablers) connect directly to the central bank's CBDC ledger. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'; S:f9000467b0ee, s.1 Introduction, p.7]
- Project Ensemble explores settling tokenised money between banks through the e-HKD as wholesale CBDC, starting with tokenised deposits. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Ensemble' section]
- The November 2025 government digital green bonds gave the HKD and RMB tranches an option to settle in tokenised central bank money, alongside traditional rails. The Government called it the world's first digital bond offering to use e-CNY and e-HKD in settlement. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money in the settlement process' item]
- Tier-4 personal e-CNY wallets for Hong Kong residents cap balances at RMB10,000 and allow retail payments only, not person-to-person transfers. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2]
- About 80,000 e-CNY wallets had been registered with Hong Kong mobile numbers by end-January 2026, and 18 local banks support top-ups through the FPS. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]

## What your bank must do

These are pilot and research designs, not binding rules. The lines below show what the published designs expect of participating banks.

**Obligations**
- [ ] On mBridge, run AML, counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and sanctions checks off the platform before sending a payment; the receiving bank runs its own check before confirming. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- [ ] On mBridge, meet each jurisdiction's AML/CTF/sanctions laws; the platform attaches a pass or fail certificate from the bank's off-platform check to each transaction. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep KYC, AML and CTF compliance off-bridge in the bank's own systems. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]
- [ ] For any e-HKD distribution role, note that the 2022 policy paper said a two-tier design could task customer-facing institutions with customer due diligence and record-keeping. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Banks may use the HKMA Supervisory Incubator for distributed ledger technology (DLT) to reaffirm their risk controls before a full DLT launch; tokenised deposits are a core focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] On mBridge, foreign banks can hold and use a CBDC, but only domestic banks can have it issued or redeemed against reserves. Check which role each counterparty has. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, pp.31-32]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- mBridge leaves AML and sanctions screening to each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- The 2022 e-HKD policy paper said customer-facing institutions could be tasked with customer due diligence under a two-tier design. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]

**To business heads**
- The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale payments, to support tokenisation and cross-border payments. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- In Phase 2, commercial banks leaned slightly towards tokenised deposits rather than e-HKD. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Executive Summary, p.2]

**To the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**
- mBridge reached MVP in June 2024; the Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1]; [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- There is no decision to issue a retail e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- The 2022 mBridge pilot ran on a centralised cloud in Hong Kong, and the report said holding data in a single cloud heightened privacy concerns. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33]
- In Phase 2, zero-knowledge-proof privacy tools tested on public blockchains made transactions up to 320 times more costly in gas fees. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', p.30]

## Common mix-ups

- "Hong Kong is about to launch a retail e-HKD." The HKMA has made wholesale the priority and has made no launch decision. [S:6bd9e65817c4, paras 4-5]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']
- "mBridge screens payments for sanctions." Each bank screens off-platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- "Any bank can mint any CBDC on mBridge." Only domestic banks can request issuance or redemption of their home CBDC. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.2]
- "e-CNY wallets work like general wallets." Person-to-person transfers are not allowed. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2 'Usage']
- "Inthanon-LionRock and mBridge are different projects." mBridge is the renamed later phase. [S:3044ec37475a, Executive Summary, p.7]

## Read these first

1. **HKMA Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) page** — HKMA, updated Sep 2026. Read the policy stance, mBridge, Ensemble and Collaborative Projects sections. The HKMA's own current summary. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/key-functions/international-financial-centre/fintech/central-bank-digital-currency/
2. **Project mBridge: Connecting economies through CBDC** — pilot report, Oct 2022. Read s.6.4 (privacy), s.6.5.2 (payments), s.7.1 and s.7.2 (sovereignty, legal, AML/sanctions). The clearest statement of bank compliance duties on a CBDC platform. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2022/20221026e3a1.pdf
3. **e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 2 Report** — HKMA, 28 Oct 2025. Read the Executive Summary and Section 5 ('Path Forward'). Why the HKMA went wholesale-first. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251028e4a1.pdf

## Open items

- No document reviewed for this guide has a official Hong Kong document after June 2024 describing any change in BISIH's role in mBridge. This module states BISIH's role only as of the 2024 MVP release and the HKMA's CBDC page.
- In October 2025 the HKMA said retail e-HKD groundwork would be finished in the first half of 2026. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 5] Its September 2026 page says this preparation work is completed, but gives no launch decision. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates' section]
- The planned common token standards from the e-HKD Industry Forum are not yet in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 6]
- The HKMA–PBoC work on upgrading e-CNY wallets and raising their limits had no finalised proposals or timetable as of March 2026. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)]; [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (2)]
- Outcomes of the BDF, BoT, BCB and Shanghai collaborations are not published in the documents reviewed for this guide.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [C5](#m-C5), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3)

title: Glossary and timeline
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): a quick reference. Look up a term in plain English, or place any document in the 2017–2026 sequence, with the official source for each line. As of 25 Sep 2026.

## How to use this page

Common abbreviations: HKMA = Hong Kong Monetary Authority; SFC = Securities and Futures Commission; FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau; LegCo = Legislative Council; VA = virtual asset; DLT = distributed ledger technology; CMU = Central Moneymarkets Unit; BIS = Bank for International Settlements; BISIH = BIS Innovation Hub; AML = anti-money laundering; CFT = counter-financing of terrorism; ML/TF = money laundering / terrorist financing; KYC = know your customer; STO = security token offering; MoU = memorandum of understanding; OECD = Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development; IRD = Inland Revenue Department; MVP = minimum viable product; FATF = Financial Action Task Force.

- Part A defines about 80 terms. Each points to the official document and paragraph where the idea is set out.
- Part B lists about 100 dated events from 2017 to September 2026. The events are facts about what was published or done. Targets are shown only as the source states them.
- Dates are those the source gives. Where a source gives only a month or year, so does this page.

## Part A: Glossary

**Institutions and legal status**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Authorized Institution (AI) | A bank or other institution authorised by the HKMA. The HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline is issued under s.7 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) and s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance, and sets the standards AIs, including RIs, should meet. | [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.1, 1.3] |
| Registered Institution (RI) | An AI that the SFC has registered for one or more regulated activities. The HKMA is the day-to-day frontline supervisor; ultimate responsibility stays with the SFC. | [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2, 2.1.3, 2.2.1] |
| Licensed corporation (LC) | A firm licensed by the SFC for regulated activities. The joint circulars apply to LCs and RIs together as 'intermediaries'. | [S:b79266f3da51, paras 4-6] |
| HKMA | Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Among other roles, it grants stablecoin issuer licences under the Stablecoins Ordinance. | [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 2]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1] |
| SFC | Securities and Futures Commission. It licenses VA trading platforms, and the Government proposes that it lead licensing and standard-setting for VA dealing and custody. | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] |
| FSTB | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau. It issued Policy Statement 2.0 and runs the VA licensing consultations jointly with the SFC. | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 2]; [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1] |
| Frontline regulator | The HKMA's proposed role for banks under the coming VA dealing and custody regimes: it would supervise them, while the SFC sets the standards. | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4] |
| SB-1 | HKMA Supervisory Policy Manual module on supervising RIs' regulated activities. It is a statutory guideline under Banking Ordinance s.7(3). | [S:8934af8cc884, p.1 'Purpose', 'Classification'] |
| Executive officer | A person an RI appoints, with the HKMA's written consent, to directly supervise a regulated activity. At least two are needed per activity. | [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9] |

**Virtual assets and platforms**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Virtual asset (VA) | The legal term, defined in s.53ZRA of the AMLO. Policy Statement 2.0 (June 2025) says the Government will now say 'digital assets' instead. | [S:8a016a912528, footnote 1]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] |
| Digital asset (HKMA custody usage) | Covers VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets, and the keys, seeds and backups used to reach them. | [S:ed61d7c335e7, footnote 1, p.1] |
| VASP | VA service provider. The HKMA expects banks to assess each VASP customer's ML/TF risk on its own facts, with extra due diligence where needed. | [S:642680fa4467, p.4, item (b)] |
| VATP | VA trading platform. In SFC usage, a corporation licensed for Types 1 and 7 under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO), or holding an AMLO VA service licence. | [S:19d52ade6849, footnote 1] |
| Deemed-to-be-licensed | A platform that was operating before 1 June 2023, met the deeming conditions and may keep operating while its licence application is decided. It is not licensed and may never be. | [S:c787f990209d, Note 1, 'Reminder for investors', Note 2] |
| Non-contravention period | The 12-month window (1 June 2023 to 31 May 2024) in which pre-existing VATPs with a genuine Hong Kong presence could operate without breaching the AMLO licensing rule. | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 6] |
| Associated Entity | A wholly owned Hong Kong subsidiary of a VATP that holds client assets on trust and does no other business. | [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 1.1, 10.1] |
| Cold storage | Offline key storage. The SFC expects VATPs to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage. | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.6(c)] |
| Compensation arrangement | An SFC-approved arrangement a VATP should hold to cover potential loss of 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot and other storage. For banks' custody, the HKMA's May 2026 guidance instead expects liability to clients plus adequate financial resources. | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] |
| Professional investor | Defined in the SFO (Schedule 1, Part 1, s.1). Any other person is a 'retail client'. | [S:19d52ade6849, footnote 4] |
| Complex product | A product that triggers the SFC's complex-product rules, including a suitability check even without a solicitation. VA-related products are very likely complex. | [S:8a016a912528, paras 5-6.1] |
| Joint circular | The SFC–HKMA circular on intermediaries' VA activities. The December 2023 version replaced those of January 2022 and October 2023, and was supplemented in September 2025. | [S:8a016a912528, note after para 3, p.1]; [S:b79266f3da51, para 1] |
| Staking | Locking a client's VAs in a proof-of-stake network's validation to earn rewards. | [S:b79266f3da51, para 4] |
| Shared order book | An arrangement letting an SFC-licensed VATP pool orders with an overseas affiliate platform, using fully pre-funded orders and delivery-versus-payment settlement. | [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 10, 13] |
| Perpetual contract | A leveraged VA derivative with no expiry. Under the SFC's February 2026 framework, licensed VATPs may propose them, and they should be offered to professional investors only. | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Scope of application', 'Eligible investors and reference assets'] |
| Funding rate | Periodic payments between long and short holders of a perpetual contract that keep its price near spot. The SFC expects settlement at least once every 24 hours. | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Scope of application', 'Trading and settlement'] |
| Travel Rule (VA transfers) | For banks, the HKMA Guideline sets customer due diligence for occasional VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more and points to AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A. RIs must also have regard to Chapter 12 of the SFC AML Guideline for VA provisions. | [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1(b)(iii), fn 15; para 1.3, fn 1] |
| Unhosted wallet | Software or hardware through which a person holds and moves VAs, keeping the private key themselves. The HKMA's May 2025 consultation proposed that licensed stablecoin issuers check whether a customer's wallet is custodial or unhosted. | [S:0d6e6d0253ff, footnote 4, paras 3.2.2-3.2.4] |
| Suspicious VATPs list | A dedicated SFC list that helps the public spot suspicious platforms doing business in Hong Kong. | [S:ea8889eb1fc4, item 2]; [S:dddd919625e9, para 3] |

**Coming VA regimes**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| VA dealing service | Under the June 2025 proposal, dealing in VAs as a business in Hong Kong, from simple conversion to brokerage and block trades. Banks would register with the SFC, with the HKMA as frontline regulator. | [S:27d27650e820, para 1.10] |
| VA custodian service | Under the December 2025 conclusions, safekeeping for others, as a business, the private keys or similar instruments that can move VAs. Trustees or managers that only delegate custody are out of scope. | [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6-8] |
| VA advisory / VA management | Proposed regimes whose scope will match the SFO regimes for advising on securities (Type 4) and asset management (Type 9). | [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2] |
| Deeming / grandfathering | Automatic transitional licensing for incumbents. None is planned for the VA dealing or VA custodian regimes. | [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48] |
| Expedited approval | A faster approval track promised for SFC-licensed VATPs, and for LCs and RIs already providing VA dealing services. | [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36] |
| MPC (multi-party computation) provider | A technology firm that splits control of private keys. Whether it needs a custodian licence is decided case by case, mainly on whether it can move client VAs on its own and whether clients can always reach their assets independently. | [S:f41a543388bc, para 11] |
| VA OTC regime | The February 2024 proposal for the Commissioner of Customs and Excise to license spot VA trading businesses, including shops and ATMs. The June 2025 dealing proposal revised it. | [S:efcdb0ae3849, para 2.6]; [S:27d27650e820, para 1.1] |

**Stablecoins and bank capital**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | The law that set up licensing for regulated stablecoin activities. It commenced on 1 August 2025. | [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1-2] |
| Fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) | A stablecoin that references one or more fiat currencies. Issuing one in Hong Kong as a business, or issuing one that references the Hong Kong dollar anywhere, needs an HKMA licence. | [S:79b5b51a1a1b, p.4 'What to regulate']; [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 2] |
| Relevant Stablecoin | A specified stablecoin issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer under its licence. | [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] |
| Register of licensed stablecoin issuers | The HKMA's public list under s.21 of Cap. 656. | [S:270f1f7324ab, intro paragraph] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox | An HKMA arrangement launched in March 2024 to share supervisory expectations with would-be issuers. Admission was not an HKMA endorsement, and participants had to apply separately for a licence. | [S:f2a668eb3b93, Annex, Objectives] |
| Cryptoasset (capital rules) | A digital representation of value that relies mainly on cryptography and DLT or similar technology, and can be used to pay, invest or access goods or services. | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.2.1] |
| Group 1a / 1b | Tokenised traditional assets (1a) and stablecoins with effective stabilisation mechanisms (1b). Both carry the same capital requirements as the underlying traditional asset, plus any infrastructure add-on. | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.3.2] |
| Group 2a / 2b | Unbacked cryptoassets, and tokenised assets or stablecoins that fail the classification conditions. They are fully capitalised; limited hedging is recognised for 2a and none for 2b. | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.3.3] |
| CRP-1 | HKMA non-statutory guidance on classifying cryptoassets. The Banking (Capital) Rules prevail if they differ. | [S:b7d630146e6c, p.1 'Classification', para 1.1.4] |
| Negative vetting | LegCo's 28-day scrutiny of subsidiary legislation. The cryptoasset capital, disclosure and exposure-limit amendment rules completed it in August 2025. | [S:974899bbef4d, p.1] |

**Tokenisation and digital money**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tokenised deposit | A digital form of a commercial bank deposit, issued by the bank. | [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Ensemble'] |
| Tokenised product (HKMA) | A DLT-based digital form of a real-world asset product that is not SFO-regulated (stablecoins excluded). The sales rules for the underlying product generally apply to its tokenised form. | [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage', fn 1; 'General principle', pp.1-2] |
| Tokenised security (SFC) | A traditional security in a token wrapper. Its complexity is judged by looking through to the underlying security. | [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 23-24] |
| Cash token | In Project Evergreen, a token minted by the CMU representing a claim on the HKMA for one Hong Kong dollar. | [S:a0b44be27c40, para 33] |
| Non-native issuance | A bond first issued off the DLT platform and then tokenised on it. In Project Evergreen, CMU book entries came first and beneficial interests were then recorded on the ledger. | [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 25-26] |
| CMU / CMU OmniClear | The Central Moneymarkets Unit. The HKMA owns it; CMU OmniClear Limited, a wholly owned Exchange Fund subsidiary set up in October 2024, operates it for the HKMA. | [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-3] |
| Digital Bond Grant Scheme | HKMA grant of up to HK$2.5 million per eligible digital bond issue in Hong Kong, open for an initial three years from November 2024. | [S:633ce27d4f9b, paras 2-3] |
| Supervisory Incubator | An HKMA arrangement letting banks confirm DLT risk controls before a full launch, with optional live trials. | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 1, 3] |
| DLT | Distributed ledger technology. The HKMA's non-binding considerations expect an AI's board and senior management to take full responsibility for DLT risks. | [S:1884530ff235, Introduction; item 1] |
| CBDC / e-HKD | Central bank digital currency; the e-HKD is the HKMA's possible digital Hong Kong dollar for wholesale and retail uses. The HKMA currently prioritises wholesale use. | [S:d51dc8884c8a, introduction] |
| Wholesale CBDC (wCBDC) | Central bank digital money for settlement between banks, the basis of Project Ensemble. | [S:5a9cad53f2be, paras 1-2] |
| Project e-HKD+ | The September 2024 renaming of Project e-HKD as it widened from the e-HKD alone to new forms of digital money, including tokenised deposits. | [S:2f93aa2b9560, para 1] |
| Three-rail approach | The HKMA's e-HKD path: foundations (Rail 1), use cases and pilots (Rail 2), implementation planning (Rail 3). | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Three-rail approach'] |
| Project Ensemble / EnsembleTX | The HKMA project for tokenised-money settlement; EnsembleTX is its real-value pilot phase from November 2025. | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] |
| Ensemble Architecture Community | An HKMA-formed group (May 2024) of regulators, banks and technology firms that develops industry standards for interoperability. | [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-3] |
| mBridge | A multi-CBDC platform for real-time, 24/7 cross-border payment-versus-payment settlement. | [S:6b0fae230518, para 2] |
| Off-bridge compliance | On mBridge, banks meet each jurisdiction's KYC and AML/CFT rules outside the platform. | [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3] |
| PvP / DvP | Payment-versus-payment and delivery-versus-payment. The Ensemble Sandbox was built to test both for interbank settlement. The SFC describes DvP as a simultaneous exchange of assets that lowers non-delivery risk. | [S:460620ab7f2b, para 2]; [S:f009f1a6d615, para 13] |
| Atomic settlement | Settling both legs of a deal at the same instant, each leg depending on the other. | [S:9f8886b0fb21, s.4.1.3, p.30] |
| Purpose-bound money | A 'wrapper' that sets conditions on how money is used while leaving the underlying value intact. Phase 2 pilots examined it as an alternative to a natively programmable e-HKD, which could weaken fungibility. | [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Programmability', p.33; Glossary, p.43] |
| Access Enabler | In Project Sela, a new kind of intermediary that provides customer-facing retail CBDC services, such as onboarding and KYC, without holding users' CBDC or its own liquidity. | [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 2, p.8] |
| e-CNY tier-4 wallet | A personal digital renminbi wallet opened with a Hong Kong mobile number, without real-name checks. Balance is capped at RMB10,000; retail payments only, no person-to-person transfers. | [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2] |

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
